Vienna's Ortstaxe is 5% of the charge for the stay (excluding VAT and breakfast) from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027; until 30 June 2026 it was 3.2% after a flat 11% deduction.
From 1 July 2027 Vienna's Ortstaxe is 8% of the charge for the stay, excluding VAT and breakfast.

The Ortstaxe applies to temporary lettings (up to 3 months) of any accommodation in Vienna, from hotels and holiday flats to campsites, and is collected by the accommodation provider; exemptions include minors staying for school, training or in youth hostels, students at Viennese universities and colleges, and stays over 3 months.
VAT on accommodation in Austria is 10% (since 1 January 2022).
Worked example (editorial arithmetic): €220 a night incl. 10% VAT, room only = €200 net; 5% Ortstaxe = €10 a night, €30 for three nights; at 8% = €16 a night.

Mango Tree Ipanema: Rua Prudente de Morais 594, a block from the beach, 400 m from Nossa Senhora da Paz station; dorms and private rooms, bar, garden, terrace, 24-hour reception; special-event bookings (naming Carnaval) need full prepayment, a cancellation 90 days before check-in gets back 50% of the deposit with a 25% penalty on the booking value (hotel wording), and no refund inside 90 days.

Vila Galé Rio de Janeiro: Four-star at Rua Riachuelo 124, Lapa, opened December 2014; 292 rooms in the Collection wing (restored 19th-century mansion) and the Lapa Towers (13 floors); pool, spa, two restaurants; Arcos da Lapa and Escadaria Selarón within walking distance.

Windsor Asturias: Three-star with 166 apartments at Rua Senador Dantas 14; rooftop view and the Ópera restaurant; a few minutes from Santos Dumont airport and metro and VLT stations; lists the Theatro Municipal and the Biblioteca Nacional nearby.

Yoo2 Rio de Janeiro: Tapestry Collection by Hilton at Praia de Botafogo 242 facing the beach; 143 apartments and suites; The Rooftop bar and Cariocally restaurant; views of the Sugarloaf and the Corcovado; room types Standard, Superior partial view, Deluxe front view, Deluxe front view jacuzzi, Presidential; packages page empty.
Windsor Florida: 422 apartments at Rua Ferreira Viana 81, a few metres from the Aterro do Flamengo; pitched as good value for money, with rooms set up for families.

Santa Teresa Hotel RJ-MGallery: Rua Almirante Alexandrino 660; set in a historic coffee farm from 1850; rooms with garden or Guanabara Bay views; Térèze restaurant, Le Spa and a pool; room list from Superior Room to Royal Suite; offers show a Bride's Day package and an M Moment, no Carnival offer.
Windsor Marapendi: Five-star at Avenida Lúcio Costa 5400 facing the sea in Barra da Tijuca; 487 apartments; pool and sauna; accepts cats and dogs up to 5 kg for a fee.

No tourist tax is charged on hotel stays in the city of Rio de Janeiro in October 2026; a bill for a R$15 'sustainable tourism fee' on visitors staying in the city was before the City Council's committees in June 2026, with no plenary vote scheduled.

claim: Quebec's tax on lodging is usually 3.5% of the price of an overnight stay, calculated on the night only (breakfast, parking and other supplies excluded); it is a flat $3.50 per night when a unit is rented to an intermediary such as a tour operator.
GST (5%) and QST (9.975%) are calculated on the total of the overnight price, the tax on lodging and anything supplied with the room.
The tax on lodging does not apply to campsites, units in youth tourist accommodation establishments, rentals of six hours or less or of more than 31 consecutive days, or occasional rentals.
Our arithmetic: a $250 room carries $8.75 lodging tax (3.5%), then GST $12.94 and QST $25.81 on $258.75, for $297.50 a night (about 19% more).

The STM 747 airport bus fare is $11.25 per person and gives a 24-hour pass for bus, métro, exo train and REM in Zone A; on board it must be paid in coins with exact change (no paper bills); also sold at door-28 machines (cash, debit, Visa/Mastercard) and in the Chrono app.

The 747 leaves YUL from door 28; route 1 serves Lionel-Groulx métro and René-Lévesque Boulevard to the René-Lévesque/Berri terminus (stop 52905, since 26 Jan 2026); route 2 runs only to Lionel-Groulx; departures generally every 10-20 minutes all day, with overnight departures roughly hourly.

The REM's YUL-Aéroport-Montréal-Trudeau station is still under construction by Aéroports de Montréal; dynamic testing on the branch began 8-9 Aug 2026 and commissioning of the branch's two stations is planned by the end of 2027.
STM Zone A fares: 1-trip $3.75 (not valid on the 747), 24-hr $11.25, 3-day $21.75, weekly (Mon-Sun) $33.25; the 24-hr, 3-day and weekly passes are valid on the 747.

Visa-exempt foreign nationals flying to or transiting through Canada need an eTA: CAN$7, most approved within minutes, valid up to 5 years or until the passport expires; US nationals and US permanent residents need neither a visa nor an eTA.
Hotel Saint-Sulpice (414 rue Saint-Sulpice) is an all-suite hotel whose lofts start at 500 sq ft with a king bed and kitchenette.
Hotel Zero1 (1 René-Lévesque Blvd East) has 165 rooms and suites, each with a kitchenette.
Maison Grinder (1730 rue Notre-Dame Ouest) has 15 rooms; its Chambre Salon rooms are 200-265 sq ft, on the lobby floor facing rue Notre-Dame.
Auberge de La Fontaine (1301 rue Rachel Est) has 21 rooms overlooking Parc La Fontaine and no elevator.

In the City of Vancouver short-term accommodation carries 8% PST, 3% MRDT and a 2.5% Major Events MRDT (1 Feb 2023 to 31 Jan 2030); because the provincial taxes exceed 12%, 5% GST applies to the room price plus those taxes, about 19.2% in all ($200 room = $238.35 in the province's example).
BC's PST, MRDT and Major Events MRDT on Vancouver accommodation are charged on the whole purchase price, including added fees such as resort, cleaning and destination marketing fees.
PST and MRDT do not apply to accommodation once the same guest's continuous stay has exceeded 26 days (27 days or more).
The City of Richmond levies a 3% MRDT on accommodation, renewed for five years through to 2027; outside the City of Vancouver GST is not charged on PST or MRDT.
The GST rate in British Columbia is 5% (BC does not use HST).
The Canada Line connects YVR airport and Waterfront Station in Downtown Vancouver in approximately 25 minutes.
An additional $6.50 YVR AddFare applies to trips starting at YVR-Airport, Sea Island Centre or Templeton stations (to Bridgeport onward); there is no AddFare for journeys to the airport.

TransLink adult fares: contactless/cash $3.50 (1 zone), $5.10 (2 zones), $6.70 (3 zones); Compass stored value $2.85/$4.20/$5.40; DayPass $12.55; 1-zone fares on all buses at all times, weekends, holidays and weekdays after 6:30pm.
In TransLink's tariff the City of Vancouver is fare Zone 1 and the City of Richmond (which includes YVR on Sea Island) is Zone 2.
TransLink accepts contactless Amex, Mastercard and Visa cards and mobile wallets at the adult cash fare, tapping in and out at SkyTrain stations; a Compass Card requires a $6 refundable deposit.

Visa-exempt foreign nationals need an eTA to fly to or transit through a Canadian airport; it costs CAD $7, most applications are approved within minutes, it is valid up to five years or until the passport expires; U.S. citizens are exempt and arrivals by car, bus, train or boat do not need one.
The City of Vancouver acknowledges that it is on the unceded traditional territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations.
Fairmont Pacific Rim, 1038 Canada Place, has 367 rooms and suites, a rooftop pool, a fifth-floor spa and the Botanist restaurant and bar.
The Sylvia Hotel, 1154 Gilford Street on English Bay, is a designated heritage building from 1912 with 120 rooms and suites.
Skwachàys Lodge, 31 West Pender Street, opened in 2012, is an Indigenous boutique hotel and social enterprise with 18 rooms and housing and studio space for 24 Indigenous artists; no parking on site.
The Victorian Hotel (514 Homer St, 1898 building) lists rooms from 247 sq ft (Legacy King) to 450 sq ft (Rockwell Suite).

Whistler hotel rooms carry 8% PST and a 3% MRDT (the municipality describes the 3% as in addition to the 8% PST); GST (5%) is charged on the room price but not on the PST or MRDT outside the City of Vancouver, so about 16% of the room price in total. Worked example is editorial arithmetic: C$350 room + C$40 resort charge = C$390; PST 31.20, MRDT 11.70, GST 19.50; total C$452.40.
PST and MRDT apply to the whole purchase price including added fees such as resort fees, and are not charged once a guest's continuous stay has exceeded 26 days.
The GST rate in British Columbia is 5%.
Whistler Blackcomb schedules winter 2026/27 opening day for 20 November 2026, subject to weather and conditions; its hours page lists no closing date.
Winter 2026/27 base-area lift hours: opening day to 15 January 9:00 am to 3:30 pm; 16 January to 12 February 9:00 am to 4:00 pm; 13 February to closing day 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

Epic Pass 2026/27 (USD): adult (31+) $1,169; young adult (18-30) and teen (13-17) $929; child (5-12) $599; unlimited, unrestricted access at Whistler Blackcomb; also five consecutive days at Hakuba Valley and Rusutsu in Japan; Epic Mountain Rewards lists 20% off lodging.

Whistler Blackcomb Day Pass (adult, 4 days, no peak dates) C$517 (C$130 a day); adding peak dates +C$93; highest 7-day-advance adult lift ticket price this season C$309 a day (checked 25 Oct 2026; prices vary by date).
The Resort Municipality of Whistler acknowledges that it is on shared unceded L̓il̓wat7úl and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory.

Whistler is about 120 km from Vancouver; Tourism Whistler puts the shuttle journey at 2.5 to 3 hours depending on traffic, weather and road conditions, and lists three year-round operators (Whistler Shuttle, YVR Skylynx, Epic Rides from downtown Vancouver).

YVR Skylynx 2026/27 winter timetable (22 Nov 2026 to 19 Apr 2027): daily Express YVR 10:00 am to Whistler 12:15 pm and YVR 1:30 pm to Whistler 3:45 pm without stops; standard 7:00 am from YVR via downtown Vancouver and Squamish reaches Whistler 10:00 am; Express and standard service runs every day of the year.

YVR Skylynx meets at its kiosk in the International Arrivals area beside the escalators; buses stage at Bus Bay 9; Whistler drop-off is the Whistler Gateway loop near the Visitor Centre; Creekside pick-up and drop-off is by reservation outside Legends Hotel.

YVR Skylynx price page (dated 'To November 21, 2026'; currency and winter fares not separately stated): YVR to Whistler/Squamish standard $55 one way, express $65 one way; first set of skis or snowboard free.

Tourism Whistler says winter tires are required on the Sea to Sky Highway (Highway 99) from 1 October to 31 March; BC accepts winter tires marked M+S or with the three-peak mountain snowflake symbol, with at least 3.5 mm of tread.
BC Transit Whistler: adult single ride $2.75, adult DayPASS $5.50.

Fairmont Chateau Whistler, 4599 Chateau Boulevard, has 519 guest rooms and suites at the foot of Blackcomb Mountain, calls itself ski-in/ski-out, has slope-side pools, the Vida Spa and an on-site golf course; parking is for an additional fee.
Four Seasons Resort and Residences Whistler, 4591 Blackcomb Way: its Ski Concierge is at the base of Blackcomb Mountain, a five-minute walk or complimentary shuttle ride from the Resort.

The Westin Resort & Spa, Whistler, 4090 Whistler Way, is at the base of Whistler Mountain; a renovation of guest rooms and spaces is under way with possible work sounds limited to 7am-5pm; indoor and outdoor pools connected, each with a hot tub.

Hilton Whistler Resort & Spa, 4050 Whistler Way, steps from the Whistler Blackcomb gondolas; its booking page shows a C$40.00 resort charge per night, included in the displayed price but excluding taxes.

Aava Whistler Hotel (4005 Whistler Way): two-minute walk from Whistler Village and five minutes from the gondolas; Deluxe rooms measure 294 sq ft; heated outdoor pool, hot tub, sauna; free ski boot dryer and ski lockers in winter.
Pangea Pod Hotel, 4333 Sunrise Alley: about 210 m to the Whistler Village gondolas; adults only (18+ at check-in); no elevator, accommodation begins on the second floor; pods are not soundproof.
Delta Hotels Whistler Village Suites, 4308 Main Street: all-suites; outdoor pool and complimentary whirlpool; minimum age to check in 19; on-site parking daily $32.00.
Pinnacle Hotel Whistler Village, 4319 Main Street: secure underground parking $29+tax, pet-friendly rooms $40+tax, pool and hot tub, seasonal mountain base shuttle.
Summit Lodge Whistler, 4359 Main St: the hotel describes itself as tucked away in the more sedate, forested edge of Whistler Village; Queen Deluxe Studios with queen bed and pull-out sofa bed.

Nita Lake Lodge, 2131 Lake Placid Road: in Creekside, 5 km south of the main Village; Creekside has its own gondola station; parking $35 a night plus taxes; complimentary seasonal slopeside ski lockers.

Legends Whistler (Lodging Ovations), 2036 London Lane: condominium-style lodge, one- to three-bedroom suites with full kitchens, 'only a minute away from the Creekside Gondola', heated outdoor pools and hot tubs.
HI Whistler, 1035 Legacy Way: private ensuite rooms and 4-bed shared rooms, shared kitchen and Cheaky's Cafe; HI members get up to 15% off the Vancouver-Whistler bus.

Alberta's tourism levy is 6% of the purchase price of accommodation booked after 31 March 2026 (4% before 1 April 2026), including cleaning, pet, extra-amenity and booking or online-broker fees; it does not apply to lodging occupied continuously by the same person for 28 days or more.

GST is 5% in Alberta, which has 0% provincial sales tax, and is charged on hotel room rentals; the sources do not state whether GST is also charged on the tourism levy, so the worked example shows both cases.

Parks Canada's Banff daily admission is C$12.25 adult, C$10.75 senior, free for youth 17 and under and C$24.50 for a family or group in one vehicle; the annual Discovery Pass is C$83.50 adult; a daily pass is valid until 4:00 pm the day after purchase; a pass is required when spending time in a national park including stops in towns and villages.
Parks Canada's 2026 free-admission window ran from 19 June to 7 September 2026, as described on Buffalo Mountain Lodge's FAQ, so winter stays need a pass.

Banff Airporter's winter 2026/27 schedule runs 15 December 2026 to 31 May 2027; adult one way is C$88.90 to Banff and C$85.90 to Canmore (return C$177.80 and C$171.80), seniors C$80.01, children 6-17 C$44.45, under 5 free; GST not included and fuel surcharges may apply; the fall fares are the same; Calgary departures run from 9:00 am to 11:00 pm and a 9:00 am departure reaches Banff at 11:00 am.

Brewster Express's winter schedule runs 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027, serving Banff, Canmore and Lake Louise with drop-offs at every Banff hotel; fares start from CA$66.75 per adult one way based on a round trip, excluding taxes and fees; Calgary to Banff buses leave at 9:30, 10:30, 12:30, 14:00, 15:30, 17:00, 18:30 and 20:00 and Calgary to Lake Louise at 9:30, 10:30, 14:00, 15:30 and 18:30.

Roam Transit adult fares: Banff local single $2 and day pass $5; Canmore-Banff Route 3 single $6 and day pass $15; Banff-Lake Louise Express 8X single $12.50, reservable in fall and winter with a $3 per-booking fee; system-wide day pass $30 including a round-trip Lake Louise reservation; the Lake Louise Village to Lakeshore winter service is cash only on the bus; a fare-system change is coming in November.

Roam's Route 2 runs year round between Tunnel Mountain, downtown Banff and the Fairmont Banff Springs; Route 3 runs every day between downtown Canmore and downtown Banff; Route 8X runs year round from the Banff High School Transit Hub to Lake Louise Village and the Lakeshore; Moraine Lake is closed after 13 October until spring and no Roam ticket includes it until 1 June.

Mt Norquay lists opening on 6 November 2026, says it is 7 minutes from Banff, and runs a free first-come, first-served winter shuttle on two routes: Route 1 from Canalta Lodge, Caribou Lodge, The Fox, The Kenrick, Ptarmigan Inn and the Banff train station, and Route 2 from the Banff Springs Hotel, Mt Royal parking lot and Scout Hall/Peaks, reaching the mountain 10 minutes after the station stop.

Lake Louise Ski Resort opens 6 November 2026 with a season pass valid to 2 May 2027 and lifts 9:30 am to 4:30 pm; it is about 60 km (40 minutes) west of Banff and 184 km (about 2 hours) west of Calgary; free winter shuttles between the resort and the communities of Lake Louise and Banff are listed, with winter schedules to be posted.

Banff Sunshine's 2026/27 hours list chair and conveyor lifts 9:30 am to 4:30 pm; the resort is about 8 km west of Banff on the Trans-Canada Highway; a free Sunshine Shuttle runs daily from the town of Banff; Sunshine Mountain Lodge is described as Banff's only ski-in, ski-out hotel.
Calgary International Airport is approximately 130 km from Fairmont Banff Springs, and Buffalo Mountain Lodge puts the drive at about 1.5 hours.
Coast Canmore says Canmore is minutes from the park gates and about 20 minutes from the Town of Banff, and that staying in Canmore avoids higher prices and crowds.
Fairmont Banff Springs lists 724 guest rooms and suites at 405 Spray Avenue and parking available for an additional fee.

Lake Louise Inn lists 247 rooms at 210 Village Road, a complimentary shuttle to Lake Louise Ski Resort in winter, free parking, a daily resort fee included in all reservations, and a minimum check-in age of 18.
Mount Royal Hotel lists free cancellation up to 72 hours before arrival, a $10 a night parking fee and both rooftop hot tubs closed for maintenance on 30 October 2026.
Coast Canmore Hotel lists parking at $10 per night per room, first come first served, and says Banff Airporter drops off at the hotel.
The City of Toronto Municipal Accommodation Tax is 6% of the purchase price of the room portion; the temporary 8.5% rate ended on 1 August 2026, and HST is also payable on the MAT portion.
Ontario's Harmonized Sales Tax is 13%.
Our arithmetic: a $300 room carries $18.00 MAT (6%), then HST of $41.34 on $318.00, for $359.34 a night, about 19.8% more than the quoted rate.

UP Express adult (13-64) one-way fare from Pearson to Union is $12.35 ($24.70 round trip); the adult PRESTO fare is $9.25 one way and is the only fare available with PRESTO contactless; children 12 and under travel free.
UP Express runs from Pearson Airport to downtown Toronto in 28 minutes.
TTC adult fare: $3.30 with a PRESTO card or an Interac debit or credit card, $3.35 in cash; cash payers get no two-hour transfer and no monthly fare capping.
A complimentary shuttle runs every 15 minutes between Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport and Union Station; the Union Station stop is on the west side of Fairmont Royal York Hotel.

The Billy Bishop ferry is free for pedestrians, crossing every 15 minutes from 05:15 to 00:07; the 509 Harbourfront streetcar from Bathurst and Queens Quay West reaches Union Station in under 15 minutes.

Le Germain Hotel Toronto Mercer is a boutique hotel on Mercer Street in the Entertainment District, within walking distance of King Street bars and Queen Street shops, with a rooftop terrace on the 11th floor; valet service carries additional fees.
Pantages Hotel (200 Victoria Street) has 106 suites in Toronto's theatre district; check-in is at 3 pm and check-out at 11 am.
Fairmont Royal York (100 Front Street West) has been a Toronto landmark since its opening in 1929.
Hotel Victoria (56 Yonge Street) has 56 rooms, has stood on Yonge Street for more than 110 years and puts the Financial District and Commerce Court seconds away.
The Omni King Edward Hotel (37 King Street East) has 301 accommodations, a heritage dating to 1903, and describes itself as conveniently located near a subway station.
Four Seasons Hotel Toronto (60 Yorkville Avenue) is in Yorkville near Bloor Street and Bay Street, with Café Boulud and a spa it calls the city's only Forbes 5-Star Spa.
The Hazelton Hotel (118 Yorkville Avenue) has Deluxe King rooms starting at a minimum of 465 sq ft; the Luxury Two Queen Room is at the back and overlooks a laneway.
The Drake Hotel (1150 Queen Street West) has 51 art-filled rooms across the Modern and Classic Wings and live shows at the Drake Underground.
Gladstone House (1214 Queen Street West) dates its history to 1889; its rooms are Studio Queen 180 sq ft, Studio King 210 sq ft, Loft King 310 sq ft and Corner King 325 sq ft.
The Westin Harbour Castle, Toronto (1 Harbour Square) has an indoor pool, a whirlpool, a tennis court and 70,000 square feet of meeting space.
Le Germain Hotel Toronto Maple Leaf Square (75 Bremner Boulevard) is a 167-room boutique hotel by the CN Tower and the waterfront, steps from Scotiabank Arena.
Alt Hotel Toronto Airport (6080 Viscount Road, Mississauga) is linked to the airport terminals and economy parking by the free 24/7 LINK train and has a 24-hour gym on the 14th floor.

China's VAT Law, in force from 1 January 2026, sets VAT at 6% for services and intangibles not listed at 13% (goods, repair, movable-property leasing), 9% (transport, postal, basic telecoms, construction, real-estate leasing, listed goods) or zero (Art. 10); hotel accommodation is not among the services listed at 13% or 9%. The State Taxation Administration's 2019 Q&A puts lifestyle services at 6%, and a Fujian finance department page quoting the 2016 notice lists catering and accommodation within lifestyle services. EDITOR: the rate for hotel rooms is our reading of these texts, not a sentence in any one of them.

Art. 7 of the VAT Law says VAT is a tax outside the price (the sales amount excludes VAT) and must be shown separately on the transaction document; Art. 16 of the implementing regulation sets out how to compute the sales amount when the seller prices tax-inclusive (tax-inclusive amount divided by 1 plus the rate).

In the Shanghai government and tax-authority pages read for this guide, no separate per-night tourist or hotel occupancy tax is mentioned. This is a negative finding, not an official statement that none exists.
HUALUXE Shanghai Twelve at Hengshan's page on ihg.com showed 'Starting from 1169.45 CNY' and 'Excludes 10% Service Charge' on 20 October 2026.
On 20 October 2026 the Holiday Inn Shanghai Nanjing Road's rooms page said 'Price includes taxes and fees', and the InterContinental Shanghai Pudong's page said 'Price excludes taxes and fees'.

Our arithmetic, not an official rate: a room quoted at 1,000 yuan, with VAT assumed to apply to the room and any service charge together, costs 1,000 yuan if VAT and the charge are included, 1,100 yuan if VAT is included but a 10% charge is not, and 1,166 yuan (1,000 x 1.10 x 1.06) if both a 10% charge and 6% VAT are added; a 15% charge would add 150 yuan instead of 100.

Shanghai's official guidance says foreign guests staying in hotels present a valid passport or residence permit and fill in a temporary accommodation registration form (source: Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Public Security). The NIA says that under Article 39 of the Exit and Entry Administration Law hotels register foreign guests' stays and send the information to the local public security organ; the Ministry of Public Security's rules require the form to reach the police within 24 hours, and in May 2024 the authorities said hotels must not refuse foreign guests because they lack the capacity to process the paperwork (China Daily, hosted on the Shanghai government site).
The National Immigration Administration's English site carries its policy pages on visa-free entry and transit; the guide only points readers there.

The maglev operator sells a single (economy) for RMB 50, with a 20% discount (RMB 40) on presenting a same-day plane ticket or using a public transport card, and a return (valid 7 days) for RMB 80; the operator's own page calls the ride 8 minutes. Longyang Road is the maglev's city terminus, where the Shanghai government says to change to metro line 2.

The maglev operator's Chinese fare page says Visa, Mastercard, American Express and JCB (printed 'JGB') chip contactless cards with small-payment contactless enabled can be tapped at the gate for the RMB 50 single economy fare.

Pudong airport is about 30 km from downtown; metro line 2 from Terminal 1&2 station to People's Square takes about one hour and costs about 7 yuan; a taxi to People's Square is around 180 yuan and about 50 minutes.

Hongqiao airport is 13 km from the city centre; Terminal 1 is served by metro line 10, which connects both terminals, and Terminal 2 by lines 10 and 2; a taxi to the centre typically takes about 30 minutes and costs 100 to 150 yuan.
The Airport Link Line connects Hongqiao and Pudong airports in about 40 minutes; fares start at 4 yuan and the full journey costs 26 yuan.

Shanghai Metro fares are 3 yuan for up to 6 km plus 1 yuan for every further 10 km; the one-day pass is 18 yuan; eligible UnionPay, Visa, Mastercard, American Express and JCB contactless cards can be tapped at the gates if password-free small payments are enabled.

The Bund is a 1.5 km waterfront and protected historical district in central Shanghai, on the west bank of the Huangpu River, with 52 buildings that once housed old Shanghai's financial institutions and trading companies.

Lujiazui Financial City lies directly across the river from the Bund; it is the core functional area of Shanghai's International Financial Center and holds the Oriental Pearl Tower, the Shanghai International Convention Center and the Shanghai World Financial Center.
The Shanghai government's Jing'an city-walk route runs from West Nanjing Road to the Suhe Bay commercial areas past several flagship stores.

The Radisson Blu New World's page says its main entrance faces People's Park, it sits at the start of the Nanjing Road pedestrian street and it is connected to metro lines 1, 2 and 8; the Holiday Inn Shanghai Nanjing Road describes itself as adjacent to People's Square and the Bund.

Traders Hongqiao Airport and Shangri-La Hongqiao Airport each say they are connected to Terminal 2 of Hongqiao airport, with access to metro lines 2 and 10 and Hongqiao Railway Station; the Shangri-La describes itself as in Hongqiao's international CBD.

Fairmont Peace Hotel: 'A Shanghai icon for over a century' on the Bund with views of Pudong; Art Deco-inspired furnishings; Fairmont Gold executive floor; complimentary 30-minute guided tour of the Peace Museum for guests; the page calls Fairmont Gold rooms 'interior facing' and Signature Riverview Suites 'breathtaking views of Pudong'. Room counts on the page differ (268 or 270), so the guide gives none.

Hotel Indigo Shanghai on the Bund: No. 585 Zhong Shan Dong Er Road, in the South Bund, adjacent to Shiliupu Wharf, Yu Garden, BFC Bund Financial Center and ROCKBUND; about 1 km from Yuyuan Garden metro station (lines 10 & 14) and East Nanjing Road metro station; pool; 2 on-site restaurants.

Radisson Blu New World Hotel, Shanghai: 88 Nanjing Road (W) at the start of the Nanjing Road pedestrian street; main entrance faces People's Park; lobby access to New World City mall with tax-free shopping for overseas visitors; metro lines 1, 2 and 8; fitness centre with indoor pool; 45th-floor revolving restaurant Epicure on 45; the room list gives no sizes.

Holiday Inn Shanghai Nanjing Road: No. 595 Jiujiang Road, Huangpu; on the Nanjing Road pedestrian street, overlooking Century Square, adjacent to People's Square and the Bund; Standard Rooms 30 sq m; One Bedroom Suite 56 sq m; Two Bedroom Suite 48 sq m; rooms page says 'Price includes taxes and fees'.

Okura Garden Hotel Shanghai: built in the 1920s, one of the most significant buildings erected by the French in Shanghai, the former French Club, with a 30,000 sq m garden; on South Mao Ming Road in the Huai Hai Road business circle; metro line 1 South Shaanxi Road station exit 3 100 m; five restaurants (Rose, Baiyulan, Yamazato, Sazanka, Continental Room) and three bars (Oasis, Ye Lai Xiang, Sky Bar); the Superior Room page gives no size.

HUALUXE Shanghai Twelve at Hengshan: 12 Hengshan Road, Xuhui; premium boutique art hotel, neo-Chinese aesthetic; only 20 m from metro line 1; 169 guest rooms; near the Former Residence of Soong Ching-ling, Wukang Road and Anfu Road; page showed 'Excludes 10% Service Charge'.

The PuLi Shanghai: beside Jing'an Park; Michelin-starred French restaurant Phénix, Long Bar, Garden Terrace; 25-metre indoor infinity pool with views of Jing'an Park; rooms from Deluxe Room to Jing'an Suite; the page lists no rates.

Holiday Inn Express Shanghai Jing'an Temple: 839 Middle Yan'an Road, adjacent to the Shanghai Exhibition Center and Jing'an Temple, near metro lines 2, 7 and 14; fitness centre, Wi-Fi, one restaurant; no pool on the amenities list; Standard Rooms 20 to 37 sq m, Suite 28 sq m.

Regent Shanghai Pudong: 210 Century Avenue, Pudong; floor-to-ceiling windows on the Lujiazui skyline, a 'sky-high infinity pool', three restaurants: Camelia (Italian), Mi Teppanyaki and Shang-Xi (Cantonese); the page lists no rates.

InterContinental Shanghai Pudong: No. 777 Zhangyang Road, Pudong, in Lujiazui; pool, spa, three on-site restaurants; Lane 1192, a re-creation of old Shanghai in the basement of Century Link mall, a five-minute walk away; the page showed 'Price excludes taxes and fees' on 20 October 2026.

Traders Hongqiao Airport, Shanghai: connected to Terminal 2 of Hongqiao airport, access to metro lines 2 and 10 and Hongqiao Railway Station; 520 Traders rooms; indoor heated pool; Premier Airport View Room looks out on landings and take-offs; restaurants shared with the adjacent Shangri-La.

Shangri-La Hongqiao Airport, Shanghai: connected to Terminal 2, within walking distance of the railway station and metro lines 2 and 10; 91 Horizon Club rooms and suites on floors 9 to 12, 45 to 176 sq m, with lounge privileges; 2 restaurants shared with Traders; 'heart of Hongqiao international CBD'.
Official 1-day ticket on Wed 16 Dec 2026: adult CNY 475, child CNY 356, senior CNY 356 (calendar read 19 Nov 2026).
Standard 12-59, child 3-11, senior 60+ on the visit day; under-3s free.
Free refund before 23:59 seven days before the visit; RMB 80 per ticket from 6 days to the day before; none from 00:00 on the visit date.
Official 1-day ticket can be exchanged twice, at least 48 hours before the original date; ID cannot be changed; not transferable.

Each guest books with their own valid government ID; foreign guests use a valid foreign passport; original physical ID must be shown at entry; copies/digital not accepted; one ID buys one ticket per visit date.
Under-3s are admitted free but guardians must show the child's original ID.
Disney Premier Access is sold only via the official website, app, WeChat account and Fliggy store, after buying park tickets.
Official site names its direct channels and a list of travel partners by legal entity name (e.g. Shanghai Ctrip International Travel Service Co.,Ltd).

For 2026 the tourist tax in the City of Dubrovnik is EUR 2.65 per person per night from 1 April to 30 September and EUR 1.85 in the rest of the year at accommodation where catering is provided (campsites EUR 1.95 and EUR 1.30), set by the Dubrovnik-Neretva County Assembly under article 15 of the Tourist Tax Act.
Under the Tourist Tax Act (NN 52/19) children under 12 do not pay the tourist tax (article 5) and persons aged 12 to 18 pay it reduced by 50% (article 6); the tax is per person and night.
Croatian VAT on accommodation services in hotels and similar establishments is 13%; the general rate is 25% (Tax Administration; Act on VAT article 38(3)(a)).

Platanus, the licensed airport shuttle operator, charges EUR 10 one way and EUR 15 return (return valid 15 days); the bus leaves outside Arrivals about 30 minutes after each flight arrival; children under 6 travel free.

The Platanus shuttle from the airport stops at the Old Town (Ploče Gate), about 30 minutes, then the main bus station in Gruž, about 35 minutes (final stop), 500 m from the ferry port; it lists no stop at Pile.

From the city, the Platanus shuttle leaves the main bus station (Gruž, platform 8), then stops at Grawe station (5 minutes) and the cable car stop near the Old Town (10 minutes); about 35 minutes from the bus station, about 25 minutes from the cable car stop.

Dubrovnik Airport says Libertas lines 11, 27 and 38 travel daily to and from the airport; the drive averages 30-35 minutes and up to an hour in summer; no taxi fare is published, a price list is at the taxi information window in the arrivals building (terminal B) or on +385 20 640 100.
Libertas price list (Dubrovnik): ticket bought on the bus EUR 2.50, 1-hour ticket EUR 1.73, daily (24-hour) ticket EUR 5.31, three-day ticket EUR 11.95; the page still shows a kuna conversion note.

Libertas's city timetable lists 14 lines (1A, 1B, 2A, 3, 3A, 3B, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8A, 9, 17); nine (1A, 1B, 2A, 3, 3B, 4, 6, 9, 17) have Pile in their name; line 6 is Babin Kuk-Pile and line 4 Hotel Palace-Pile.

The City of Dubrovnik's decision on vehicle access to the traffic zone in the protected historic ensemble applies the system from 1 March to 30 November (extendable by the mayor in congestion); vehicle access is by pass; the lower cable car station is at Ploče; Adriatic Luxury Hotels' notice dated 30 July 2026 says vehicle access around the Old Town is restricted to permit holders only.

Hotel Stari Grad, Od Sigurate 4, Old Town: 11 rooms and three suites; Above 5 rooftop restaurant recognised by the Michelin Guide since 2018; Standard rooms 18 m2, Deluxe 21 m2, every room for max 2 people.

Prijeko Palace, Prijeko 22: 15th-century noble residence, nine individually designed double rooms each dedicated to an artist, rooftop restaurant Stara Loza in the Michelin Guide; Trnski room 12 m2, Kramaric 20 m2 overlooking lively Prijeko Street.

Hotel Excelsior Dubrovnik, Frana Supila 12: 158 rooms and suites (139 rooms, 19 suites) across Villa Odak (1913) and The Tower; 0.6 km to the Old Town; indoor pool, spa, beach, three restaurants; The Tower Classic room has a city view.

Villa Dubrovnik, Vlaha Bukovca 6: designed 1961, a small hotel of about thirty rooms by 1970, perched on a cliff with views of Lokrum and the Old Town, rooms by Studio Arthur Casas; the hotel says Sveti Jakov Beach, Orsula Park and the city walls are a short walk away.

Hotel Bellevue Dubrovnik, Pera Cingrije 7: five-star boutique hotel carved into a 30 m cliff on Miramare Bay, pebble beach at its base, beach services for all guests from summer 2026; 1.4 km and a 10-minute walk to the Old Town.

Hotel Lero, Iva Vojnovica 14: open since 1972, 15 minutes' walk to the walls and 5 to Miramare Beach, garage; Classic rooms 20 sqm, Superior wing built 2015 with 23-30 sqm rooms; pool open 1 May to 1 October.

Hotel Lapad, Lapadska obala 37: family-owned, construction started 1912 and opened March 1914 with a Victorian facade, Classic wing built 1987, 3 km from the Old Town; Superior rooms in the historic wing have no balcony.

Hotel Kompas Dubrovnik, Ul. kardinala Stepinca 21: 4+ star hotel overlooking Lapad beach with a spa, Zenith Bar and the Sphere and Suton restaurants; Classic rooms with balcony; 4.1 km to the Old Town.

Hotel Ivka, Ulica od Sv. Mihajla 21, Lapad: small family-owned hotel with a closed garage and free Wi-Fi, bus station close, Old Town 2 km, beach 10 minutes' walk; single room 17 m2, double/twin 20 m2.

Valamar Lacroma Dubrovnik Hotel, Iva Dulcica 34, Babin Kuk: 4-star, 940 m2 Balance Mediterranean Spa, Maro World 1,800 m2 family entertainment centre; hotel lists town centre 6,000 m and bus terminal 3,000 m; autumn offer travel dates 1 Nov-29 Dec 2026.
Valamar Tirena Hotel, Iva Dulcica 36, Babin Kuk: 4-star, 200 m from the sea, outdoor pool with water slides and swim-up Splash Pool Bar; autumn offer travel dates 16-22 Oct 2026.
Valamar Argosy Hotel, Iva Dulcica 140, Babin Kuk: designed for adults, outdoor and indoor pools including an infinity pool, wellness centre; autumn offer travel dates 14-24 Oct 2026.

Prague's local fee for a stay (poplatek z pobytu) is 50 CZK per person for every started day of a paid stay except the day of arrival (in practice per night), for stays of up to 60 consecutive days with one provider.
Czech law caps the local fee for a stay at 50 CZK per person per day; Prague charges the maximum.
Exempt from Prague's fee: people under 18, blind people, holders of the ZTP/P card and their companion, and other groups listed in the Act on Local Fees.
Worked example (our arithmetic): a couple staying four nights pays 2 x 4 x 50 CZK = 400 CZK (roughly €16 at an approximate exchange rate).
PID/DPP line 59 runs between the airport terminals and Nádraží Veleslavín (metro A) every 3 to 10 minutes with a 17-minute journey; PID estimates about 35 minutes to the centre.
Line 100 runs between the airport and Zličín (metro B) every 10 to 20 minutes; PID estimates about 45 minutes to the centre.

The Airport Express (AE) between Terminal 1 and Prague main station (Hlavní nádraží) has a special PID fare of 200 CZK (100 CZK for children 6-15), sold by the driver; ordinary PID single tickets and Prague time passes are not valid. PID estimates about 45 minutes to the centre.

PID's airport page says that since 3 March 2025, because of road repairs, the city transport boarding stop at Terminal 1 is temporarily closed and boarding is at the Terminal 2 stop; the AE boards at Terminal 1 (its Terminal 2 stop is alighting only).
PID Prague fares (full fare, ages 15-60): 30 min 36 CZK app / 39 CZK paper; 90 min 46 / 50 CZK; 24 h 140 / 150 CZK; 72 h 340 / 350 CZK.

PID tickets can be bought in the PID Lítačka app, at machines, or on contactless payment terminals in all city transport vehicles; app and contactless tickets are valid after a 60-second protective period; paper tickets are validated once in a yellow validator.
In Prague, children under 10 travel free without a document and seniors from 65 travel free with an identity document showing date of birth (also for foreign passengers).
Worked example (our arithmetic): seven 90-minute app tickets cost 322 CZK and eight cost 368 CZK, against 340 CZK for the 72-hour app ticket.
Night lines 907 and 910 serve Terminal 2 at the standard PID fare (50 CZK paper / 46 CZK app).
Prague airport Terminal 1 serves non-Schengen flights (e.g. UK, USA, Japan); Terminal 2 serves Schengen flights.
UNESCO's Historic Centre of Prague comprises the Old Town, the Lesser Town and the New Town; the New Town was built by Emperor Charles IV and keeps its medieval town plan.

One Jewish Museum in Prague ticket covers the Old-New, Spanish, Pinkas and Maisel synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery; the Pinkas Synagogue houses the memorial to the Shoah victims from the Czech lands.

Four Seasons Hotel Prague: 157 accommodations (138 rooms, 19 suites) across four buildings by the Vltava near Charles Bridge; CottoCrudo Italian restaurant; AVA Spa with vitality pool overlooking Prague Castle; Modern Room 33 m2 (smallest category); rooms face the river or the streets.
Hotel Paris Prague: 5-star Art Nouveau hotel built 1904, Brandejs family for three generations, 86 rooms, U Obecního domu 1; Deluxe rooms 19-24 m2, some with balcony; direct booking upgrade offer.
Hotel Josef, Rybná 20, Prague 1: designed by Eva Jiřičná, opened 2002; spiral staircase, garden, bakery, balcony rooms on the top floor, Mini rooms described as compact, Castle View rooms.

Mandarin Oriental, Prague: Nebovidská 459/1, opened 12 September 2006 in former Malá Strana monastery buildings; spa in a former Renaissance chapel; Monastiq restaurant; Charles Bridge, Kampa, Prague Castle 5-minute walk; Old Town Square 20-25 minutes.

Aria Hotel Prague: 51 rooms and suites on four music-themed floors (contemporary, classical, opera, jazz), next to the Vrtba Garden; breakfast included; Deluxe rooms 30 m2 with a view of the Winter Garden atrium or the Vrtba Garden.
Lokál Inn, Míšeňská 66/12: house U Bílé kuželky by Kryštof Dientzenhofer, built 1708-1714; Lokál restaurant with tank Pilsner below; breakfast included, served 8-10am; promo code DIRECT for 10% off.

Jalta Boutique Hotel, Václavské náměstí 45: post-war socialist-realist building, 1950s-style rooms, original marble floors, spiral staircase to a terrace over Wenceslas Square and the National Museum.

Motel One Prague-Florentinum: a few minutes' walk from Republic Square; marionette-themed lobby; One Lounge with Bohemian crystal chandeliers; room sizes 16 m2 and 20 m2; refurbishment notice: bar closed 5-19 October (breakfast paused 14 Sep-4 Oct).

Le Palais Art Hotel Prague, U Zvonařky 1, Prague 2 (Vinohrady): Belle Époque, ceilings by Luděk Marold who lived and worked there; 72 rooms and suites; Artista restaurant; Pure Spa; Economy rooms are 'old standard' attic rooms with skylights; Deluxe on floors 1-3.

Czech Inn, Francouzská 76, Prague 10: design hostel in a restored 19th-century building; dorms with curtained beds and shared bathrooms, ensuite and premium dorms, private rooms, apartments; breakfast, bar, guest kitchen.

Botanique Hotel Prague, Sokolovská 11, 186 00 Prague (Karlín): next to Florenc metro, bus and tram; 15-minute walk from the heart of Old Town; renovated rooms; Green Key certified; free breakfast when booking direct.

Mama Shelter Prague, Veletržní 1502/20, Prague 7-Holešovice: 238 rooms, ten floors, designed by Jalil Amor, 8th-floor restaurant and rooftop (no rooftop reservations), five-minute tram ride to the Old Town.

Prague's Old Town Square and Wenceslas Square Christmas markets run 28 November 2026 to 6 January 2027; Peace Square from 20 November and Republic Square from 25 November, both to 24 December 2026 (Visit Czechia).

Kudy z nudy's listing gives Wenceslas Square market hours of 10:00-14:00 on 24 December and 12:00-22:00 on 25 and 26 December 2026.

Prague's local fee for a stay (poplatek z pobytu) is 50 CZK per person for each started day of the stay, excluding the day of arrival (in practice per night); under-18s and holders of the ZTP/P card with a companion, among others, are exempt; the hotel collects it.
Worked example (our arithmetic): a couple staying five nights pays 2 x 5 x 50 = 500 CZK in local fees.

PID airport fares for lines 59, 100 and night lines 907/910: 50 CZK paper, 46 CZK app, 55 CZK SMS; night lines run every 30 minutes from Terminal 2; PID says boarding for city transport is at the Terminal 2 stop because of road repairs since 3 March 2025.

Hotel U Prince: Old Town Square 29, 24 rooms furnished with antique furniture, building of 12th-century origin, fifth-floor rooftop terrace partly covered and heated and open all year; covered garage about 500 m away; no room sizes or breakfast details on the pages.

Hotel Rott: four-star, Malé náměstí 138/4, since 2001; standard room 20 m2, superior 25 m2, suite 60 m2; breakfast included; rooftop terrace built spring 2021 free for direct bookers; says no reservation needs prepayment and all cancel free until 48 hours before arrival; cancellation text still mentions pandemic measures.

Mosaic House Design Hotel, Odborů 4, Prague 2: 94 air-conditioned rooms; Standard 18-22 m2, Comfort 25-28 m2, Superior 18-26 m2 with balcony or terrace; on foot 12 minutes to Wenceslas Square and 15 to Old Town Square by the hotel's own list.

Sophie's Hostel, Melounova 2, Prague 2: dorms, pod beds, private rooms and apartments; breakfast buffet 7:00-11:00; dorms accept guests aged 18-39 only; airport directions via metro to I. P. Pavlova (line C); no walking times to markets given.

Hotel Anna, Budečská 17, Prague 2: 26 rooms, breakfast buffet included 7:30-10:00, tram stop about 150 m, 20% direct-booking discount, reception 8:00-21:00, air conditioning a paid extra April-October; walking times: Peace Square 7 min (500 m), Wenceslas Square lower part 23 min (1.4 km), Old Town Square 35 min (2.4 km), Republic Square 35 min (2.3 km).

Hotel Malá Strana, Melnická 9, Prague 5: about 50 m from the Újezd tram stop; Charles Bridge 15 min, Prague Castle 20 min, Kampa 10 min, National Theatre 14 min on foot; breakfast included 7:30-10:00; 20% direct-booking benefit.

Copenhagen charges no tourist tax in 2026: a municipal tourism levy requires legal authority from Parliament, which the City Council requested in June 2024 but has not been granted; a reported 2027 hotel tax for Copenhagen and Aarhus was left out of the government's 2027 finance bill (October 2026).
Denmark's VAT rate is generally 25% of the value of goods and services; in retail prices VAT is included and amounts to 20% of the price.
Denmark participates in ERM II at a central rate of 746.038 kroner per 100 euro (DKK 7.46038 per euro), with a ±2.25% band.

The M2 metro runs from Copenhagen Airport (Terminal 3) via Christianshavn, Kongens Nytorv and Nørreport; the Metro puts the airport-to-centre ride at 14 minutes, with trains about every 2 minutes in rush hour, every 3 off-peak, and from 01-07 about every 8 minutes after Fri/Sat and every 20 minutes other nights.
DOT/Metro adult single tickets: 2 zones DKK 24 (1h15), 3 zones DKK 30 (1h30); the 3-zone ticket covers city centre to airport; two children under 12 free per adult, ages 12-15 half price.

City Pass Small (zones 1-4, incl. the airport) costs DKK 100/160/220/280/340 for 24/48/72/96/120 hours; City Pass Large (zones 1-99) DKK 200-680; sold in the Rejsebillet app, at the airport, DSB machines and metro stations.

The Rejsebillet app sells single tickets and the City Pass and replaces the DOT Tickets (DOT Billetter) app; the Rejsekort app works by check-in/check-out with a 20% discount for journeys starting outside rush hour.
InterCity trains run from Copenhagen Airport Terminal 3, tracks 1 and 2, to Copenhagen city centre; tickets cannot be bought on board; airport metro ticket machines take coins and cards, not notes.
Copenhagen Card DISCOVER (adult): DKK 589/859/1,039/1,219/1,419 for 24/48/72/96/120 hours; 80+ attractions, transport in zones 1-99 including the airport.

Visit Copenhagen: Christianshavn was established in the early 17th century (canals, houseboats, Church of Our Saviour, Rampart); Kødbyen is the former meatpacking district; Assistens Cemetery holds H.C. Andersen and Kierkegaard; Strøget is the main pedestrian shopping street; Tivoli is next to Central Station; Vesterbro was once the red-light district; Østerbro 'elegant'.
Andersen Boutique Hotel (Helgolandsgade 12): 69 rooms; Cool rooms 11-13 m² from DKK 1,650 a night; complimentary glass of wine 17:00-18:00 (hotel site, Oct 2026).
Villa Copenhagen: former Central Post & Telegraph Head Office (1912), Tietgensgade 35-39; 25 m heated rooftop pool at 28-30°C for staying guests; children 7am-7pm; rooms from 17 m².
Hotel d'Angleterre, Kongens Nytorv 34: 92 rooms and suites, Michelin-starred Marchal, Balthazar Champagne bar, spa; 'over 270 years' on the square.

Room sizes from hotel sites: Ibsens Hotel Tiny 10-12 m²; Hotel Sanders Double Room 12-13 m² facing a green atrium; Hotel Kong Arthur Double Economy 14-19 m² with semi-double bed; 71 Nyhavn Hotel 130 rooms, warehouse completed 1805; NH Collection Copenhagen 394 rooms; CPH Living 12 double rooms, opened 2009; Rye115 20 rooms, no elevator.

Tivoli Gardens' Christmas season runs 13 November 2026 to 3 January 2027 per Tivoli's own pages; Visit Copenhagen's Tivoli page still showed 14 November 2025 to 4 January 2026 when read on 4 November 2026.

Tivoli's own opening-hours calendar (read 4 Nov 2026) shows Christmas-season hours of 11:00-22:00 Sunday to Thursday and 11:00-23:00 Friday and Saturday, closed on 24 December, 11:00-23:00 on 25 and 26 December, 11:00 to midnight on 31 December and 11:00-22:00 on 3 January.

The Julemarked Nytorv & Gammeltorv organiser gives 6 November to 21 December 2026, Mon-Wed 11-19, Thu 11-20, Fri-Sat 11-21, Sun 12-19 (last day closes at 20), 200 m from Rådhuspladsen, next to Strøget, with a free ice rink; the city's visitor service lists it as free with skates to borrow free.

Christmas at Højbro Plads, described by the city's visitor service as a new market for Denmark, Greenland and the Faroe Islands, runs 14 November to 20 December 2026 per Visit Copenhagen, free, 11-21 on 14 November; the organiser of the traditional Højbro Plads market says it is not held there in 2026 and moves to Rådhuspladsen.
The city's visitor service lists a new Christmas market at City Hall Square on Fri 11 December 2026, 11-18 on that date, free; exact opening hours to be confirmed later.
Nimb Hotel, Bernstorffsgade 5: five-star superior boutique hotel, 38 rooms and suites from 23 m2 to 240 m2, 300 m2 wellness area; its Christmas page lists Christmas Eve at Nimb Brasserie.

1 Hotel Copenhagen, Krystalgade 22: its Copenhagen Holiday Escape offer is valid for stays 14 November 2026 to 3 January 2027 and includes daily breakfast and entrance tickets to Tivoli Gardens (Tivoli only).
Scandic Palace Hotel, Raadhuspladsen 57: 169 rooms, hotel built in 1910; Economy 15-17 m2, Standard 17-22 m2, Superior 21-28 m2.

Hotel Alexandra, H. C. Andersens Boulevard 8: four-star, 61 rooms furnished with Danish mid-century classics, breakfast 7.00-11.00; standard retro doubles about 15-16 m2, de luxe about 25 m2, suites about 35 m2.
Savoy Hotel, Vesterbrogade 34: 66 rooms on 6 floors, all facing a quiet courtyard; says it is close to Tivoli, the Lakes and the Central Train Station; no room sizes on its room pages.
Wakeup Copenhagen Bernstorffsgade, Bernstorffsgade 35: 585 rooms with TV, desk, air conditioning and free Wi-Fi; hotel says Tivoli Gardens is within just a few minutes' walk.
Admiral Hotel, Toldbodgade 24-28: in a warehouse from 1787, just steps from Nyhavn and Amalienborg; Classic room from 2019 is 20 m2.
Phoenix Copenhagen, Bredgade 37: 213 rooms including 3 suites and 4 Junior suites; Standard rooms 12-17 m2; between Amalienborg Palace and Nyhavn.

CPH Living, Langebrogade 1A: floating hotel on a barge, opened 2009, 12 double rooms with a glass wall onto the harbour, rooftop terrace, free basic breakfast; late check-in after 6 pm must contact the hotel.

Hotel Kong Arthur, Nørre Søgade 11: peaceful corner of the inner city in the Nansensgade neighbourhood, Ni'mat Spa, reception open 24/7; Christmas stay offer includes the New Nordic breakfast buffet and two cocktail vouchers for the lobby bar.

Cabinn Metro, Arne Jacobsens Alle 2: built 2009, 708 rooms with 1,555 beds, 6.5 km from Central Station and Tivoli, 10 minutes from the airport; breakfast buffet DKK 125 per person per day; parking DKK 175/24 hours; from the airport take the train to Orestad Station.
Clarion Hotel Copenhagen Airport, Ellehammersvej 20, Kastrup: just 2 minutes from Terminal 3; standard double 33 m2; Metro to the capital in less than 15 minutes.

Finland's reduced VAT rate, which covers accommodation (hotels, motels, hostels, farm stays, camping sites and cottage rental), restaurant services and passenger transport (taxis, buses, trains, domestic flights), is 13.5% from 1 January 2026; it was 14% up to 31 December 2025.
Finavia lists the Airport Express and Santa's Express from Rovaniemi Airport to Santa Claus Village and Rovaniemi Railway Station; tickets are sold on the bus and timetables are on Airportbus.fi.

The operator Airport Express sells an adult one-way Airport Express ticket at EUR 8 and a child (4-12) one-way ticket at EUR 4; its Airport Express meets arriving flights and operates 9:00-21:00; the buses do not accept cash (buy online or pay by card on board).
Santa Claus Village is 8 km north of Rovaniemi city centre and Rovaniemi Airport is 3 km from the village.

Local bus 8 links Rovaniemi railway station, the centre and the Arctic Circle (Santa Claus Village) and runs around the year; the city sells tickets in the Waltti app and accepts contactless payment on the bus.
The main bus stop for Rovaniemi's local buses (Linkkari) is on Ruokasenkatu.

VR runs the double-decker Santa Claus Express night train from Helsinki or Turku to Rovaniemi (also Kolari and Kemijarvi), with seats or sleeper cabins, wifi and power sockets in cabins; VR's page lists no times or fares.

Santa Claus Village December 2026-January 2027: Santa Claus Office daily 8:00-20:00 (30 Nov 2026-3 Jan 2027); Santa Claus' Main Post Office daily 9:00-20:00 (1 Dec 2026-6 Jan 2027); Christmas House Shop daily 7:00-22:00; Iittala closed 24-25 Dec; Marimekko and Pentik 10:00-16:00 on 24 Dec and 12:00-19:00 on 25 Dec.

Visit Rovaniemi gives December as -20 to -10 degrees C with an average day length of about 2.5 hours, and says the sun does not rise at all on the shortest day (21 or 22 December); the Finnish Meteorological Institute defines the polar night north of the Arctic Circle as the period when the sun does not rise above the horizon.

Visit Rovaniemi says the northern lights season runs from late August to the beginning of April and that the lights can be seen on around 150 nights a year in Finnish Lapland when weather and viewing conditions are favourable; it states that no tour provider can guarantee a sighting.

Original Sokos Hotel Vaakuna applies special terms to leisure reservations for 16.11.2026-31.3.2027: payment in full in advance at booking and no refund on changes or cancellations; the hotel also warns that Nightclub Doris causes noise in the rooms on some dates.

From 1 January 2026 the Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur's taxe de séjour per person per night is, metropolitan tax plus 34% additional tax, total: palace EUR 4.80+1.63=6.43; 5-star 3.50+1.19=4.69; 4-star 2.60+0.88=3.48; 3-star 1.70+0.58=2.28; 2-star (and 4-5 star holiday resorts) 1.00+0.34=1.34; 1-star hotels, B&Bs, youth hostels 0.80+0.27=1.07; minors are exempt.

The 2026 rate sheet splits the tax into the metropolitan tax and a 34% additional tax for the Ligne Nouvelle Provence Côte d'Azur; the portal says the finance law no. 2022-1726 of 30 December 2022 introduced a 34% additional tax in the Alpes-Maritimes, Var and Bouches-du-Rhône. The sheet lists no other surcharge (no departmental or regional line). The portal says 2027 rates stay identical to 2026, and the metropolitan tax applies in all 51 member communes, Èze included.

Accommodation without classification or awaiting classification pays 6.70% (5% + 1.70%) of the pre-tax price per person per night, capped at EUR 6.43; the Métropole's own example: two people in a EUR 80 room pay EUR 40 x 6.70% = EUR 2.68 each, EUR 5.36 a night. The tax is displayed and invoiced but not always included in the price.
Our arithmetic: a couple for four nights at a four-star pays 2 x 4 x EUR 3.48 = EUR 27.84 (EUR 20.80 metropolitan + EUR 7.04 surcharge); at a five-star 2 x 4 x EUR 4.69 = EUR 37.52.

Per the airport, tram line 2 (Port Lympia / Centre ville) links Terminals 1 and 2 to the city centre at the Jean Médecin station in less than 30 minutes and to the port at Port Lympia; a tram runs about every 7 to 8 minutes on weekdays; the link Terminal 2 / Terminal 1 / Grand Arénas is free.

Lignes d'Azur: Solo (one journey, transfers 74 minutes, return trips forbidden) EUR 1.70; Pass 1 jour EUR 7; 1 aller/retour Aéroport EUR 10 (transfers 74 minutes after first validation, sold at agencies, the app and ticket machines); an anonymous reloadable card needs a refundable EUR 2 deposit. The airport's page lists indicative 2026 flat taxi fares (TTC) from the airport; Nice-Centre EUR 32.00. Taxis show a roof sign TAXI ville de Nice and a meter; a receipt is mandatory from EUR 25; card payment is accepted in the vehicle. The fares are fixed by prefectoral order (not opened).

The Nice tourist office's guide says TER trains link Nice quickly with the main towns of the Côte d'Azur; the airport page describes the Pass Sud Azur Explore as unlimited train, tram and bus in the Alpes-Maritimes and Monaco for 3, 7 or 14 days. Maison Durante's site mentions trains to Monaco, Villefranche and Èze.

The tourist office's guide describes Vieux-Nice as a maze of coloured lanes, baroque churches and façades, authentic markets and restaurants with the Niçois-cuisine label; the Cours Saleya flower and produce market; every Monday the Cours Saleya becomes an antiques market of more than 200 exhibitors.

The tourist office's guide calls the Promenade des Anglais the seaside avenue of seven kilometres on the Baie des Anges with luxury hotels and Belle Époque villas; European aristocrats took winter quarters in its Belle Époque hotels.

Berlin's Übernachtungsteuer (City Tax) is 7.5% of the net price of the overnight stay, excluding VAT and extras such as breakfast; the rate rose to 7.5% on 1 January 2025.
Since 1 April 2024, business (berufliche) overnight stays in Berlin are subject to the City Tax.
From 1 January 2025 the former City Tax exemption for stays of more than 21 days no longer applies.

The City Tax is levied on the amount paid for the overnight stay (per room price), not per person; the law (ÜnStG §4-5) sets the base as the price for the stay without VAT and other services, and the rate at 7.5%.

claim: District V's and VII's decrees define the tourist-tax base as the price of the guest night less VAT, without compulsory breakfast and other services (District VI's notice says the same); the district websites for I and V describe it as the gross room price.

Under Act C of 1990 on local taxes, section 31, people under 18 are exempt from the tourist tax; the act lists other exempt groups, including inpatients and people staying for study or for work at a business based in the municipality.

Under Act C of 1990, section 33, a municipality's tourist tax is capped at 4% of the base where it uses a percentage (the act's alternative is a fixed per-person, per-night amount, with a base figure of 300 HUF).
Our arithmetic: two adults sharing one room at 60,000 HUF a night before VAT and without breakfast, four nights: base 240,000 HUF, tax at 4% is 9,600 HUF (2,400 HUF a night).

Bali charges each foreign tourist a levy of IDR 150,000, paid once while travelling in Bali, before leaving Indonesia.

The levy is paid cashless via the Love Bali website or app (encouraged before departure), at payment counters at Bali's airport and port, or via registered endpoints (hotels, travel agents, attractions); accepted: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, bank transfer, virtual account, UnionPay, QRIS; the voucher is emailed with a QR code.

Exempt from the levy: diplomatic and official visa holders, transport crew, KITAS/KITAP holders, family-unification, student and golden visa holders (and other visas on application); cruise passengers pay.
The levy is governed by Bali Provincial Regulation 6 of 2023 as amended by Regulation 2 of 2025, and Governor Regulation 25 of 2025.

Indonesia's Visitor Visa (e-VOA) costs IDR 500,000; single entry, 30-day stay, for tourism, government visits, business meetings, goods purchasing or transit; each traveller including children needs one; passport valid 6 months from arrival.
The e-VOA is available at Ngurah Rai airport (and Benoa seaport); visa on arrival can also be obtained at the port of entry.
A visa on arrival can be extended at the immigration office covering where the visitor stays (Ngurah Rai Immigration Office lists the steps).
All travellers must submit an arrival card within 3 days before arriving in Indonesia (All Indonesia).

In Ireland, guest and holiday accommodation (hotels, guesthouses, B&Bs) is taxed at the reduced VAT rate of 13.5% (rates in force from 1 January 2026: standard 23%, reduced 13.5%, second reduced 9%); from 1 November 2020 to 31 August 2023 it was taxed at the second reduced rate, 9%.

From 1 July 2026 restaurant and catering services, including meals served in hotels, guesthouses and B&Bs, are taxed at the 9% second reduced rate; alcohol, bottled water and soft drinks stay at the 23% standard rate; a single room-and-breakfast price must be apportioned between the two rates.

Revenue's Example 1: a B&B charging €150 for one night with breakfast (breakfast valued at €20) accounts for €15.46 VAT on the €130 accommodation at 13.5% and €1.65 VAT on the €20 breakfast at 9%, total €17.11.
At 13.5% VAT included in the price, the VAT in a €200 room is €200 × 13.5 ÷ 113.5 = €23.79, or €71.37 over three nights (editorial arithmetic on Revenue's rate).

Ireland has no tourist, city or bed tax on hotel stays: Revenue's accommodation guidance lists only VAT; Dublin City Council has stated it lacks the legal capacity to introduce a bed tax without new national legislation (Dublin's four councils asked the Government for powers); the Budget 2027 tax policy changes, announced 6 October 2026, include no visitor levy or accommodation VAT change.

Dublin Bus 41 runs around the clock between Swords, Dublin Airport and Lower Abbey Street; the 16 runs from the airport to Ballinteer about every 10–15 minutes; the cash fare is €2.60 in coins only (no notes, bank cards or tap-to-pay), and the Leap TFI 90 Minute Fare is €2.

The TFI 90 Minute Fare in Dublin is €2.00 adult on Leap, covering Dublin Bus (excluding Express and Nitelink), Go-Ahead Ireland Dublin City Bus, Luas and DART/Commuter Rail within Zone 1; Express and Nitelink cost €2.40; adult Leap caps are €6.00 a day and €24.00 a week.

The TFI Leap Visitor Card costs €8 for 1 day (24 hours), €18 for 3 days (72 hours) and €24 for 7 days, valid on Dublin Bus and Go-Ahead Ireland city buses, Luas, DART and Commuter Rail in Dublin, not on Bus Éireann; it is sold at Dublin Airport at the T1 Convenience Store and WHSmith in Terminal 1 Arrivals and SPAR in Terminal 2 Arrivals.

Dublin Bus does not accept bank cards or phone tap-to-pay on board (Leap or coins); the NTA's Next Generation Ticketing programme will introduce account-based ticketing across bus, rail and Luas, with initial focus on the Greater Dublin Area.

Latroupe Jacobs Inn, 21-28 Talbot Place, Dublin 1: private rooms for 2, dorms of 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 beds with shared en-suite, large bar for drinks and live events, 24-hour reception, Irish buffet breakfast.

The Morgan Hotel, 10 Fleet Street, Temple Bar: four stars, 168 air-conditioned rooms, 10 Fleet Street Restaurant & Bar; offers include Stay Longer & Save 20% for 3+ nights (stays until 31 March 2027) and Advance Purchase 15% off with prepayment.
Temple Bar Inn, 40-47 Fleet Street: 101 en-suite rooms, 24/7 reception, complimentary buffet breakfast with every direct booking; Single 10 m2, Twin 15 m2, Cosy Double 12 m2.

The Shelbourne, 27 St Stephen's Green: 'hospitality since 1824'; Saddle Room and Horseshoe Bar; homepage notice (raw HTML checked): 'undergoing room renovations to May 2027 - some noise may occur. The Spa, including the swimming pool, is now closed.'

The Merrion, Upper Merrion Street, Dublin 2: 142 bedrooms and suites, 18 m pool, spa and gym, 2-star Michelin Restaurant Patrick Guilbaud (the hotel's wording); Booking.com lists the address as Merrion Square.
Maldron Hotel Smithfield: 4 star, 92 bedrooms including triple and quad rooms, 'with the Luas just moments away'.

Generator Dublin, Smithfield Square: 'right next to the Jameson Distillery'; private rooms, dorms, 6-bed female dorm; Shuffleboard Bar 11am-11.30pm; cafe open to 1.30am Friday and Saturday; 24-hour reception.
Anantara The Marker Dublin Hotel, Grand Canal Square: 187 rooms of 30-35 m2, spa with 23-metre infinity pool, Rooftop Bar & Terrace, within walking distance of College Green and Grafton Street.

Clayton Hotel Cardiff Lane: '4 Star Hotel Dublin Docklands', complimentary access to a 22-metre pool described as one of the largest in Dublin, separate kids' pool, 3Arena and Aviva Stadium within easy walking distance; page gives no address or room count.

Herbert Park Hotel & Park Residence, Ballsbridge, D04 R2T2: 4-star hotel and self-catering studio apartments, underground parking, 24-hour TechnoGym suite for guests, 10-minute walk to Lansdowne Road DART.

Rome's contributo di soggiorno is charged per person per night by hotel class: €10 at five-star, €7.50 at four-star, €6 at three-star, €5 at two-star and €4 at one-star hotels, €3.50 at hostels, and €5 to €7 at guest houses, B&Bs, holiday homes and short-term rentals; these rates apply from 1 October 2023 (Giunta Capitolina deliberation 255 of 17 July 2023) and are still the current ones listed by Roma Capitale in October 2026.
Rome's city tax applies for at most 10 consecutive nights in the same property in a calendar year (5 at campsites), and children are exempt until their 10th birthday.
The Leonardo Express runs non-stop between Fiumicino Airport and Roma Termini in 32 minutes, every 15 minutes, for €14 (Mini-groups ticket for four: €40); from Fiumicino it runs 05:38 to 23:27.

An FL1 regional ticket between Fiumicino Aeroporto and any station inside Rome's Zona Anello costs €8 (Trenitalia Tariff 1/Ter, valid from 28 October 2024); FL1 reaches Roma Tiburtina in 48 minutes and runs every 15 minutes on working days and every 30 minutes on Sundays and public holidays.
Ciampino Airlink combines a 10-minute bus from Ciampino airport to Ciampino station with a train to Roma Termini for €2.70.

In Rome a Metrebus BIT ticket costs €1.50 and is valid for 100 minutes from validation; the Roma 24H, 48H and 72H tickets cost €8.50, €15 and €22; ATAC accepts contactless cards (tap&go) on surface vehicles and at metro turnstiles.

Florence's imposta di soggiorno is charged per person per night: €8 at five-star, €7 at four-star, €6 at three-star, €4.50 at two-star and €3.50 at one-star hotels, €7 at residenze d'epoca, €6 at B&Bs, affittacamere, holiday flats (CAV) and short-term tourist rentals, and €4 at youth hostels and case per ferie; these rates were approved by Giunta deliberation 535 of 10 December 2024, apply from 1 February 2025, and are still the current ones listed by the Comune di Firenze in October 2026.
Florence's city tax applies to non-residents for at most 7 consecutive nights, and minors are exempt until their 12th birthday.

Since 30 July 2024 (Council deliberation 57/2024, safeguard measures) Florence has barred new short-term tourist rentals in the UNESCO historic core (Zone A1); from 21 June 2026 (DCC 28 of 4 June 2026) no new short-term rental activity may start in Zone A subzones A1, A3 and A4; every short-term rental needs a five-year municipal authorisation under the regulation in force since 31 May 2025, with units already let in 2024 exempt for three years.

Tram line T2 links Florence's Peretola airport with the city centre in about 20 minutes; the Peretola Aeroporto stop is a 2-minute walk from arrivals; first tram from the airport 05:00, last 23:58 Sunday to Thursday and 01:15 Friday and Saturday. The line opened on 11 February 2019 from Peretola to Piazza Unità, beside Santa Maria Novella station.

A Florence urban ticket for trams and city buses costs €2.00 and is valid for 90 minutes (SMS ticket €2.40); it can be bought at stop machines or by tapping a contactless card, phone or wearable on the reader on board.

On Florence's trams one bag up to 10 kg and 55x40x20 cm is free; larger bags up to 80x45x25 cm and 20 kg need one extra ticket each (maximum 2 per person); luggage over 80x45x25 cm or 20 kg is not allowed.

The PisaMover shuttle between Pisa airport and Pisa Centrale costs €6.50 single and €13.00 return, takes about 5 minutes including the intermediate stop, and runs daily from 06:00 to midnight (to 01:00 from 1 June to 30 September).

On Trenitalia's own journey planner (searched 13 October 2026 for Tuesday 10 November 2026), direct regional trains from Pisa Centrale to Firenze S. M. Novella cost €9.80 in second class and took 52 minutes (Regionale Veloce) to 1 hour 22 minutes (Regionale).
On Trenitalia's journey planner for a November 2026 weekday, direct Frecciarossa trains from Firenze S. M. Novella reach Roma Termini in 1 h 35 to 1 h 42 and Venezia Santa Lucia in 2 h 14 to 2 h 16.

Hotel Pendini's car collection service costs €28 per 24 hours for small cars and €37 for other categories, including registering the plate with the Polizia Locale for the ZTL; the hotel lists the city tax at €6 per person per night, under-12s exempt.

Hotel Orto de' Medici (4-star, Via San Gallo 30) lists Basic rooms of 140 sq ft, Classic 194 sq ft and Deluxe 215 sq ft opening onto the garden; free cancellation until 18:00 the day before arrival (promotional rates may differ); no pets.
Portrait Firenze (Lungarno Collection), steps from the Ponte Vecchio, has 37 rooms and suites and is pet friendly; its booking form says children aged 4 and over are entered as adults.
Four Seasons Hotel Firenze, Borgo Pinti 99, occupies two Renaissance palaces: Palazzo della Gherardesca (built 1473; Il Palagio, spa, pool, garden) and Palazzo del Nero (36 rooms with Duomo views).
Hotel L'Orologio Florence (4-star, Piazza Santa Maria Novella) says SMN station is within 300 metres; its Deluxe room with Santa Maria Novella square view measures 28 m².

Venice's imposta di soggiorno for hotels in high season (1 Feb-31 Dec), per person per night, in the historic centre and Giudecca: 1 star €1.00, 2 stars €2.00, 3 stars €3.50, 4 stars €4.50, 5 stars €5.00; Lido and lagoon islands €0.80/€1.60/€2.80/€3.60/€4.50; mainland €0.70/€1.40/€2.40/€3.10/€3.50. Rates valid from 1 April 2025 and still the city's current schedule in 2026.

In Venice's low season (1-31 January) the hotel tourist tax in the historic centre is €3.10 at four stars and €2.40 at three stars; B&Bs and guest houses graded 2-5 lions pay €2-€5 in high season in the historic centre.

Venice's tourist tax is due only for the first five nights of a stay; children under 10 are exempt and children aged 10 to 16 get a reduction; a receipt from a previous accommodation counts towards the five nights.

Venice's 2026 access fee trial applied on 60 days from 3 April to 26 July 2026, between 8:30am and 4pm, to the historic city only (not the minor islands such as Lido, Murano, Burano); €5 if paid by the fourth day before access, €10 after; it ended and has not applied since 27 July 2026, and the city has not set any 2027 dates.

Guests staying in accommodation in the Municipality of Venice (who pay the tourist tax) are exempt from the access fee from arrival to departure day, but must obtain a free exemption voucher with a QR code or complete a substitute declaration; the city tells guests to ask the accommodation staff for instructions.

Alilaguna's airport-Venice water bus costs €18 one way and €32 return, including one heavy bag and one hand luggage; the Blue Line serves Murano, Lido, Arsenale, San Zaccaria, San Marco, Zattere and the railway station, the Orange Line Madonna dell'Orto, Guglie, San Stae, Rialto, Sant'Angelo, Ca' Rezzonico and Santa Maria del Giglio.
ACTV Aerobus (routes 5, 15, 45) to/from Venice Marco Polo Airport: €10 for a 75-minute ticket, €18 return; Aerobus + 90-minute Rete Unica (including water buses) €18.
ATVO's Venice Airport Bus Express runs directly from Marco Polo Airport to Piazzale Roma and Mestre, about 20 minutes by ATVO's description.

ACTV standard 75-minute Rete Unica ticket (water buses) €9.50; passes €25 (1 day), €35 (2 days), €45 (3 days), €65 (7 days), excluding airport buses unless a €7 one-way or €13 return supplement is bought with the pass; the 1-day Venezia Daily Pass includes Trenitalia regional trains within the municipality (Mestre-Santa Lucia); Rolling Venice card €6 (ages 6-29) gives a 3-day ticket for €27.
The Biennale Arte 2026 runs from 9 May to 22 November 2026.

Smallest room categories among the guide's hotels, per the hotels' own sites: Pensione Accademia Basic Double 12 m² (building has no lift); Ca' Pisani Superior 14 m²; Londra Palace Classic City View 18-24 m²; Monaco & Grand Canal Golden Leaf 22 m².

Milan's imposta di soggiorno is charged per person per night by category from 1 April 2026: €12 at five-star hotels, €10 at four-star hotels and four-star tourist residences, €7 at three-star hotels and residences, €4 at two-star, €3 at one-star hotels, €7 at holiday houses (case per ferie), €3 at youth hostels and campsites, and €9.50 at B&Bs, guest rooms, holiday homes and short-term lets.

From 1 January to 31 March 2026 Milan's tourist tax was €10 at four- and five-star hotels, €7.40 at three-star, €5 at two-star and €4 at one-star, with €9.50 for B&Bs and short-term lets, valid only for 2026 under decree-law 156 of 29 October 2025 (Milano Cortina Winter Olympics); the Comune redefined the 2026 rates from 1 April.

Milan's tourist tax is charged on non-residents per person and per night; minors up to 18, people with disabilities and their companions, and university students of 26 or under enrolled at Milan universities who stay in student residences are exempt; for hotels the tax applies for the whole stay, and the 14-consecutive-night limit applies only to residences, non-profit holiday houses and holiday apartments (regulation as last amended by Council deliberation 2 of 26 January 2026).

The Malpensa Express runs from Malpensa (Terminals 1 and 2) to Milano Centrale (stopping at Porta Garibaldi) in 51 minutes and to Milano Cadorna in 37 minutes, with departures every 30 minutes from each station; a one-way ticket is €15 and a return €25, children aged 4 to 13 pay €7.50 and under-4s travel free with a paying parent.

The Comune di Milano's taxi tariff sheet (updated July 2024, still the sheet published on the Comune's taxi page) sets a fixed fare of €114 between Malpensa airport and any address in Milan, including tolls and with no supplements; Malpensa to Fiera Milano Rho is €94, Linate to Fiera Milano Rho €68 and Orio al Serio to Milan €128.
Taxis from Linate to the centre are metered: the Comune's tariff sheet lists no fixed fare for it and sets a minimum fare of €16 for trips that start at Malpensa, Linate or Orio al Serio.
Line M4 takes 12 minutes between Milan's centre and Linate airport, and the ATM urban ticket (zones Mi1-Mi3) costs €2.20.

In January 2026 the ATM ticket for zones Mi1-Mi3 costs €2.20 for 90 minutes, €7.60 for 24 hours and €15.50 for 3 days; children up to 14 travel free; card payment works at metro turnstiles (M1-M5, tap in and out) and on ATM vehicles but not on the S lines or trains.

Milan Bergamo Airport lists bus services to Milano Centrale from Autostradale, Flibco, Orioshuttle and Terravision; Autostradale runs every 30 minutes, takes 50 to 60 minutes and shows fares from €9 (labelled a limited-period promotion).
The Last Supper museum says reservation is mandatory for all tickets, it is open Tuesday to Sunday 8.15 to 19.00, and admissions for September to December 2026 went on sale on 23 June 2026.
The Pinacoteca di Brera is at Via Brera 28; Palazzo Citterio opened in December 2024 as an expansion of the Pinacoteca (the Grande Brera).

Sina The Gray, Via San Raffaele 6, is a five-star design hotel with 21 rooms and suites, 100 metres from the cathedral by its own account; the Aria terrace lounge opens in the warm season from 5pm to 11pm.

Gran Duca di York, Via Moneta 1, is a three-star in a late 19th-century palazzo, three minutes on foot from the Duomo, with 33 recently remodelled rooms in three categories (Classic, Superior, Superior with terrace); the hotel says buffet breakfast, Wi-Fi, minibar soft drinks and taxes are included in its prices.
Urban Hive Milano, Corso Garibaldi 84, is a four-star with 97 rooms; its room page describes La Mini as for solo travellers or short stays and La Cosy as for sharing.

Maison Borella, Alzaia Naviglio Grande 8, is a four-star on the Naviglio Grande in a pedestrian area, about 300 m and a five-minute walk from Porta Genova (M2) by the hotel's directions; its Maison Privée rooms are in an old railing house 20 metres from the main building.
NH Collection Milano Porta Nuova, Via Melchiorre Gioia 6, has 100 rooms renovated in 2018, the smallest 27 m²; it is 600 m from Porta Garibaldi station, and on-site indoor parking costs €40 a day.

Hotel Principe di Savoia (Dorchester Collection), Piazza della Repubblica 17, describes itself as in the centre of Porta Nuova, two minutes from Repubblica metro station and 10 minutes from Milano Centrale; its Classic Room is 27 m² for up to two guests.

Ostello Bello Grande Milan Central Station, Via Roberto Lepetit 33, is 100 metres from Milano Centrale, with free 24-hour luggage storage before check-in, self-service lockers after check-out and a bar open 24 hours with live music and DJ sets.

Hotel Manin, Via Daniele Manin 7, is a four-star facing the Giardini Indro Montanelli, owned by the Colombo family since 1904, with 124 rooms, Turati (M3) 100 m away, a free gym, and an affiliated garage from €42 a night; the restaurant is closed at lunch on Saturdays and Sundays.

The official Venice Carnival site (carnevale.venezia.it, headed 'Carnevale di Venezia 2027') gives the 2027 carnival as 23 January to 9 February 2027, with Fat Tuesday on 9 February 2027; it had not published a theme or a day-by-day programme in October 2026.
