The Carnival Official Dinner Show 2027 is at Ca' Vendramin Calergi on the Grand Canal (Cannaregio) on Sat 30 and Sun 31 January and from Thu 4 February (Fat Thursday) to Tue 9 February 2027, from 9pm; over-18s only, period costume compulsory, tickets personal, non-transferable, non-refundable and non-changeable, premium tables from EUR 650; 10 minutes' walk from the railway station, 15 from Piazzale Roma, or ACTV line 1 to San Marcuola.

In October 2026 the carnival site's Festa delle Marie page and Street Show page still describe the 2026 edition, and the site does not mention the Volo dell'Angelo, the mask contest or a St Mark's Square stage programme for 2027.
note: Recheck in mid-December and January for the official 2027 programme.

claim: The 2026 carnival (31 January to 17 February 2026) opened on Sat 31 January with a ball in St Mark's Square at 5pm, then on Sunday 1 February the Festa Veneziana water parade of about 100 decorated rowing boats from Punta della Dogana to Rialto at 11am and the start of the St Mark's Square stage programme; the 12 Marie were selected on 31 January, the Maria of the year was elected on 16 February and proclaimed in St Mark's Square on 17 February 2026.

For the 2026 Festa Veneziana water parade on Sunday 1 February 2026, the organisers' press notice said ACTV lines 1 and 2 would be modified in the morning, running via the Giudecca Canal instead of the Grand Canal for some departures.

The carnival site's 2020 and 2022 news pages describe the Volo dell'Angelo as a tradition in which the previous edition's winning Maria descends from the campanile into St Mark's Square, and the 2022 notice says it was not held that year because of pandemic restrictions; the 2027 site does not mention it.

The Enjoy Respect Venezia guidance on the carnival site says St Mark's Square is a protected historic site, asks visitors not to sit on the ground or eat and drink on monuments, church steps, bridges, wells and quaysides, and lists fines of EUR 25-500 and possible removal for breaking local rules; it publishes no carnival-specific access rules for the Square for 2027.

Venice's imposta di soggiorno for hotels, per person per night: high season 1 February-31 December in the historic centre and Giudecca is EUR 1.00 / 2.00 / 3.50 / 4.50 / 5.00 for 1-5 stars; low season 1-31 January is EUR 0.70 / 1.40 / 2.40 / 3.10 / 3.50; mainland (Mestre) high season EUR 0.70 / 1.40 / 2.40 / 3.10 / 3.50 and January EUR 0.50 / 1.00 / 1.70 / 2.20 / 2.40; Lido and islands four-star EUR 3.60 high season and EUR 2.50 January; B&B/holiday flats (lions) EUR 2-5 in the centre in high season, 30% less in January. Table valid from 1 April 2025.
note: Table is valid from 1 April 2025; check the Comune page for a 2027 schedule. 2026-11-03: Il Gazzettino (7 Sep 2026) and Tgcom24 (11 Sep) report a Comune proposal to raise the tax to about EUR 3 to 8-9 a night from March 2027 (after Carnival); not approved as of 3 Nov. Comune PDF is bot-blocked to scripts: open in a browser.

The City of Venice's council (giunta) approved the 2027 access-fee (contributo di accesso) calendar on 15 October 2026: 72 days from Good Friday 26 March to 15 August 2027, 8.30am-4.30pm, maximum fee EUR 10, with none in January or February; exclusions/exemptions, booking and payment rules still to be set.
note: The Comune's own pages (cda.ve.it, live.comune.venezia.it) are behind bot protection and could not be opened by script; the claim was taken from the Comune's release as shown in search extracts and confirmed in La Voce di Venezia, Nordest24 and QdP. claim: The 2026 access-fee trial applied on selected days between 3 April and 26 July 2026 (60 days per the city's 2026 scheme) and has ended.

Alilaguna's airport-Venice boat costs EUR 18 single and EUR 32 return, with one heavy bag and one hand luggage included; the Blue Line calls at Murano, Lido, Arsenale, San Zaccaria, San Marco, Zattere and the railway station, the Orange Line at Madonna dell'Orto, Guglie, San Stae, Rialto, Sant'Angelo, Ca' Rezzonico and Santa Maria del Giglio, and the Red Line is marked summer seasonal.

ACTV/AVM standard 75-minute Rete Unica ticket EUR 9.50; passes EUR 25 (1 day, Venezia Daily Pass), EUR 35 (2 days), EUR 45 (3 days), EUR 65 (7 days); Aerobus 75-minute ticket EUR 10, return EUR 18, Aerobus plus 90-minute Rete Unica EUR 18; Mestre Daily Pass EUR 5 (app only) covers the mainland bus and tram network and Trenitalia regional trains within the municipality.
ATVO's Venice Airport Bus Express page lists unlimited baggage and says the bus stops are at exit D, stop no. 3 for Venice and stop no. 4 for Mestre.

Gondola ferries (traghetti) cross the Grand Canal at Santa Sofia, San Tomà, Santa Maria del Giglio and Punta della Dogana and cost EUR 2.00 for tourists (EUR 0.70 for Venezia Unica residents); the historic centre has no roads and bicycles are prohibited, even when pushed.

Hotel Concordia is a four-star in Venice with 51 rooms in a 17th-century Venetian house, run by the Beggiato family for four generations; it says it is the only hotel overlooking Piazza San Marco and that most rooms look onto the basilica's spires and mosaics.

Hotel Monaco & Grand Canal is at San Marco 1332 in Palazzo Dandolo, site of the Ridotto (1638), which its own history says became a theatre of masks and gambling for six months of each year, during Carnival; rooms run from the 22 sqm Golden Leaf room to the 50 sqm Casanova Alcove.

Hotel Metropole is a five-star at Riva degli Schiavoni 4149 next to the Pieta church, with Piazza San Marco 5 minutes' walk away by its count; its spa has a heated pool (37 C in winter) and hammam, 90 minutes of exclusive use costs EUR 200 per two people, and its offers page lists Christmas and New Year's packages but no Carnival offer.

Hotel Paganelli is a three-star superior at Riva degli Schiavoni 4182 with views of the San Marco basin and San Giorgio, rooftop terraces, 24-hour reception, a lift and the Sestante osteria; its page puts the San Zaccaria stop about 50 metres away.

Ca' Sagredo Hotel is a 15th-century palace at Campo Santa Sofia by the Ca' d'Oro, declared a national monument, with a frescoed ballroom, 42 rooms and suites and the L'Alcova restaurant on the Grand Canal opposite the Rialto Market; it also markets itself for weddings, parties and events.

Hotel Abbazia is a three-star at Calle Priuli dei Cavaletti, Cannaregio 68, in a former Discalced Carmelite abbey about 100 metres from Santa Lucia station with no bridges to cross on the way, and a garden.

Combo Venezia is a hostel in the former Convento dei Crociferi at Campo dei Gesuiti, Cannaregio 4878, a few steps from Rialto and the fish market, with 255 beds, all rooms ensuite, and a 24/7 reception.

Hotel American Dinesen is a four-star boutique hotel at Dorsoduro 628 on the San Vio canal with a 24-hour concierge, cocktail bar, terrace and water mooring; its room list names Classic, Superior & Canal View and Dependance categories.

Hotel Pensione Accademia is a three-star superior in Villa Maravege, a 17th-century residence at Fondamenta Bollani 1058, with two gardens, family run for over thirty years; it counts 12 minutes to La Fenice and 15 to St Mark's Square, its Basic Double is 12 sqm and the historic building has no elevator.

Generator Venice is a hostel in a former warehouse at Fondamenta Zitelle 86 on Giudecca with a 24-hour reception, bar, terrace and female-only dorms; it says every room has a view of the gardens, the Lido, the Grand Canal or Piazza San Marco, and that vaporetto lines 2 and 4.1 stop at Zitelle, 100 metres away.
Hotel Plaza is a four-star of 209 rooms facing Venice Mestre station, which it says is less than 10 minutes by train from Venice island and 17 minutes by bus from the airport.

Anda Venice Hostel is at Via Ortigara 10, Mestre, 200 metres from Mestre station, with mixed and female dorms of 6, 7 and 9 beds (ensuite) and ensuite doubles; it puts Venice a 10-minute train or bus ride away and offers 10% off and a free drink for direct bookings.

Leonardo Express, Fiumicino to Termini: EUR 14, about 32 minutes non-stop, every 15 minutes; 4 tickets in one transaction EUR 40; Metrebus integrated tickets not valid; first train from the airport 05:38, last 23:27 (Aeroporti di Roma).
Ciampino Airlink: EUR 2.70 per person, a direct bus of about 10 minutes from the airport to Ciampino station, then a train to Termini.
ATAC: BIT single EUR 1.50 valid 100 minutes; 24-hour EUR 8.50, 48-hour EUR 15, 72-hour EUR 22; tap&go on metro turnstiles and surface vehicles.

Roma Metropolitane's network map shows metro line A with stops at Ottaviano and Cipro on the Vatican side, and Spagna, Barberini, Repubblica and Termini; Termini is where lines A and B meet. Hotel dei Consoli says Ottaviano is 150 metres from the hotel.
note: ATAC's own accessibility and journey-planner pages sit behind a bot check and were not opened; station names rest on the Roma Metropolitane map.

claim: Residenza Paolo VI is a four-star by its own description in the premises of the Augustinian General Curia, opened for Holy Year 2000, with 35 rooms, a terrace with a view of St Peter's Basilica and the Apostolic Palace, two San Pietro Junior Suites with direct views of the dome, a 13 m2 French Bed Room and a 16 m2 Double Standard.

Palazzo Cardinal Cesi, owned by the Salvatorian general house, has 29 rooms of 12, 16, 18 and 20 m2, its entrance at Via della Conciliazione 51, a cloister garden, and says tickets for General Audiences and liturgical celebrations are free and requested from the Prefecture.

Hotel Bramante, Vicolo delle Palline 24 in Borgo Pio, has 16 rooms of 18 to 30 m2, says its origins date to 1550 and an inn opened in 1873, still shows a Jubilee 2025 page, and says free tickets are collected at the Bronze Door of the Vatican.

Hotel dei Mellini has 80 rooms over six floors at Via Muzio Clementi 81, designed by Harry Gregory, a terrace with sun deck and gym, Spanish Steps 10 minutes and St Peter's 15 minutes by its own account, a 12 m2 Petit Chambre with a single bed and 25 m2 Superior rooms.

Hotel dei Consoli has 28 rooms at Via Varrone 2/D, 150 m from Ottaviano and 750 m from St Peter's Square by its directions, a top-floor terrace with breakfast and a view of the dome, 11 m2 single and 13 m2 classic rooms, and quotes the Leonardo Express at EUR 15 and about 35 minutes.
note: Booking.com redirected the deiconsoli slug to a search page (closed_msg), so Booking URL is null; hotel's own site is live with a booking engine.

claim: Hotel Raphaël is a five-star Relais & Châteaux member since 2010 behind Piazza Navona, covered in wisteria and Virginia creeper, with 50 rooms of which 20 suites, works by Miro, lithographs by De Chirico and Picasso terracottas, and the Mater Terrae restaurant (organic, vegan, biodynamic).

Albergo del Senato is a 3-star hotel next to the Pantheon on Piazza della Rotonda with a rooftop terrace and buffet breakfast included; Penthouse, Senior and Junior Suites view the Pantheon and the site says a Pantheon view is not guaranteed for Standard rooms.

Albergo Santa Chiara began in 1839 as a wine shop, has 96 rooms in 3 adjoining buildings right behind the Pantheon, breakfast only with rates that include it, and no parking in the limited traffic zone.

Hotel Forum is a four-star superior of 78 rooms and suites in an 18th-century building at Via Tor de' Conti 25, with a Roof Garden breakfast, an American bar, and separate Deluxe with view and Suite with View categories; its page calls it the only hotel in the Roman Forum.

The Fifteen Keys Hotel is a 4-star of 15 individually designed rooms of varying sizes in a five-storey townhouse converted at the start of 2015, at Via Urbana 6-7, steps from the Colosseum and Roman Forum by its own account.

Palazzo Montemartini is a five-star Radisson Collection hotel next to the Servian Walls, walking distance from the Baths of Diocletian and steps from Termini, with the Thalea spa; its terrace page describes the summer season as June to September.

The RomeHello is an Esquilino hostel with dorm beds, private rooms, a social kitchen and a garden, and says all its profits go to social and environmental initiatives; Booking.com lists it at Via Torino 45.

Como's imposta di soggiorno is charged per person per night from 1 January 2024 (Giunta resolution 387 of 10 November 2023): €5 at five- and four-star hotels, €4 at three-star, €3 at one- and two-star hotels, and €3 at B&Bs, holiday flats and affittacamere, for up to 4 consecutive nights.

Bellagio's imposta di soggiorno rates from 1 January 2024 (Giunta resolution 147 of 13 November 2023) are €1 at one-star hotels, €2 at two-star, €3 at three-star, €4 at four-star and €5 at five-star hotels, €3 at holiday homes and other non-hotel lodgings and €5 at prestige villas, applied from 1 March to 30 November each year; the tax covers up to 7 consecutive nights and children up to and including 11 are exempt.

Varenna's imposta di soggiorno is charged per person per night from 1 January to 31 December: €5 at five-star hotels, €4 at four-star, €3 at three-star, €2.80 at one- and two-star hotels and €3 at B&Bs, holiday flats and other lodgings, for up to 7 consecutive nights; children under seven are exempt.

Navigazione Lago di Como's passenger fares from 1 April 2026 for a single adult ticket: three zones (Bellagio, Menaggio, Varenna and Cadenabbia between each other) €5.50, six zones €12.00 and seven zones €13.50; Como to Bellagio, Menaggio and Tremezzo is six zones and Como to Varenna seven; the rapid-service supplement is €5.00 for six zones and €5.50 for seven. The fare matrix is an image-only PDF, read by eye.

Car ferries on Lake Como run on ordinary services between Cadenabbia, Bellagio, Menaggio and Varenna; from 1 April 2026 a single trip for a car up to 3.50 m long costs €4.60 for the vehicle only or €10.10 with the driver.
Trenord runs direct trains from Milano Centrale to Como San Giovanni in about 40 minutes with a train every hour, and from Milano Cadorna to Como Lago in about 60 minutes every 60 minutes.
Trenord trains run from Milano Centrale to Varenna-Esino in about 64 minutes without changes and about every hour, and from Lecco to Milano Centrale in about 40 minutes.
Trenord's Malpensa Aeroporto T1 to Saronno service takes about 20 minutes with a train every 30 minutes and a second-class ticket costs €8.

Palace Hotel, Lungo Lario Trieste 16 in Como, is in a late 19th-century Liberty-style building between the city centre and the lake, with the Antica Darsena restaurant and a short walk to the Brunate funicular.
Hotel Metropole Suisse, Piazza Cavour 19 in Como, is run by the Cassani family for four generations, has 70 rooms, most recently refurbished, and a façade by Giuseppe Terragni.
Albergo Firenze, Piazza Volta 16 in Como, is a three-star hotel with 44 rooms from singles to triples, breakfast buffet included in the room price and a 24-hour reception.
Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni, Via Roma 1 in Bellagio, calls itself the only 5-star luxury hotel in Bellagio and describes April to November as the season for its lounges and gardens.
Belvedere Bellagio, Via Valassina 31, has been cared for by five generations of the Martinelli-Manoni family since 1880, with an acre of private tiered lawn and a spa.

Hotel Florence, Piazza Mazzini 46 in Bellagio, has three stars by its own account, a 24-hour front desk, has been run by one family since 1864, calls municipal parking very limited with the first car park 600 m away, and its site carried a reopening banner in November 2026.
Hotel Royal Victoria, Piazza San Giorgio 2 in Varenna, is a 19th-century hotel on the town's main square with 45 rooms and a pool.

Albergo Milano, Via XX Settembre 35 in Varenna, has rooms in the main building and annexes Casa Rossa, Casa 3 Archi and Casa Gialla, of which Casa 3 Archi and Casa Gialla have portable fans rather than air conditioning, breakfast from 8 to 10, and a restaurant closed on Tuesdays.
Grand Hotel Victoria, Via B. Castelli 3/13 in Menaggio, is a five-star hotel in two buildings, one historic and one modern, with a pool and a Victoria Beach Club.
Grand Hotel Menaggio, Via IV Novembre 77, faces the lake opposite Bellagio at the point where the lake's two branches meet, with the La Veranda restaurant.
Grand Hotel Tremezzo calls itself a luxury 5 star hotel, with Belle Epoque splendour, lawns and botanic gardens, and a sister villa, Villa Sola Cabiati, with six suites reached by car or boat.
Albergo Lenno, Via Lomazzi 23 in Lenno, describes itself as a four-star hotel a few steps from the Lenno pier, with 46 rooms and five apartments in an annex.

Positano charges a tourist tax per person per night of €5 in 5-star, €4 in 4-star and €3 in 3-star hotels and €2.50 in 1-2 star hotels and other lodging, from 1 April to 31 October 2026 (2025 rates confirmed for 2026); children under 10 are exempt.

Amalfi's published tourist-tax tariff (Giunta resolution 24 of 24 February 2022, in force from 1 January 2022) is €5 for 5-star, €4 for 4-star and €3 for 3-star and other hotels, per person per night, charged from 1 April to 2 November.

Ravello charges a tourist tax per person per night of €5 in 5-star and 4-star, €4 in 3-star and €3 in 2-star hotels, from 1 April to 31 October for up to seven consecutive nights; children under 16 are exempt (tariff updated by resolution 31 of 20 March 2019).
From 1 April 2026 Praiano charges €5 (5-star), €4 (4-star), €3 (3-star) and €2 (1-2 star) per person per night in hotels (resolution 11 of 21 January 2026).
Minori's 2026 tourist tax is €4 per person per night in 4- and 5-star hotels, €3 in 1-3 star hotels and €2 in B&Bs and most other lodging, charged from 1 January to 31 December.

Maiori's 2025 tourist tax (the latest schedule we found) is €4 per person per night in 4- and 5-star hotels, €3 in 1-3 star hotels and €2 in B&Bs and rooms to let, charged all year; children under 14 are exempt.

Sorrento's tourist tax (measures approved by Giunta resolution 154 of 8 August 2023, from 1 January 2024) is €4 in 5-star, €3 in 4-star and €1.50 in hotels up to 3 stars per person per night, from 1 April to 31 October, for up to seven consecutive nights; children under 18 are exempt.
Travelmar's 2026 full fares are €12 Salerno-Amalfi, €17 Salerno-Positano, €10 Amalfi-Positano and €5 Amalfi-Minori or Maiori.
Travelmar's timetable (updated from 1 October) is an annual service from Salerno Piazza Concordia by the train station, and crossings can be delayed by rough sea.
SITA SUD's COSTIERASITA ticket costs €10 and is valid for 24 hours from first validation on SITA SUD buses in the coastal comuni it lists.
SITA SUD published a notice dated 29 October 2026 of a new Costiera timetable from 2 November 2026.
Curreri Viaggi's airport shuttle runs between Naples airport and Sorrento station and costs €13.
Campania Express lists a Naples to Sorrento train service.
Le Sirenuse's own site describes 58 rooms and a Sersale family hotel at Via Cristoforo Colombo 30, Positano.
Hotel Marincanto's site describes a pool dug into the cliff, a private beach and rooms that are all different.
Hotel Savoia's site describes a family-run four-star hotel since 1936, with Standard Rooms at the back of the hotel.
Hotel Luna Convento's site says it was born from a monastery founded by Saint Francis of Assisi in 1222, with a cloister, restaurant terrace and pool.
Hotel Lidomare's site describes a small three-star hotel at Largo Piccolomini 9, reached from Piazza Duomo, with paid car valet parking.
Belmond's page for Caruso gives 50 rooms and suites, with Double Rooms of 35-50 m2.
Hotel Villa Maria's site says it is owned by the Palumbo family, between Villa Rufolo, the main square and Villa Cimbrone.
Hotel Onda Verde's site describes five private independent villas holding 25 rooms, a pool, and beach clubs 50 metres away.
Villa Romana Hotel & Spa's site describes a modern four-star in Minori, a few steps from the old centre, with an Otium spa and Roman bath.
Hotel Miramare's site describes a four-star in central Maiori, 50 metres from the sea, with a rooftop terrace and parking at an affiliated garage 10 metres away.
Grand Hotel Excelsior Vittoria's site describes a five-star hotel family-owned since 1834, opening onto Piazza Tasso, with private access to the port.
Hotel Nice's site says it is 50 metres from Sorrento's bus and train stations and describes itself as cheap accommodation.

Naples charges a tourist tax per person per night by category, by Giunta resolution 89 of 12 March 2026: from 1 January 2026 EUR 5.00 in 4- and 5-star hotels, 4.50 in 3-star, 3.50 in 2-star, 3.00 in 1-star, 4.50 other lodging, 5.00 short lets; from 1 May 2026 EUR 6.00, 6.00, 5.50, 4.50, 4.00, 5.50 and 6.00. No 2027 schedule found.
The tax is paid per person and per night up to a maximum of 14 consecutive days, by non-resident guests older than 14.
The comune describes the 2026 update as a EUR 1 rise over the base values, made possible by the 2026 budget law (L. 199/2025).
An Alibus single ride (airport to Piazza Garibaldi and the port) costs EUR 5.00, sold on board by the driver, at the arrivals exit machines and in several apps.

ANM lists Alibus stops at Piazza Garibaldi (Stazione Centrale), Immacolatella/Porta di Massa and Molo Angioino/Beverello, with 15 minutes from the airport to Stazione Centrale and 35 minutes to the port.
From the airport the first Alibus departs at 5.30 and the last at 00.00, with a maximum interval of 15 minutes.
ANM runs Metro Lines 1 and 6 and the funiculars of Chiaia, Montesanto, Centrale and Mergellina; Line 2 is run by Trenitalia; the EAV group runs the Cumana, Circumflegrea and Circumvesuviana.

NLG's Molo Beverello to Capri hydrofoil lists an adult fare of EUR 25 one way (EUR 23 on routes marked IR); Capri adds a landing contribution of EUR 2.50 from 1 November to 30 March and EUR 5.00 from 1 April to 31 October.
Alilauro's Molo Beverello to Ischia page lists adult fares of EUR 22.00 and EUR 22.80.
Caremar lists the Naples-Capri and Naples-Ischia ferry at EUR 14.80 and the Naples-Ischia hydrofoil at EUR 21.60; it has ticket offices at Molo Beverello and Porta di Massa.
The America's Cup Match in Naples is scheduled to start on 10 July 2027 and conclude over the weekend of 17-18 July 2027.
Palazzo Caracciolo's site lists 145 rooms, on Via Carbonara, and describes itself as a meeting hotel.
Starhotels Terminus's site lists 169 rooms and suites at Piazza Garibaldi 91.
BW Signature Collection Hotel Paradiso's site lists 72 rooms, on Via Catullo 11, with a top-floor restaurant.
Hotel Ginevra's page lists 18 air-conditioned rooms on Via Genova 116 and breakfast for a fee.
Hotel Toledo's site describes a building of 1725 with a lift, on Via Montecalvario 15.
Hotel San Francesco al Monte's site says it was created within a 16th-century monastery overlooking the Bay of Naples; Corso Vittorio Emanuele 328.
Decumani Hotel de Charme's site says it is housed in Palazzo Riario Sforza, an 18th-century building, with Superior, Comfort and Economy rooms.
Chiaia Hotel de Charme's site places it on the first floor of an 18th-century palace at Via Chiaia 216, 20 metres from Piazza del Plebiscito.
Grand Hotel Vesuvio's site describes a five-star hotel on Via Partenope that faces Castel dell'Ovo.
Grand Hotel Oriente's site says it is two minutes from Toledo metro station; Via Armando Diaz 44.
Grand Hotel Santa Lucia's site describes a four-star hotel on the waterfront with recently renovated rooms and suites.
Hotel Piazza Bellini's site lists rooms and mini apartments of different sizes and categories.

Monterosso al Mare's imposta di soggiorno is €3.00 per person per night in every accommodation type, for a maximum of 3 nights, confirmed for 2026 (Giunta resolution 153 of 14 November 2025); minors up to their twelfth birthday are exempt.

Vernazza's comune (which includes Corniglia) set its 2025 imposta di soggiorno at €3.00 per person per night for every accommodation type; its regulation, amended 6 November 2025, charges up to 3 consecutive nights and exempts minors up to their tenth birthday. No 2026 tariff table was found on the portal.

Riomaggiore's comune (which includes Manarola) raised its imposta di soggiorno from €2.00 to €3.00 per person per night from 1 January 2025 (Giunta resolution 156 of 30 November 2024), for a maximum of 3 consecutive nights (resolution 89 of 6 September 2025).

Levanto's published tariff (G.C. 197 of 3 November 2023, for 2024) is €1.50 per person per night in guest houses, B&Bs, apartments and hotels up to two stars, €2.00 in hotels above two stars, for up to three consecutive nights; minors under 14 are exempt. The page was last updated 15 February 2024.

La Spezia's 2026 tourist-tax regulation (amended by council resolution 39 of 15 December 2025) charges up to five consecutive nights and leaves the amount to the Giunta; we found no current rate table, and the operator's notice for hotels cites €2.50 per person per night under Giunta resolution 45 of 5 February 2018.
Our arithmetic from the Vernazza tariff: a couple staying four nights in Vernazza pays 2 x 3 x €3 = €18, because only three consecutive nights are charged.

The Cinque Terre Treno MS Card adult one-day price was €22.00, €29.50 or €35.00 by demand band (A, B, C) in the price list for 14 March to 1 November 2026; from 2 November to 31 December 2026 the adult prices are €17.30 (1 day), €29.00 (2 days) and €34.00 (3 days). No 2027 list was published when checked.
The Cinque Terre Treno MS Card allows unlimited second-class travel on regional trains between Levanto and La Spezia, plus access to the park's services including the Via dell'Amore.

Trenitalia says that from 2 November 2026 to 19 March 2027 a specific ticket (a Liguria regional-fare ticket, a regional pass or the Cinque Terre Treno MS Card) is required to travel on regional trains stopping in the Cinque Terre.

RFI works at Riomaggiore and Manarola stations stop trains for 48 hours between Corniglia and La Spezia on the weekends of 14-15 November, 19-20 December 2026, 9-10 January and 6-7 February 2027, with Levanto-La Spezia suspended on those nights from 22.30 to 6.30.

The park's Cinque Terre Trekking Card for adults aged 12 to 69 costs €10.00 for one day, €17.00 for two days and €23.50 for three, or €15.00, €26.70 and €37.50 on high-demand days; guests of partner accommodation (SR) can buy a one-day card at €5.00. The price list carries no stated season.
Access to the Via dell'Amore, included in both the Trekking Card and the Treno Card, requires a mandatory booking subject to available places.

On the park's trail page (message of 19 November 2026, 11:48, no weather alert) section 592-1 Riomaggiore-Manarola (Via dell'Amore) was listed Turistico, 592-2 Manarola-Corniglia Escursionistico (it was Chiuso on 3 November), and 592-3 Corniglia-Vernazza and 592-4 Vernazza-Monterosso Esperto.
Path 587 between Corniglia and Case Pianca is closed from 16 November 2026 for about three months under Vernazza ordinance 19 of 2 November 2026.

On the Consorzio 5 Terre Golfo dei Poeti Line 02 price list, from La Spezia the Cinque Terre daily return ticket is €42.00 adult and €15.00 reduced, the afternoon return €28.00, and a single to Vernazza or Monterosso €30.00. The list carries no stated season.

The operator's Line 02 timetables list the main season from 20 April to 27 September 2026 and a separate Cinque Terre Trip timetable from 2 November to 8 December 2026; Line 02 serves Riomaggiore, Manarola, Vernazza and Monterosso (not Corniglia). No 2027 timetable was published when checked.
The ferry consortium names Genoa (about 100 km from La Spezia) and Pisa (78 km) as the closest airports and says the train is the best way to reach La Spezia and the Cinque Terre.
Monterosso is the largest of the five towns within the Cinque Terre National Park, per Hotel Villa Adriana's own site.

Hotel Porto Roca, Via Corone 1, Monterosso al Mare, is listed by the park as a four-star and describes itself as perched high on the cliffs, with sea-view rooms, suites, a pool and the La Terrazza restaurant.
Hotel Palme, Monterosso, describes itself as a four-star with 50 rooms, each with shower, minibar, TV and safe, fully air-conditioned, with a buffet continental breakfast, a garden and a bar.
Hotel Villa Adriana, Via IV Novembre 23, Monterosso, is a three-star with an outdoor pool and says it is open from 1 April to 25 October 2026.

Gianni Franzi, Via San Giovanni Battista 41, Vernazza, is a trattoria with rooms on Piazza Marconi, which its site calls the salotto (living room) of the Cinque Terre; its first rooms date from the late 1960s.
La Malà, Via San Giovanni Battista 29, Vernazza, is an old Ligurian house turned into guest rooms, a couple of steps from the village square, with a natural-rock terrace.
Madüneta 5 Terre is a guest house at Via Fieschi 5/9, Corniglia, listed in the park's quality-mark directory.

Hotel Ca' d'Andrean, Via Discovolo 101, Manarola, is a family-run hotel in the old centre with spacious air-conditioned rooms with bathroom, some with a terrace, in a building where olives were once pressed; breakfast is in the garden in the good season.
Hotel Marina Piccola, Via Birolli 120, Manarola, has 12 recently renovated rooms: 7 doubles, 4 triples and one Junior Suite.
Da Baranin, Via Rollandi 29, Manarola, is listed by the park as a guest house (affittacamere) and offers classic rooms, doubles with sea-view balcony, family suites and an apartment.
Hotel Villa Argentina, Via De Gasperi 170, Riomaggiore, is listed by the park as a two-star and its site offers economy rooms, sea-view rooms and apartments, reached via a nearby lift.

Hotel del Sole, Via del Santuario 114, Riomaggiore, is a small family hotel on the main street, 600 metres from the station by its own count, and says its CETS partnership lets it offer guests a discount on train and trekking tickets.

Hotel Firenze e Continentale, La Spezia, offers room categories from Economy and Comfort to Superior, Deluxe and suites, and says the station a few steps away reaches the Cinque Terre in five minutes.
The official 24h Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine ticket for one individual was listed at EUR 18.00 on ticketing.colosseo.it on 2026-11-16.
Official Full Experience tickets (arena; underground and arena; attic) were each listed at EUR 24.00; Only Arena and Forum Pass SUPER at EUR 18.00.
Ticket sales, with compulsory reservation of the time slot for entry to the Colosseum, open 30 days before the visit date.
Tickets are issued in the holder's name and an identification document must be kept visible at the park entrances.
For visits from 9 May the ticket holder's name may be changed once, by midnight on the seventh day before the visit, in limited cases.
The standard ticket gives 75 minutes in the Colosseum; the Forum-Palatine entry can be used within 24 hours before or after the Colosseum booking time; arrive 15 minutes early.
From 25 October 2026 to 28 February 2027 the park is open 8.30 am to 4.30 pm, last admission 3.30 pm; closed 25 December 2026 and 1 January 2027.
Free admission is listed for the first Sunday of the month, 25 April, 2 June and 4 November.
On 2026-12-14 the standard ticket showed slots 8:30-15:15; 9:15 and 9:30 were closed or sold out and 15:15 showed 7 available (read 2026-11-16).
The Vatican Museums full entry ticket is EUR 20.00 without online booking and EUR 20.00 + 5.00 with 'Skip the Line' booking on the official site (EUR 25 total).
Vatican Museums tickets cannot be refunded and are valid solely on the day the ticket is issued.

The Vatican Museums name tickets.museivaticani.va as the only official online ticket site and warn of look-alike domains charging higher prices; the page does not say tickets from other sellers are refused.
Vatican Museums open Monday to Saturday 08:00-20:00 (last entry 18:00); the last Sunday of each month 09:00-14:00 (last entry 12:30) with free entry, except on listed holiday dates.
Sleeveless or low-cut garments, shorts above the knee, miniskirts and hats are not permitted in the Vatican Museums.
Japan's International Tourist Tax, the departure tax, is ¥3,000 per person from 1 July 2026, collected in the price of your ticket.
note: Secondary sources say tickets issued by 30 June 2026 keep the old rate; confirm with the National Tax Agency before stating it. The three related-reading cards take their text from add_internal_links.ARTICLES.

claim: By the Kyoto Local Meteorological Office's 1991-2020 normals, Kyoto's cherry trees first flower on 26 March and reach full bloom on 4 April.
In 2026 Kyoto's cherry trees first flowered on 23 March and reached full bloom on 30 March; in 2025 the dates were 27 March and 5 April.
note: Recheck in spring 2027 and add that year's dates.

claim: For the 2026 season, the first cherry forecasts came from the Japan Meteorological Corporation on 18 December 2025, Weathernews on 8 January 2026 and the Japan Weather Association on 29 January 2026.
Since 1 March 2026 Kyoto City charges an accommodation tax per person per night by room rate: ¥200 under ¥6,000, ¥400 from ¥6,000, ¥1,000 from ¥20,000, ¥4,000 from ¥50,000 and ¥10,000 from ¥100,000.
note: Related-reading cards take their text from add_internal_links.ARTICLES.

claim: The Philosopher's Path runs for about 2 km beside a canal from Ginkaku-ji to Nyakuoji Shrine, under some 400 cherry trees.
The Keage Incline is a 582-metre former inclined railway for canal boats, with about 90 cherry trees along its tracks.
note: Find the Kyoto City Waterworks Bureau's own page for the length and tree count.

claim: Nijo Castle has about 300 cherry trees of some 50 varieties; its 2026 cherry festival ran from 19 March to 19 April with evening openings.
note: Replace with the 2027 dates once announced.

claim: The Westin Miyako Kyoto traces its history to 1890, sits beside the Keage Incline three minutes' walk from Keage station, and completed a renovation in 2020 that halved the number of rooms and added a spa on a hot spring under the grounds.
Hotel Okura Kyoto Okazaki Bettei opened on 20 January 2022 with 60 rooms on four floors, on the grounds of the Okazaki Betsuin temple.
Suiran, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Kyoto has 39 rooms around a Meiji-era summer residence in Arashiyama, 17 with their own hot-spring bath.
By the Japan Meteorological Agency's 1991-2020 normals, Tokyo's cherry trees first flower on 24 March and reach full bloom on 31 March.
In 2026 Tokyo's cherry trees first flowered on 19 March and reached full bloom on 28 March; in 2025 the dates were 24 March and 30 March.
note: Recheck in spring 2027 and add that year's dates.

claim: Since 1966 the Japan Meteorological Agency has observed Tokyo's cherry sample tree at Yasukuni Shrine; it records flowering when five or six flowers are open and full bloom when about 80% are open.
Until 31 March 2027 Tokyo's accommodation tax is ¥100 per person per night on rooms of ¥10,000 to ¥14,999 per person and ¥200 from ¥15,000; rooms under ¥10,000 are exempt.
From 1 April 2027 Tokyo's accommodation tax becomes 3% of the room charge on stays of ¥13,000 or more per person per night, with cheaper stays exempt and licensed private lodging (minpaku) included.

Ueno Park, one of the five places designated as Japan's first public parks in 1873, has about 800 cherry trees, a blossom spot since the priest Tenkai brought cherries from Mount Yoshino in the 17th century; the 77th Ueno cherry festival ran from 14 March to 5 April 2026.
note: Festival dates change every year; recheck in spring 2027.

claim: Sumida Park's cherry trees line both banks of the Sumida River for about 1 km between Azuma Bridge and Sakura Bridge; the avenue is said to date from the eighth shogun, Tokugawa Yoshimune.
Chidorigafuchi has about 260 cherry trees along a green path of about 700 m, and Chiyoda City runs the boat pier on the moat, with rowing boats, pedal (cycle) boats and swan boats.
The Meguro River has about 800 cherry trees along about 3.8 km of both banks, with night lighting in season.

Shinjuku Gyoen has about 900 cherry trees of about 70 varieties, flowering from February to mid-April; adult entry is ¥500, alcohol is not allowed, and the Shinjuku Gate is a 10-minute walk from Shinjuku Station's South Exit.
Park Hyatt Tokyo occupies the top fourteen floors of the 52-storey Shinjuku Park Tower and reopened on 9 December 2025 after a 19-month renovation.

From 1 March 2026 a boat at the Chidorigafuchi pier costs ¥1,500 for 30 minutes (¥3,000 for 60) in cherry-viewing season and ¥1,000 for 30 minutes otherwise; the pier closes from December to February.
note: Recheck before the 2027 season; the city revised fees on 1 March 2026.

claim: Since 1 March 2026 Himeji Castle has charged ¥2,500 to everyone aged 18 or over who does not live in Himeji City, Japanese or foreign, and ¥1,000 to Himeji residents aged 18 or over; under-18s enter free.
note: The fee is by residence, not nationality: a resident is anyone with an address in Himeji City, shown with a My Number card, a driving licence or another official photo ID with name and address, and the city lists the residence card among them, so foreign residents pay ¥1,000 too. Before 1 March 2026 every adult paid ¥1,000 and children ¥300. Group rates (30 or more): ¥2,000 and ¥800.

claim: Himeji City says it set the March 2026 admission fee from what the castle's upkeep, operation and conservation will cost over the next ten years.
note: The city also says the money will go to restoring the castle's historic appearance and to inbound and digital services.

claim: Niseko United's 2026/27 price list puts an adult 1-day All Mountain Pass, which covers Annupuri, Niseko Village, Grand Hirafu and HANAZONO, at ¥12,600 in the regular season (12-23 December 2026 and 1-22 March 2027) and ¥13,500 in the peak season (24 December 2026 to 28 February 2027); none of the four resorts lists a foreigner price.
note: These are the listed prices; online they are lower (¥11,900 regular, ¥12,800 peak, on the HANAZONO page). No price by nationality or residency on the Niseko United, Grand Hirafu, HANAZONO or Annupuri price pages (English and Japanese) or in Niseko Village's 2025-26 price list; the one resident price found is jp.niseko.kutchan-local-pass. Niseko Moiwa is not in Niseko United and was not checked. Watch narrowed on 2026-10-08 to Niseko sentences, so other ski areas' lift prices (Hakuba) are not flagged.

claim: For 2026/27, Grand Hirafu and HANAZONO sell people registered as living in Kutchan a Hirafu-HANAZONO day pass for ¥3,000, marked down from ¥12,500, and a season pass for ¥90,800, marked down from ¥181,700, online only, after proving residence.

Japan's consumption tax has a standard rate of 10% and a reduced rate of 8%.

The Hotel Sanraku Kanazawa, Owaricho 1-1-1, has 215 rooms (superior rooms 32 to 35 m2); its page gives Omicho Market 1 minute, castle park 3, Kenrokuen 10 and Higashi Chaya 12 minutes on foot; it introduced a new online booking system on 27 May 2026.

Hotel Intergate Kanazawa, Takaokamachi 2-5, has 166 rooms, a communal bath (no towels supplied in the baths), a lounge with a gallery of Kanazawa crafts, no parking, and the Minamicho/Oyama Shrine bus stop at its door from the station east exit.

Sumiyoshiya Ryokan, Jukken-machi 54, says it has the longest history, 300 years, of the city's ryokan; about 300 m from the Omicho corner; two common baths, free bicycles, washer and dryer at ¥200 each use; dinner service suspended; closed 27 to 29 October 2026 and 24 to 26 November 2026.

Hiroshima Prefecture has charged an accommodation tax since 1 April 2026: ¥200 per person per night when the room-only price (including service charge, excluding meals and consumption tax) is ¥6,000 or more, nothing below ¥6,000; school trips and their leaders are exempt; the guest pays the hotel, which collects and remits it.

The prefecture's overview page describes only the prefectural accommodation tax; no separate Hiroshima City or Hatsukaichi accommodation tax was found on the official pages read (absence of evidence, not a statement by the city), and the hotels checked (Iwaso, Hotel Miyajima Villa, Toyoko Inn, Candeo) quote only the prefecture's ¥200 from 1 April 2026.

Hatsukaichi City's Miyajima Visitor Tax has applied since 1 October 2023 to people entering Miyajima by boat: ¥100 per person per visit, or ¥500 per person for a year; ferry operators add it to the fare; residents, commuters to the island, pre-school children, school-trip participants and holders of disability handbooks are exempt.

The JR West Miyajima Ferry adult fare is ¥200 one way (child ¥100; ¥400 and ¥200 return), about 10 minutes, with the ¥100 visitor tax charged separately on entering the island; IC cards and the Japan Rail Pass and JR-West Rail Pass are accepted; Great Torii route sails from Miyajimaguchi 9:10 to 16:10; a restoration project is under way for the Great Torii.

The JR West Miyajima Ferry's access page says the JR Sanyo Main Line from Hiroshima Station to Miyajimaguchi station takes about 28 minutes, and from Miyajimaguchi station you go through an underpass to the terminal.

Hiroden's airport limousine bus costs ¥1,500 for adults and ¥750 for children one way (IC cards accepted); Hiroshima City's tourism FAQ (updated 8 April 2026) gives about 50 minutes to Hiroshima Station and about 55 to the Hiroshima Bus Center, which sits near the Prefectural Office and the Peace Memorial Park.
Hiroshima City's FAQ lists a local bus from the airport to JR Shiraichi station (¥490, about 15 minutes) then the Sanyo Line to Hiroshima Station in about 45 minutes.
Hiroden's streetcar page gives a flat adult fare of ¥240 and child fare of ¥120, paid on getting off, and lists Genbaku Dome-mae to Hiroden-miyajima-guchi at ¥240.

Hiroden's recommended sightseeing route gives 13 minutes by streetcar from Hiroshima Station to Genbaku Dome-mae (Atomic Bomb Dome, Peace Memorial Park, Peace Memorial Museum) and 49 minutes on line 2 from there to Miyajima-guchi, then a 10-minute ferry.

Hiroden's 1-Day Streetcar Pass is ¥700 (child ¥350) and its 1-Day Streetcar and Ferry Pass ¥1,000 (child ¥550) including the Miyajima visitor tax; the ferry part covers the Miyajima Matsudai Kisen boats and is not valid on the JR Miyajima Ferry.

The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum is open 7:30-19:00 (March-July, September-November), 7:30-20:00 in August and 7:30-18:00 December-February, last entry 30 minutes before closing; admission is ¥200 for adults, ¥100 for high school students and free for junior high school students and younger; closed 30-31 December and mid-February (15-20 February 2027 for an exhibition change).

The museum says it is very crowded in the daytime and recommends early morning or evening; online reservation is needed for the extended early and late slots; web tickets can sell out; free guided tours by Hiroshima Peace Volunteers and daily talks by A-bomb legacy successors are listed; it describes using victims' belongings, A-bombed artifacts and survivors' testimonies to convey the horrors and inhumane nature of nuclear weapons.

Hotel Granvia Hiroshima is directly connected to JR Hiroshima Station, has the Granvia Floor on the 20th floor and a fitness room for guests, Standard Single rooms of 17-18 m2 and Standard Twin rooms of 26 m2; its official site says JR Hotel Members services and official-site booking pause from 02:00 on 8 November to 06:00 on 10 November 2026.

Toyoko Inn Hiroshima-eki Shinkansen-guchi No.1, 2-6-25 Hikari-machi, is a 4-minute walk from the Shinkansen exit of JR Hiroshima Station, serves a free onigiri breakfast 6:30-9:00, has a self-check-in kiosk and 55 paid parking spaces at ¥1,000 a night (first-come); check-out is 10:00.

Dormy Inn Hiroshima (Aki no Yu), 3-28 Komachi, is on Peace Boulevard, 3 minutes' walk from Chuden-mae streetcar stop, about 6 minutes' walk west to the Peace Memorial Park entrance and about 15 minutes north to the Atomic Bomb Dome, with large baths and saunas on the 8th floor, a free shuttle bus to Hiroshima Station, reopened 1 May 2026, and a notice (22 May 2026) warning of suspicious messages to Booking.com guests.

Rihga Royal Hotel Hiroshima, Motomachi 6-78, is 3 minutes' walk from Kamiyacho-higashi and Kamiyacho-nishi streetcar stops with the Hiroshima Bus Center and Astram Kenchomae both a short walk away; its health club has a 25 m, five-lane heated pool and hotel guests use it by reservation in two-hour slots; Standard Twin rooms are 22-38 m2.

Mitsui Garden Hotel Hiroshima, Nakamachi 9-12, describes itself as on Peace Boulevard within walking distance of the Peace Memorial Park, has a complimentary guests-only top-floor lounge, a 20 m2 room with two 1,230 mm beds, is about 7 minutes by car from Hiroshima Station and runs interior renovation from 1 April 2026 to 31 May 2027; it posted a phishing warning on 25 May 2026.

Candeo Hotels Hiroshima Hatchobori, 14-1 Hatchobori, gives Hatchobori Station as 2 minutes away, has a rooftop open-air bath (SkySpa), a Double with Desk of 16 m2 and no parking of its own or affiliated.

Nest Hotel Hiroshima Hatchobori, 13-12 Nobori-cho, has 126 non-smoking rooms of 13-24 m2 with Simmons beds and a complimentary breakfast served in the room; its page gives 2 minutes' walk to Ebisu-cho, 3 to Hatchobori and 10 to Hondori shopping street.

Iwaso, 345-1 Miyajima-cho (founded 1854), has four detached one-storey cottages built in the Taisho-Showa era and a radon hot spring open 15:00-24:00 and 6:00-9:30; Itsukushima Shrine is 300 m (3 minutes' walk) away, the pier 15 minutes' walk; a shuttle runs 8:00-20:00 but not to a timetable (phone 0829-44-2233 once the boat time is set).

Hotel Miyajima Villa (Miyajima-cho 1165), produced by the Kinsuikan ryokan (founded 1902), has town-house, sea and mountain concept rooms, a tatami-floored viewing bath fed by an artificial quasi-natural spring that is not open-air, excludes guests with tattoos from the large bath, closes 14-18 December 2026 for maintenance, and notes that the main sights have no car parks.

Miyajima Guest House Mikuniya has Japanese-style private rooms (one of ten tatami mats, four of eight) and a four-bed dormitory, rental yukata at ¥300, is about 5 minutes' walk from Itsukushima Shrine and about 15 from the ferry, offers no pick-up service and charges ¥1,000 per hour for check-in after 21:00.

Miyajima Coral Hotel, Miyajimaguchi 1-9-8, is about 5 minutes' walk from JR Miyajimaguchi station and about 30 seconds from the pier, offers free parking for guests from noon on arrival to noon on departure, a coin laundry, 11 room types including a 20 m2 Japanese-modern twin, and says the ferry crossing takes about 10 minutes.

Grandvrio Hotel Miyajima Wakura (Miyajimaguchi) has a natural hot spring with an open-air bath and sauna facing the Meoto Iwa rocks off Hanaguri island, 171 free parking spaces and a free shuttle from JR Miyajimaguchi station; the pier is about 12 minutes' walk or 3 minutes by car.

Tokyo Skytree's first-sunrise special opening is on Friday 1 January 2027, 5:30 to 7:30am, for 800 people; 580 places go through an online lottery at 11,000 yen with a 1,000-yen shop voucher (applications noon 5 Nov to 11:59pm 26 Nov 2026, results by email planned 1 Dec); the twin-room packages with the ticket at Tobu Hotel Levant Tokyo (from 75,000 yen for two) and Asakusa Tobu Hotel (from 80,000 yen), five rooms between them, went on sale at noon on 5 Nov and were marked 受付終了 by 20 Nov 2026.

Quintana Roo's lodging tax (Ley del Impuesto al Hospedaje, art. 8) is 5% of the invoiced value of lodging at hotels and similar establishments, and 6% for apartments, houses and private villas; the guest who pays for the lodging is the taxpayer (art. 7).

The law requires the provider to determine, withhold and pay the lodging tax expressly and separately (art. 11); the tax is never part of the value of the lodging (art. 12); on packages that include food and other services, the base is the lodging element, and at least 60% of the invoice total if the invoice does not itemise (art. 10).
Mexico's general IVA rate is 16% (Ley del IVA, art. 1), applied to the values the law sets, and the IVA is never part of those values.

Mexico City's Código Fiscal (arts. 162 to 164) taxes lodging: hotels, hostels and motels apply 3.5% to the total value of the lodging consideration (art. 164); where an intermediary collects payment for flats and houses the rate is 5%; the provider is the taxpayer but must pass the tax on to the guest (art. 162).

Article 163: the tax arises when payment is received and the base includes deposits, advances and other concepts; if lodging is bundled with accessory services (transport, food, use of facilities) that the provider does not itemise and prove, the whole value is treated as lodging. The December 2025 decree reforming the Código Fiscal for 2026 changed the audit (dictamen) threshold for lodging-tax payers to 14,913,178 pesos but did not amend arts. 162 to 164. Hotel Era says it has just eight rooms (Standard, Deluxe, Superior Suite, Superior Family), on Calle 6 Sur, La Veleta, with a pool, spa, fitness centre and The Garden Bar & Lounge; no room sizes are listed.

Akumal Bay Beach & Spa Resort's site describes 310 oceanfront junior suites in four beachfront buildings, all-inclusive, with direct access to the coral reef for snorkelling; it lists Tulum airport at about 40 miles (65 km), 55 minutes by car.

Under Law 47-06 (articles 70-76) the stay tax in tourist accommodation is charged per person and per night, added to the accommodation price, children under 12 are exempt, operators are responsible for collecting it, and invoices must show the amount separately; it is paid quarterly to the commune.

Article 73 of Law 47-06 sets legal ranges per person per night: guest houses, congress centres and luxury hotels MAD 15-30; riads and houses rented to tourists MAD 10-25; hotels 5 stars MAD 10-25, 4 stars 5-10, 3 stars 3-7, 1-2 stars 2-5; tourist residences 3-7; other tourist accommodation 2-5. Under article 168 the rate within the range is fixed by a decision of the commune after council approval; the Marrakech commune's own rate was not found.
The DGI's VAT page lists accommodation and restaurant services at the 10% reduced rate; the standard rate is 20%.
Editors' arithmetic: two adults, four nights, legal range MAD 10-25 gives MAD 80-200; a MAD 1,800 room for four nights is MAD 7,200 and 10% VAT is MAD 720.

ibis Marrakech Centre Gare (Avenue Hassan II, Place de la Gare) has 109 rooms, buffet breakfast, a 24-hour bar and a garden with a pool; Accor puts Jemaa el-Fnaa at a 10-minute drive.

Sir Albert (Albert Cuypstraat 2-6) is a former diamond factory; its gym is at Albert Cuypstraat 44.

Kamana Lakehouse says neighbouring development work began in April 2024, with noise Monday to Saturday 8am to 6pm, and that Lakeview Luxe and Tahuna Lakeview room views may be affected at times; it offers complimentary parking.
Arrowtown is described by the regional tourism organisation as a historic town with a legacy of the 1860s Otago gold rush.
If you last arrived in New Zealand on or after 1 November 2026 you can drive on an overseas car licence for 12 months; if you arrived before that, 18 months for a car licence.
A licence not in English needs an accurate English translation or an IDP; the IDP can be current or expired up to 6 months (car licences only); carry your overseas licence.
New Zealand drives on the left; roads are narrow, winding, sometimes steep; most are two-way single lane each way; not all rail crossings have active warnings; seat belts required; phone use illegal.
At one-lane bridges a red-bordered round sign means give way; a blue rectangle with white arrow means others give way to you; all one-lane bridges are signposted.
NZTA release 24 Aug 2026: SH94 Te Anau-Milford reopened after an overnight snow closure and was scheduled to close again for avalanche risk; the Milford Road Alliance runs avalanche control.

Jucy car search for 21-29 Nov 2026 from Queenstown Airport: small hatch and compact SUV 'Not available for pickup on 21st Nov'.
Norway's low VAT rate of 12% covers letting of rooms (accommodation); the normal rate is 25%. The Tax Administration page shows no explicit year but its year selector lists 2026 first.

Under the Storting's law on visitor contributions (decision of 5 June 2025), a municipality may charge an overnight fee of 3% of the payment for the stay excluding VAT (§ 2-3); it applies to the whole municipality (§ 2-1), to stays of under 30 consecutive days, the duty arises when the stay begins, the fee must be itemised in sales documents, and the municipality may set which months it applies; the ministry must approve the municipality's plan before the fee takes effect (§ 2-2).

Tromsø's council (kommunestyret) decided on 24 June 2026 to introduce the overnight fee, planned from 1 January 2027; the plan must be approved by the ministry before the fee can take effect (no approval found as of 28 Oct 2026); the draft local regulation is on public consultation with responses due 30 October 2026; the consultation does not cover the rate, which the city says is set in the law at 3%.

Visit Tromsø says the polar night lasts approximately from 27 November to 15 January, with a few hours of twilight a day; light returns gradually from mid-January and the sun is usually not visible from central Tromsø until later in January because of the surrounding mountains.

Visit Tromsø says the northern lights may be visible from late August to early April, that clear skies and darkness are essential, and that Tromsø lies within the auroral zone; it makes no guarantee of sightings.

Bussring's Tromsø Airport Express (Flybussen): adult NOK 125 one way, NOK 200 return (price list from 1 November 2024); trip to the airport about 15 minutes per Bussring (about 20 per Visit Tromsø); stops include The Dock Hotel, Scandic Ishavshotel, Havneterminalen (Prostneset), Storgata 44 (Scandic Grand), Polaria Strandveien, Moxy Hotel and the airport; Svipper says Flybussen tickets cannot be bought in the Svipper app; Visit Tromsø says it has dedicated luggage space.

City bus routes 24, 26, 40 and 42 stop at Tromsø Lufthavn Langnes (limited luggage space); tickets via the Svipper app, ticket machines or Visa/Mastercard on board, no cash; Svipper adult single 1 zone NOK 50 from 1 Feb 2026, off-peak single in Tromsø NOK 30 weekdays 09:00-14:00 and 17:00-01:00.

Avinor: the taxi rank is to the left outside the arrivals hall, the ride to the city centre takes about 10 minutes, and taxi drivers must give the price in advance; Visit Tromsø says prices vary between operators.

Quality Hotel Grand Tromsø (Storgata 44): breakfast always included, gym, social lounge. Comfort Hotel Xpress Tromsø (Grønnegata 35-39): next to Tromsø Cathedral, 8 minutes' drive from the airport, parking from NOK 42/h. Smarthotel Tromsø (Vestregata 6): double room 9 sqm, superior 12-15 sqm, breakfast buffet included when booking direct. Radisson Blu Hotel Tromsø: Cozy Small Room 12 m2, standard 18 m2, superior 23 m2, 4 km from Langnes Airport.

Scandic Ishavshotel (Fredrik Langesgate 2): by the quayside, 50 m from the Hurtigruten ferry, standard 19-21 m2, standard single 16-20 m2. Clarion Hotel The Edge (Kaigata 6): by the water, about 10 minutes from the airport, superior twin 16-22 m2, breakfast depends on price type, parking from NOK 40/h. The Dock 69°39 by Scandic (Skansegata 7, 0.5 km to centre): standard 16-18 m2, superior 20-21 m2, wellness with entrance fee aged 16+. Home Hotel With (Sjøgata 35-37): breakfast, fika and dinner included, compact double 13 m2, standard twin 15 m2.

St. Elisabeth Hotel & Spa (Mellomvegen 50): hotel describes a peaceful location 10 minutes from the city centre; daily spa sessions, adults-only after 13:00, spa passes booked online. Moxy Tromsø (Huldervegen 2): listed by Visit Tromsø as by Tromsø Airport; parking NOK 25/h or NOK 170/day; airport shuttle in partnership with Airport Express.
Tromsø Lodge & Camping is in Tromsdalen with 58 cabins in five categories, open all year, free parking, breakfast buffet; 5 minutes by car or 30 minutes on foot to the centre.

Malangen Resort (Skutvik, 9055 Mestervik) is a 70-minute drive south of Tromsø; shuttle bus from Tromsø city centre at fixed times 1 Dec-19 Apr, flexible shuttle 20 Apr-30 Nov; 10 hotel rooms, cabins and 20 waterfront apartments; the resort says its wilderness camp has minimal light pollution and calls itself one of the best northern lights hotspots in the Tromsø area.
Visit Tromsø says northern lights may be visible from late August to early April, but clear skies and darkness are essential.

In 2026 Kraków charges no local fee (opłata miejscowa) or tourist tax: Polish law allows the local fee only where climate, scenic value and tourism conditions are all met, and the City of Kraków's tourism office says most municipalities, Kraków included, do not meet them.

A Polish amendment to the local taxes act, passed by the Sejm on 18 Sep 2026 (Senate: no amendments, 24 Sep; President's signature recorded 15 Oct 2026), applies from 1 Jan 2027: a council may introduce a local fee in places with landscape value of up to 5.00 zloty a person a night (5.50 in spa-protection areas), set by council resolution and collected by the accommodation provider; the Council of Ministers is to set minimum landscape qualities by regulation. No Kraków council resolution was found.
VAT on accommodation services (PKWiU 55, Annex 3 item 47) is 8% in 2026 (the 8% rate applies under Art. 146aa of the VAT act, consolidated text Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1263).

Koleje Małopolskie line SKA1 links the Kraków Airport station (beside the terminal, covered footbridge) with Kraków Główny: 17 minutes on the timetable valid 25 Oct to 12 Dec 2026 (e.g. 06:17 to 06:34), departures about every 30 minutes from 06:17 to 22:17 and hourly earlier and later; fare Airport to Kraków Główny PLN 20 per Kraków Airport (Airport to Wieliczka PLN 24, matching the operator's page); luggage free.

Kraków Airport lists city/agglomeration bus lines 209 and 300 and night line 902; ZTP Kraków's line list shows 300 running Os. Podwawelskie to Kraków Airport and 902 running Dworzec Główny Wschód to Kraków Airport via Balice (209 is listed as Salwator to Mników via Balice). Lines 208 and 252 do not appear on either list.

ZTP Kraków price list for tickets valid in zones I+II+III: 15-minute PLN 4, 30-minute or single-ride PLN 6, 60-minute PLN 8, 90-minute PLN 9, 24-hour PLN 25; joint 70-minute KMK+KMŁ ticket PLN 10, valid on Kraków vehicles and trains between stations named Kraków, excluding Kraków Lotnisko (Kraków Airport).
SKA1 runs Kraków Główny to Wieliczka Rynek-Kopalnia in about 25 minutes; single ticket PLN 7.50.

Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial: admission to the grounds is free; entry requires a personalised entry card reserved online only at visit.auschwitz.org; no cards at the entrance; the Memorial advises booking in advance and arriving at least 30 minutes before the tour; visitors are asked to behave with due solemnity and respect.

Wieliczka Salt Mine tourist route: tours at designated hours depending on online ticket availability; online, at a ticket machine and at the ticket office (which sells only places not already bought online); 2-3 hours, about 3.5 km, maximum depth 135 m.
Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory, a branch of the Museum of Krakow, is at Lipowa 4; online tickets go on sale 90 days before a visit.

Hotel Stary: Szczepańska 5, steps from the Main Market Square; two restaurants and a wellness and spa area with sauna and pool; rooms on floors I-VI, some with balconies over the Main Market Square; room categories listed without sizes.

H15 Hotel Francuski: Pijarska 13; the hotel calls it the first building in Kraków built as a hotel; Brasserie L'Olympique; pet-friendly; Michelin Guide recommended for 2026; Comfort double 20 sqm, Premium double 26 sqm.

Hotel Pod Różą: Floriańska 14, former Renaissance palace, five-star, restaurant under a glass roof, wellness and spa in medieval cellars, renovated 2020; some rooms face Floriańska/Royal Route, others St Tomasz Street.
Hotel Rubinstein: Szeroka 12, historic tenement house with boutique character, restaurant, Sky Bar; breakfast included in several packages; Single 14 sqm, Economy Standard 18 sqm.

Metropolitan Boutique Hotel: Berka Joselewicza 19, between the Old Town Square and Kazimierz; 59 air-conditioned rooms; 24-hour gym; Fab Fusion restaurant; four stars; Classic 21-24 sqm, Superior 24-29 sqm.
Hotel Kazimierz (Hotel Kazimierz I): Miodowa 16, restored historic building, 38 rooms, air conditioning, breakfast buffet 07:00-10:30, no parking on site, no room sizes listed.

Hotel Copernicus: Kanonicza 16, Gothic building below the Royal Castle, Restaurant Copernicus, Copernicus Spa by L'Occitane in the Gothic cellars, first hotel in Poland in Relais & Châteaux per the hotel; room categories without sizes.
Hotel Senacki: Grodzka 51; by the hotel's count 450 m to the Main Market Square, 600 m to Wawel, 1.3 km to Kraków Główny; breakfast served daily; historic cellars.

Qubus Hotel Kraków: Nadwiślańska 6 (Podgórze per Booking.com), on the Vistula bank next to Kazimierz; about 196 rooms by sum of listed room types; top-floor glass-walled indoor pool 4 x 8 m, gym, jacuzzi, dry and steam saunas open 07:00-22:00, free for guests; Wawel about 20 minutes on foot per the hotel; pool and sauna closed Mondays 10:00-14:00 for maintenance.

Hotel Europejski: Lubicz 5, three stars; completed 1884; 41 rooms and 87 beds; five minutes from the station by the hotel's count; reception reached from Radziwiłłowska Street; Single 12 sqm, 2-person Plus 16 sqm; double size not stated.
ibis Krakow Stare Miasto: Pawia 15, 320 m / 5 min walk to Kraków Główny per Accor; hotel text says Old Town is a 15-minute walk; IBIS Kitchen restaurant; double/twin 14 sqm, premium/family 16 sqm.
ibis budget Krakow Stare Miasto: Pawia 11, 200 m / 3 min walk to Kraków Główny per Accor; hot buffet breakfast; car park; shuttle at additional charge; Standard single/double 12 sqm.

Porto's municipal tourist tax is EUR 3 per person per night, up to a maximum of seven consecutive nights (EUR 21), in force since 1 December 2024; guests aged 13 and over pay and children aged 12 and under are exempt, with proof.

Porto exempts children aged 12 and under, stays motivated by medical treatment (plus two companions), guests with a disability or incapacity of 60% or more (plus two companions), displaced people, the first night in pilgrim hostels, people housed by public social bodies and asylum seekers; exemptions need supporting evidence.

On 25 September 2026 Lusa reported that Porto council would vote the following Tuesday on starting the administrative procedure to amend the tourist tax regulation; the proposal named no value, and in July the mayor had admitted raising the tax from three to four euros. No decision was found.

Vila Nova de Gaia's city tax (taxa de cidade) is EUR 3 per night for guests aged 16 and over, up to seven consecutive nights per person per stay; Regulamento n.º 970/2026 was published on 22 July 2026 and enters into force 30 days after publication; it was EUR 2.50 before. Medical stays (one companion) and disability of 60%+ are exempt; groups travelling for work, study, sport or culture pay 50%.

Hotel-type accommodation falls under the reduced 6% VAT rate (item 2.17 of List I of the CIVA), which applies only to the accommodation price, including breakfast if not invoiced separately, according to a binding ruling published by Portal das Finanças (PIV 24650, 2023). The ruling does not itself say mainland.

Our arithmetic: two adults for four nights pay 2 x 4 x EUR 3 = EUR 24 in Porto or Gaia; with a 14-year-old the Porto total is EUR 36 and Gaia's stays EUR 24; nine nights are capped at seven, so EUR 42 for two adults.

Metro do Porto line E (violet) serves the airport and, per the airport's own page, runs every 20 or 30 minutes depending on the time and day; the airport-Trindade trip is a Z4 fare. No journey time was confirmed because metrodoporto.pt is closed to automated access.

Andante lists the Z4 trip at EUR 2.30 with a contactless bank card validated at stations including Aeroporto and Trindade, valid for 1h15m on Metro do Porto and STCP; from four journeys in a day the charge is capped at EUR 7.75 (the daily ticket).
The airport's page lists STCP and Resende (and other operators) for buses and says taxis circulate 24/7 and wait at ranks; it gives no taxi fare.

The Guindais funicular links the lower Ribeira station with the upper Batalha station, with track slopes reaching a maximum of 36.1% (Visit Porto); STCP Serviços suspended it from Saturday 18 July 2026 for a certification renewal and no reopening date was found as of 19 October 2026.

Visit Porto's Historic District (Porto and Gaia) lists Ponte Luís I, Palácio da Bolsa, São Bento station, Ribeira, the Sé, the Clérigos Tower, the Alfândega and Port wine caves, and calls the historic centres of Porto and Gaia the ideal choice for UNESCO World Cultural Heritage.

Visit Porto's Downtown (Baixa) district covers Avenida dos Aliados, the Bolhão market, Rua de Santa Catarina, the Coliseu, Igreja do Carmo, Jardim da Cordoaria, Bombarda, Batalha and Rua de Cedofeita, and says it truly comes alive at night.

Visit Porto's Boavista district lists Casa da Música, the Palácio de Cristal, the Botanical Garden, the Bom Sucesso market and the Faculty of Architecture, and describes a mix of modern and traditional architecture and many international companies.

Visit Porto's Atlantic district covers Foz, beaches, seafront promenades, the Pérgola da Foz and the Parque da Cidade, described as the largest urban park in the country at over 85 hectares and the only European park beside the sea.

Pestana Vintage Porto: Praça da Ribeira 1, built by combining 18 buildings, views of the Douro, the Gaia cellars and the Dom Luís I bridge; Rib restaurant, Vinology Wine Bar, Heritage Bar, gym; room types include Front View, Bridge View and River View.

Porto A.S. 1829 Hotel: between Rua das Flores and Largo de São Domingos, in the Araújo & Sobrinho stationery shop building; 41 rooms in eight types; restaurant Galeria do Largo; Double Small 14 m2, Double 15 m2, Superior City View 20 m2.
Infante Sagres: Praça D. Filipa de Lencastre 62; 85 rooms and suites; full renovation completed in 2024; summer terrace and plunge pool with seasonal closure from 6 October.

Grande Hotel do Porto: Rua de Santa Catarina 197, pedestrian street with restricted car access; classical style from 1880; 94 rooms; standard rooms 14-17 m2; five minutes from São Bento station by the hotel's count; gym and terrace.

Gallery Hostel: Rua Miguel Bombarda 222; opened 2011 in a restored 19th-century building; rooms named after local artists; art gallery and games room; seven dorms and two private rooms in the hostel building; garden-wing doubles of 18 m2; complimentary bike rental and daily walking tours.

ROSA ET AL Townhouse: Rua do Rosário 233, Cedofeita; seven suites in an 18th-century building; Queen Deluxe City Heritage 33 m2 with original plasterwork ceiling; Queen Deluxe suites face Rua do Rosário street life.

The Yeatman: Rua do Choupelo, Vila Nova de Gaia; Relais & Châteaux; on a hill amid the Port wine lodges; every room and suite has a terrace or balcony with views over Porto; indoor and outdoor infinity pools, Wine Spa, restaurant with two Michelin stars.
Porto River Soul Hotel: Gaia; 65 rooms in six types; near the Port wine cellars, the Dom Luís I bridge and Ribeira; Rabelo restaurant, Azure wellness; Superior River View 22 m2, Interior View 26 m2.

Hotel da Música: Mercado do Bom Sucesso, Largo Ferreira Lapa; 85 rooms; no swimming pool; gym; car park EUR 12/day; Standard Room from EUR 85 on the hotel's own page; Crystal Palace Gardens 1 km, Luís I Bridge 3.5 km, airport 17 km by the hotel's count; autumn sale up to 15%.

Porto Palácio Hotel by The Editory: Avenida da Boavista 1269; Auge restaurant on the 19th floor with panoramic views; spa of 1,500 sqm with indoor pool; Executive Rooms 29 m2; the hotel describes the avenue as the heart of Porto's business and financial centre.

Vila Foz Hotel & Spa: Avenida de Montevideu 236, Foz do Douro; restored 19th-century manor plus a contemporary building; 66 rooms and suites; spa; Vila Foz restaurant (one Michelin star, 2022 guide, by the hotel's text) and Flor de Lis.

Duas Portas: Rua das Sobreiras 516, Foz; eight rooms, four facing river and sea and four facing the garden; in front of the mouth of the Douro, ten minutes from the centre by its own count; wine bar, bicycles; airport transfer and tours at extra cost.

claim: Singapore's GST has been 9% since 1 January 2024 and is charged on the price including the usual 10% service charge, about 19.9% over the headline price in all.

Contactless Visa, Mastercard and American Express cards and phone wallets can be tapped at MRT gates and on buses (SimplyGo).

Marina Bay Sands opened in 2010; its SkyPark infinity pool, 150 m long and 200 m up, is for hotel guests only; a US$1.75 billion renovation is rebuilding its rooms into about 1,850, some 770 of them suites.
Raffles Singapore opened in 1887 and reopened on 1 August 2019 after a restoration begun in 2017, as an all-suite hotel with 115 suites.
Pan Pacific Singapore has 790 rooms at Marina Square, linked to the Marina Square mall and the Suntec convention centre.
The Fullerton Building was completed in 1928 as the General Post Office, opened as The Fullerton Hotel Singapore (400 rooms) in 2001, and became a National Monument in 2015.
The Warehouse Hotel has 37 rooms in an 1895 godown at Robertson Quay and opened in January 2017.
Pan Pacific Orchard, a 23-storey garden hotel by WOHA, opened in June 2023 with four open-air terraces (forest, beach, garden, cloud).
Hilton Singapore Orchard, the former Mandarin Orchard at 333 Orchard Road, reopened on 24 February 2022 after a S$150 million renovation, with 1,080 rooms, Hilton's largest hotel in Asia Pacific.
YOTEL Singapore Orchard Road has 610 compact rooms ('cabins') over 30 floors at 366 Orchard Road and opened in 2017.
PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering opened in January 2013: 367 rooms in a WOHA tower with some 15,000 square metres of planted sky terraces, about twice the area of its site.
The Clan Hotel Singapore has 324 rooms at 10 Cross Street, opened on 1 March 2021, with direct access to Telok Ayer station.
Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa has 454 rooms with balconies on the beach at Siloso Road.
Capella Singapore, by Foster + Partners around two 1880s military buildings on Sentosa, opened in March 2009 with 112 rooms.

The Chinatown festival organiser lists Chinatown station (North East and Downtown lines), Outram Park (East-West line) and Maxwell (Thomson-East Coast line) as the MRT stations for its sites.

River Hongbao 2026, its 40th edition, ran at Gardens by the Bay from 15 to 24 February 2026, free to enter, with festivities from 6.30pm on 15 and 16 February and from 2.30pm daily from 17 to 24 February; it is organised by SFCCA with SCCCI, SPH Media's Chinese Media Group, the Singapore Tourism Board and the People's Association; riverhongbao.sg still described 2026 on 1 November 2026.

South Africa's standard VAT rate is 15% on supplies of goods and services by registered vendors.
SARS's VAT 411 guide treats hotel-type accommodation as 'commercial accommodation', a taxable supply (as opposed to exempt accommodation in a dwelling).

TOMSA is a 1% tourism levy charged on the room rate at accommodation businesses that take part; it is voluntary for businesses, compulsory for guests where it is collected, is administered by the TBCSA and passed to South African Tourism, and TOMSA says it is not a tax.

Editors' arithmetic (not an official example): on a R3,000 room, 15% VAT is R450 and a 1% levy is R30, giving R3,480; TOMSA does not say whether its 1% is worked out before or after VAT, so before is assumed.

Airports Company South Africa lists authorised airport taxis (walk-in from the transport kiosks and domestic arrivals desk, 5am to midnight), Uber and Bolt as app-based operators, and the shuttle companies Citi Hopper and Centurion Tours, and advises arriving passengers to use only authorised airport taxis and not to accept rides from unsolicited drivers.

From 1 July 2026 MyCiTi's myconnect card costs R40; a Mover fare for 0-5 km is R19.50 peak (weekdays 06:45-08:00 and 16:15-17:30) and R15.00 saver; One Day Pass R130, Three Day Pass R290, Seven Day Pass R420.
