Cape Grace's site gives West Quay Road, V&A Waterfront; a private quay; rooms onto the harbour, marina or Table Mountain; Harbour View and Mountain View deluxe categories; a pool, Fairmont Spa and Heirloom restaurant.
Victoria & Alfred Hotel's site: a 1904 North Quay Warehouse at PierHead, V&A Waterfront; 24-hour room service; complimentary beverage on arrival; pool, spa and gym available at The Dock House.
Mount Nelson's site: 76 Orange Street, Gardens; open since 1899; 196 rooms and suites; nine acres of gardens; seven restaurants; rooms 32-63 m2, Signature Suites 88-180 m2.
The Grand Daddy's site: 38 Long Street; boutique rooms and suites; Rooftop Airstreams, described as the only collection of authentic, fully converted Airstreams on a rooftop.

Ashanti Gardens Guesthouse's site: 7 Union Street, Gardens; two restored Victorian buildings; en-suite double, twin and triple rooms and a family room; a communal kitchen in each house; reception 8am-4pm with a team member on site 24 hours; Ashanti Lodge Backpackers has closed.

Cape Town Lodge's site: 4-star, 101 Buitengracht Street; 124 rooms on higher floors with views of Table Mountain, Lion's Head, Signal Hill, the harbour and the Bo-Kaap; rooftop pool; complimentary fitness centre; Superior Rooms have a shower only.

The Winchester Hotel's site: 4-star, 221 Beach Rd, a 1920s Cape Dutch-style building on the edge of the Sea Point Promenade; courtyard, pool, Shoreditch restaurant, Harvey's Bar; limited off-street parking.

The Greenhouse Guesthouse's site: Victorian guest house, 69 Somerset Road, Green Point; 7 bedrooms with en-suite showers; V&A Waterfront, Zeitz Museum, Bo-Kaap and Robben Island ferries within 5-10 minutes' walk; Cape Town Stadium 1 km; MyCiTi stop on the doorstep.

The Twelve Apostles Hotel and Spa's site: Victoria Road, Camps Bay; 70 rooms and suites; ocean or mountain vistas from almost every room; a spa; Camps Bay 8-minute drive and V&A Waterfront 15-minute drive.

The Bay Hotel's site: 69 Victoria Road, Camps Bay beachfront; four pools, a gym, indoor and outdoor padel courts, a spa, the Tides restaurant; Mountain View rooms face Table Mountain and the Twelve Apostles range.

The Cellars-Hohenort's page on Collection McGrath: five-star, nine acres of gardens in the Constantia Valley, 15 minutes' drive from the city centre, 51 guest rooms and suites with views of Table Mountain.
The Alphen's site: Alphen Drive, Constantia; Provincial Heritage site; 18 designer suites in the Mill Range and Dower House; heated pool, spa and three restaurants; edge of the Constantia Greenbelt.

From 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 Barcelona's tourist tax (Catalan rate + €5 city surcharge) is €12 a person a night at five-star and grand luxe hotels, €8.40 at four-star, €9.50 in tourist flats, €6 in youth hostels and €7 in other establishments, including three-star hotels.
Barcelona's ordinance 2.2 (approved 30 January 2026) phases the city surcharge in: €5 from 1 April 2026, €6 from 1 April 2027, €7 from 1 April 2028, reaching the €8 maximum from 1 April 2029.

Catalonia's tax on stays exempts under-17s, is charged for at most 7 nights per person per continuous stay in one establishment, applies the rate in force at booking if the booking and tax are paid then, and forms part of the VAT base.
From 1 October 2026 El Prat de Llobregat and L'Hospitalet de Llobregat (among others) add municipal surcharges; a four-star there pays €1.80 + €1.80 = €3.60 a person a night.
Our arithmetic: a couple, four nights, four-star = 2 × 4 × €8.40 = €67.20; five-star = 2 × 4 × €12 = €96.

The Aerobús (A1 to T1, A2 to T2) runs 24 hours a day all year; a single is €7.75 and a return €13.30, under-4s free; into town it stops at Plaça d'Espanya, Gran Via–Borrell, Plaça Universitat and Plaça de Catalunya.

The R2 Nord train leaves from T2 roughly every 30 minutes from 6am to midnight, stopping at Sants, Passeig de Gràcia and El Clot-Aragó; all integrated travel cards are valid on Rodalies to and from the airport; free T1–T2 shuttle.
Metro L9 Sud serves T1 and T2 every 7 minutes; TMB gives 32 minutes to the centre; the Airport ticket is €5.90; single tickets and the T-casual are not valid at the airport stations.
A TMB single ticket (metro, bus, Montjuïc funicular) costs €2.90 in 2026.
The one-zone T-casual costs €13 for 10 integrated journeys, with up to 3 transfers within 75 minutes.
The Hola Barcelona Travel Card gives unlimited travel for 1–5 days from €12.50 (24 h), 10% off online, and includes one metro trip from and one to the airport.
Barcelona's metro runs 5am–midnight Monday to Thursday, until 2am on Fridays and eves of holidays, and non-stop on Saturday nights.

Hotel Neri: 22 rooms and suites in two historic buildings, one a 12th-century palace, on Plaça Sant Felip Neri (Carrer de Sant Sever 5); only the Deluxe Balcony room has a balcony on the square; the hotel's 'Momento Neri' package (one night Deluxe with breakfast) is €530.

Room sizes from the hotels' own sites: Majestic entry rooms 20–25 m²; Casa Bonay Passage Mini 172 sq ft; Hotel Gótico doubles 18 m², singles 13 m², triples 24 m²; Hotel REC Quiet REC about 15 m²; Hotel Brummell 12–20 m².
No tourist tax applies in Madrid in 2026: Spain has no national tourist tax and the Comunidad de Madrid has no taxes or surcharges of its own in force in 2026 (Ministry of Finance).
Spain applies its reduced 10% VAT rate to hospitality services (hotels and restaurants); the standard rate is 21% (Ley 37/1992, arts. 90 and 91).
From 1 April 2026 Barcelona's tourist tax at a four-star hotel is €8.40 a person a night (Catalan rate €3.40 + city surcharge €5).

EMT's Exprés Aeropuerto (line 203) runs 24 hours between T1, T2, T4 and Cibeles/Atocha; single fare €5 paid on board (cash, card or mobile); passes not valid; Atocha 6:00-23:30 every 15-20 min, Cibeles 0:00-5:40 every 35 min; Atocha to T1 30 min.

Metro de Madrid single zone A ticket costs €1.50 for up to 5 stations, +€0.10 per extra station, max €2.00; the airport supplement for Aeropuerto T1-T2-T3 and T4 stations is €3; Multi card costs €2.50.
Metro line 8 runs Nuevos Ministerios - Airport T4, 06:05 to 02:00.

Cercanías line C1 (Príncipe Pío - Atocha - Chamartín - Airport T4) leaves from T4 floor -1; Aena lists singles at €1.70 (1-2 zones), €1.85 (3 zones), €2.60 (4 zones); free for passengers with AVE tickets connecting with a flight.
Madrid taxis charge a fixed €33 (Tarifa 4), 24 hours, between the airport and the area inside the M-30, with no supplements; the city kept the price unchanged for 2026.

Madrid's tourist travel pass (Título/Abono Turístico) zone A costs €10.30 (1 day), €17.50 (2), €23.10 (3), €27.80 (4), €33.40 (5), €43.20 (7); valid calendar days from first use; under-11s 50% off; no airport supplement needed on Metro; not valid on the Exprés Aeropuerto bus.

Paseo del Prado and Buen Retiro, a landscape of Arts and Sciences, was declared UNESCO World Heritage in July 2021; it includes the Paseo del Prado from Cibeles to Atocha and the 120-hectare Retiro gardens; the Prado, Thyssen and Reina Sofía lie within two kilometres.

Malasaña is bounded by Gran Vía, Calle Fuencarral, Calle Carranza and Calle de San Bernardo; it is named after Manuela Malasaña, a heroine of the 2 May 1808 uprising, and was the birthplace of the movida madrileña in the 1980s.
Construction of Gran Vía began in 1910.

Cervantes lies in the church of San Ildefonso (convent of the Trinitarias Descalzas) on Calle Lope de Vega; Lope de Vega's house museum is on Calle Cervantes; Calle de las Huertas has quotations from Spanish writers carved in its cobbles.
Barrio de Salamanca was planned in the second half of the 19th century by José de Salamanca, Marquis of Salamanca, on a grid; Calle Ortega y Gasset is the Golden Mile of fashion.
Madrid Pride (MADO) 2026 ran from 25 June to 5 July, centred on Chueca, with stages at Plaza de Pedro Zerolo, Plaza del Rey, Puerta del Sol and Plaza de España.
Room Mate Alicia (Plaza de Santa Ana) lists its Single rooms at 10 m² and its Double Suite with Terrace at 50 m².
Room Mate Óscar is on Plaza de Pedro Zerolo, with a terrace with pool, breakfast until 12, dog friendly, Standard rooms 21-26 m².
Only YOU Hotel Atocha occupies a restored 1886 building on Paseo de la Infanta Isabel with 204 rooms around a central courtyard.
Wellington Hotel & Spa Madrid, Calle Velázquez 8, has 237 rooms and suites and the Le Max Wellness Club with pool, Jacuzzi, sauna and steam bath.
Four Seasons Hotel Madrid, in Centro Canalejas, unites seven historic buildings; Superior rooms face an open-air inner courtyard.

Casa de las Artes Meliá Collection is a four-star at Calle de Atocha 83 in the Barrio de las Letras, with terrace junior suites (one room with a 35 m² terrace) and dogs accepted on request at extra charge.

Generator Madrid, Calle San Bernardo 2, is a five-storey building that was once a car park and petrol station, with private en-suite rooms, shared and female-only dorms and the Broken Shaker rooftop bar.

No tourist tax is in force in Seville or elsewhere in Andalusia in October 2026: the Junta de Andalucía's list of the region's own taxes (ecological taxes, the customer-deposit tax, the single-use plastic bag tax and the improvement levy) includes none on tourist stays, and no decree or bulletin creating one was found.

Santa Cruz was Seville's Jewish quarter until the expulsion of 1492; the tourist office calls it a high-traffic tourist area and asks visitors to respect residents; the Cathedral, Giralda and Real Alcázar are listed among its sights.

Plaza Nueva has been the centre of civil power for centuries and is home to the City Hall; Sierpes and Tetuán are among the city's busiest shopping areas; the Plaza de Armas bus station is listed in the same district; El Arenal was Seville's main port in the Middle Ages and has the Torre del Oro, Hospital de la Caridad and the Maestranza bullring and theatre.

Triana began as a suburb outside the city walls and is the birthplace of potters, bullfighters, sailors and flamenco artists; Calle Betis has river views, the Triana ceramics centre and flamenco peñas and tablaos are listed; the 19th-century Triana Bridge connects it to the centre.

The Alameda de Hércules, inaugurated in 1574, is considered the oldest public promenade in Europe; two Roman columns at its southern end carry statues of Hercules and Julius Caesar; renovated in 2008; part of the city's alternative scene; the tourist office advises going in the late afternoon or at sunset. It lies in La Macarena, with the Macarena basilica and one of the best-preserved sections of the 12th-century Almohad walls.

Nervión lies east of the historic centre and includes Santa Justa station; ibis Styles counts a 20-minute walk to Santa Cruz and the Giralda; Catalonia Santa Justa counts 15 minutes on foot to the historic centre.

EME Catedral Mercer, Calle Alemanes 27: 5-star, 16th-century Andalusian building, 'in the picturesque Santa Cruz District, in front of the impressive Seville Cathedral'; rooftop pool and solarium (hours 11:00-20:00); Superior 22-29 m², Deluxe 25-27 m²; M SPA Thermal Circuit by prior reservation, maximum 6 people.

Hotel Casa 1800 Sevilla, Calle Rodrigo Caro 6: two minutes' walk from the Cathedral and Giralda; house-palace whose structure dates from an 1864 refurbishment; 33 rooms in six categories; rooftop pool open 365 days a year 10:00-20:00 with day passes for non-guests in summer; no private parking; top categories have a private terrace and jacuzzi.

Hotel Murillo, Calle Lope de Rueda 7-9, Barrio de Santa Cruz: '2 star hotel'; Superior doubles on the upper floors with private terrace, kettle with coffee and infusion set; the group's site lists Hotel Murillo Reinoso, Suites Murillo Alcázar, Suites Murillo Catedral and Suites Murillo Plaza Sta. Cruz.

Hotel Inglaterra, Plaza Nueva 7: the Fonda Inglaterra opened in 1857 opposite the Town Hall and the hotel calls itself the oldest hotel in the city; Classic rooms 20-30 m², Deluxe Double 34-44 m²; Coffee Corner with complimentary tea, coffee and water; La Terraza rooftop bar, 'one of the most popular night spots in Seville'.

Hotel Bécquer, Calle Reyes Católicos 4: four stars, family tradition over fifty years, free minibar, Sevillian courtyard; free flamenco performances for guests on Fridays (25 Sept; 16, 23, 30 Oct; 6, 13 Nov 2026); Cathedral 900 m on foot, Real Alcázar 950 m, Triana 400 m via the Isabel II bridge; Holy Week processions pass the entrance.

Hotel Simón, Calle García de Vinuesa 19: 18th-century Andalusian building, 50 m from the Cathedral, 'uno de los hoteles más antiguos de Sevilla'; patio with fountain; 24-hour reception; continental buffet breakfast; footer 'Categoría: 1 Estrella'; some rooms with traditional Andalusian decoration, tiles and dark wood furniture.

Triana House, Calle Rodrigo de Triana 94: boutique hotel and bed and breakfast with seven rooms, each paying tribute to an Andalusian province; 'the first Passivhaus-certified hotel in Andalusia'; no room sizes published.

Albergue Triana, Calle Rodrigo de Triana 69: hostel in a traditional Triana house, shared room or double, breakfast included, jacuzzi in summer; Cathedral and Real Alcázar 15 minutes' walk, Calle Betis 5 minutes, Triana Market 8 minutes; Booking.com lists it as Hostel Triana Backpackers.

The Corner House, Alameda de Hércules 11: urban hotel with a rooftop overlooking the square, restaurant El Disparate ('recomendado en la Guía Michelín', per the hotel), reception 8:00-16:00, late check-in by arrangement.

Catalonia Santa Justa, José Laguillo 8: close to the AVE station, 15 minutes on foot to the historic centre; rooftop pool, jacuzzi and spa; single 10 m², double 16 m²; pool closed 31/10 to 31/03 (dates subject to change).

Metrovalencia's fares page lists SUMA T1+, T2+ and T3+ (unlimited travel for 24, 48 and 72 hours, AB+ combination) at €9, €14 and €17, card not included.
Metrovalencia's temporary fare reductions run to 31 December 2026 and apply to multi-trip and monthly passes (SUMA 10, monthly SUMA, TuiN and others), not to the single ticket.

Visit València lists metro hours of 04:00 to 23:30 on weekdays and 05:00 to 00:30 at weekends, with an average frequency of every 10 minutes, and says the Valencia Tourist Card (24, 48, 72 hours) covers the metro to and from the airport, tram, EMT, Metrobus and Renfe local trains.
Última Hora reported on 10 March 2026 that Metrovalencia would run uninterrupted from Friday 13 March to the early morning of 20 March 2026, 168 hours.
Visit València puts lines 3, 5 and 9 at Xàtiva or Colón for the old centre, tram line 10 for the City of Arts and Sciences and Ruzafa, and tram lines 4 and 6 for the beaches and the marina.

Caro Hotel: five-star boutique hotel at Calle Almirall 14 (Seu-Xerea), 38 rooms in two historic buildings, about 200 m from the cathedral; the hotel calls itself the oldest standing building in València, with Roman and Arab-wall remains; booking direct offers free cancellation up to 48 hours before arrival.

Only YOU Hotel Valencia: 100 m from Plaza del Ayuntamiento and 500 m from the cathedral and Silk Exchange; gastronomic spaces at street level and on the ninth floor including El Mirador; room categories include Inner Premium and Premium with views.
Red Nest Hostel Valencia: C/ de la Paz 36, 24-hour reception, dormitories of 4 to 12 beds, common area on the fifth floor, breakfast at Purple Nest Hostel 300 m away (extra).
Sercotel Valencia Ruzafa: 73 rooms at Carrer de Cuba 4, just over 10 minutes' walk from the Town Hall Square, outdoor pool, private parking, Double Room 16 m2.
Petit Palace Ruzafa: Carrer de Sueca 14, doubles 18 m2, singles 14 m2, closest hotel to the Joaquín Sorolla AVE station, flexible check-out until 15:00 on Sundays and Mondays.
Hospes Palau de la Mar: late-19th-century bourgeois palace on Calle Navarro Reverter in the Eixample, with the Bodyna spa and the Ampar restaurant.
ILUNION Aqua 4: Luis García Berlanga 19-21, four-star, near the Oceanogràfic, 163 double rooms of 20 m2, ground-floor restaurant, accessible rooms.
Room Mate Ciencias: Avenida Instituto Obrero 20, double rooms 15 m2, breakfast until 11:30, dog friendly, parking upon reservation and availability, next to the City of Arts and Sciences.
Hotel Primus Valencia: four-star at C/ Menorca 22, 600 m from the City of Arts and Sciences, spa, gym, terrace, outdoor pool in the garden, free parking and 14:00 check-out listed for web bookings.

Las Arenas Balneario Resort: five-star grand luxury, Eugenia Viñes 22-24, facing Las Arenas beach, Classic room (city view) 28 m2, Deluxe (terrace with sea view) 30 m2 excluding terrace, heated pool, Sorolla restaurant.
Hotel Boutique Balandret: Paseo Neptuno 20, 21 rooms, open since 2015, facing Las Arenas beach, late check-out until 14:00 for web bookings subject to availability.
Sabbia Valencia: Paseo de Neptuno 30; Classic interior 14 m2 (single use), Double interior 16 m2, Superior city 18 m2, Junior suite with sea views 23 m2 with jacuzzi; public parking.

The city of Pamplona says the San Fermín festival takes place between 6 and 14 July; its 2027 working calendar lists 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 13 and 14 July as San Fermín holidays. The 2027 programme was not yet published on 2026-11-04.

The 2026 bando (last year's) says every bull run starts at 8:00 barring force majeure, runs through Santo Domingo, Plaza Consistorial, Mercaderes and Estafeta, bars under-18s, limits the route to runners and authorised people from 07:15, closes route-facing bars and shops by 06:00 and doorways from 07:15, and bans objects such as rucksacks, bags and bottles.
The 2026 bando makes owners responsible for the condition of facades and balconies and says they must not be occupied by more people than is suitable.

About 12,500 people gather in Plaza Consistorial on 6 July for the Chupinazo (city); the 2026 bando closed businesses facing the square from 10:00 to 13:00 on 6 July; Hotel Pompaelo's page puts the Chupinazo at noon and sells balcony viewing for it and the Pobre de mí without stating prices.
The independent guide sanfermin.com gives the course as 875 metres, says runs usually take two to three minutes, and says spectators must stay behind the second line of fencing.
The city's tourism page says the oldest known records of festivities for Saint Fermín date back to the 12th century.
Euronews reported that a protest in 2022 was organised by PETA and AnimalNaturalis, the 18th year in a row that demonstrations had taken place ahead of San Fermín.
Spain applies 10% VAT to hospitality services (hotels included); the general VAT rate is 21%.
Our arithmetic: a €200 room price that includes 10% VAT contains €18.18 of VAT, leaving €181.82 before VAT.

No tourist tax on hotel stays was found in force in Navarra or Pamplona in November 2026. On 29 September 2026 the Pamplona council's Presidency Committee approved a declaration urging the Government of Navarra to regulate a local tourist tax and saying the council would study a tourist-ecological tax for San Fermín; no law or decree creating one was found.
Aena's Pamplona Airport page lists the car, taxi and shared taxi as ways to reach the airport, and does not list a bus; it gives no fare in the text we read.
Alsa's published timetable for Pamplona to San Sebastián shows coaches such as 09:45 to 11:00, with first departures at 06:55.
Noticias de Navarra reported on 30 June 2026 that the villavesas (Transporte Urbano Comarcal) would run 24 hours on most lines during San Fermín 2026, with changes for the fireworks and concerts.
Gran Hotel La Perla is operating on Plaza del Castillo as a five-star hotel with 44 guest rooms with balconies over Estafeta Street and the square, plus five attic rooms.
Hotel Pompaelo Plaza del Ayuntamiento & Spa is operating as a four-star boutique hotel with views over Plaza Consistorial.
Hostal Arriazu is operating on Calle Comedias 14 with 20 soundproofed rooms renovated in 2018 and a 5% direct-booking discount.
Pamplona Catedral Hotel is operating as a four-star boutique hotel in a former 19th-century nunnery beside the Portal de Francia.
Hotel Maisonnave is operating at Calle Nueva 20 and offers a 12% discount for booking on its official site.
Alda Centro Pamplona (formerly Hotel Eslava) is operating on Plaza Virgen de la O 7, with check-in from 14:00 and check-out until 12:00.
Hotel Tres Reyes Pamplona is operating next to the Taconera Gardens with an outdoor swimming pool.
Hotel Yoldi is operating at Avenida San Ignacio 11 as a three-star hotel with 50 recently renovated rooms.
Hotel Albret is operating at Calle Ermitagaña 3 with 106 exterior rooms and offers up to 20% off for stays between 5 and 14 July under a San Fermín 2027 banner.
Hotel Blanca de Navarra is operating on Avenida Pío XII and its page puts it 850 metres from the Parque de la Ciudadela.
Hotel Sancho Ramírez is operating at Sancho Ramírez 11 with private parking at €10 a night subject to availability and free cancellation until 12:00 on the day of arrival.
Hotel Pamplona Plaza is operating at Avenida Don Marcelo Celayeta 35 as a three-star hotel with free underground parking.

Sweden has no tourist tax, national or municipal, in 2026; a 2025/26 Riksdag motion (2025/26:2817, V) asks the government to investigate letting municipalities introduce local bed fees (bäddavgifter).
Swedish VAT on room rental in hotels, guesthouses and hostels is 12%, as are closely linked services such as breakfast, parking, phone, sauna and laundry; the standard rate is 25%.
From 1 April 2026 Swedish VAT on food (livsmedel) is 6%; restaurant services stay at 12%.
Konsumentverket: a private consumer should be able to count on a company quoting prices including VAT unless clearly stated otherwise.
Worked example (our arithmetic): a 2,000 SEK room includes 214.29 SEK VAT (2,000 × 12/112); four nights cost 8,000 SEK including 857.14 SEK VAT, with nothing added.

Arlanda Express one-way fares: 1 adult 340 SEK (return 640), 2 adults 460, 3 adults 580, 4 people 700; up to seven extra passengers 120 SEK each; youth 18-25 160 SEK with ID; pensioner 65+ 210 SEK; under-18s free with an adult or pensioner ticket holder; SL tickets not valid.
Arlanda Express runs non-stop to Stockholm Central Station in 18 minutes with departures every 12-15 minutes; it serves Arlanda South (Terminals 2 and 4) and Arlanda North (Terminal 5).
SL single ticket including the Arlanda passage fee: 200 SEK adult, 183 SEK discounted; passage fee alone 157 SEK for everyone over 18 with a valid SL ticket.
SL commuter trains stop at Arlanda Central Station in SkyCity between Terminals 4 and 5; the trip to Stockholm Central Station takes 38 minutes.

Vy Flygbussarna Arlanda T5/T2 to Stockholm C (Cityterminalen): adult 129 SEK, young 8-25 99 SEK, children 0-7 free (up to 4 per adult); about 40 minutes; departures every 20 minutes on the route timetable.
Our arithmetic, one way: two adults pay 460 SEK (Arlanda Express), 400 SEK (SL incl. passage fee) or 258 SEK (Flygbussarna); four adults 700 SEK vs 800 SEK on the SL commuter train.
Swedavia advises asking whether a fixed taxi price applies; all taxi companies must show a comparison price in black digits on a yellow label.

SL contactless pay-as-you-go (Visa, Mastercard, American Express; physical or digital wallets): single journey 43 SEK default fare, valid 75 minutes; no touch-out; a card pays only for its owner; physical and digital versions count as separate cards.
SL travelcards (adult): 24 hours 180 SEK, 72 hours 360 SEK, 7 days 470 SEK; the SL smart card costs 50 SEK; travelcards are valid on Djurgården ferry 82 (Slussen-Djurgården).

Lord Nelson Hotel: Västerlånggatan 22, Gamla Stan; 17th-century building just under six metres wide, called by the hotel Sweden's narrowest hotel; guests since 1974; windowless room types (Captain's Family Room, Captain's Small Double).
Hobo: Brunkebergstorg 4; 201 rooms; Standard and Superior 18-22 m²; Sleeper windowless 12 m²; breakfast almost always included when booked on the hotel website.
Grand Hôtel Stockholm: Södra Blasieholmshamnen 8; overlooks the Royal Palace and Gamla Stan; guests since 1874; five restaurants, Cadier Bar, spa with saunas and pools.
Hotel Diplomat: Strandvägen 7C; Art Nouveau; since 1911; first hotel of the family-owned Diplomat Collection.
Ett Hem: Sköldungagatan 2, Lärkstaden; private residence built 1910; interiors by Ilse Crawford.
The Rival: Mariatorget 3; privately owned; 99 rooms; theatre for 735; breakfast buffet always included.
NOFO Hotel: Tjärhovsgatan 11; family owned; 109 rooms; heritage-listed building; Tiny Double up to 14 m² with 140 cm bed; breakfast included when booking direct.
Scandic Malmen: Götgatan 49-51; newly renovated; Standard rooms 15-17 m²; cash-free.
Hotel Skeppsholmen: Gröna gången 1; two buildings from 1699; tennis court built by King Oscar II in 1882, described as Sweden's first outdoor court.
Villa Källhagen: Djurgårdsbrunnsvägen 10, by the Djurgårdsbrunn canal; reception open 24 hours; dinner Mon-Thu 17:00-21:00; bar closes 23:00.
Zurich's City Tax, collected per overnight stay by hotels and Airbnb hosts for Zürich Tourismus, is CHF 3.50 per guest per night since May 2023, up from CHF 2.50.
Zürich Tourismus is financed 65% by the City Tax; hotels in Zurich and the region collect it, under a voluntary agreement with the Zurich hoteliers' association (2023 report), and Airbnb takes part.
Swiss VAT on accommodation (overnight stay with breakfast) is the special rate of 3.8%; the normal rate is 8.1%.
Trains run from Zurich Airport to Zürich HB every 5-10 minutes between 5 am and midnight, taking 10-15 minutes; single CHF 7 (children CHF 3.50), 24-hour pass CHF 14; tram 10 takes about 35 minutes.
ZVV fares (adult, 2nd class, valid from 15 Dec 2024): 1-2 zones single CHF 4.60 (1 hour), 24h CHF 9.20; 3 zones single CHF 7.00 (1 hour), 24h CHF 14.00.
ZVV zones 110 (City of Zurich) and 120 (Winterthur) count double; Zurich Airport is zone 121, so airport-city trips are three zones.

Zürich Card: CHF 29 for 24 hours and CHF 56 for 72 hours (children CHF 19/37); includes public transport in zones 110, 111, 121, 140, 150, 154, 155 incl. airport-HB, free entry to many museums, short lake and Limmat cruises; new prices from 13 December 2026; self-financing, not subsidised by the city.

Zürich Tourismus describes District 1 (Old Town, both banks of the Limmat), District 2 (left shore: Enge station of Ticino granite, Museum Rietberg, Seebad Enge, Rote Fabrik), District 4 (Langstrasse, long regarded as a den of iniquity, now restaurants and nightlife), District 5 (Zürich-West around the Prime Tower, Viadukt, Freitag Tower) and District 8 (from behind the Opera House to Seebad Tiefenbrunnen; Chinawiese, Seebad Utoquai).
Zürich HB is the busiest and largest train station in Switzerland.
Storchen Zürich: Weinplatz 2, first mention of the house 1357, 64 rooms and suites, Limmat terrace open May-October; Old Town View Double 18 m², River View Double 18-25 m².
Hotel Adler Zürich: 3-star superior at Rosengasse 10, all rooms air-conditioned; Small Double 18 m² with 140 cm bed; Standard Double 21 m² king bed; 7 minutes' walk from the main station.

Hotel Schweizerhof Zürich: 5-star, Bahnhofplatz 7 opposite the main station, since 1877, 92 rooms and suites, triple-glazed windows, standard doubles 20-25 m², complimentary City Ticket for direct bookings.
Hotel Montana Zürich: Konradstrasse 39, 300 m / 3 minutes' walk from the main station, 74 rooms; Comfort Double Queen 18 m², 140 x 200 cm bed; Deluxe 22-26 m².
La Réserve Eden au Lac Zurich: Utoquai 45, redesigned by Philippe Starck, 40 rooms and suites, rooftop bar; Lake View Rooms with king bed, mostly south-facing; entry category Standard Courtyard Room.
Sorell Hotel Seefeld: Seefeldstrasse 63, 65 rooms; Standard Single min. 14 m², Grand Standard Double min. 24 m².

B2 Boutique Hotel Zürich: 4-star in the former Hürlimann brewery, 60 rooms and suites, library of 33,000 books, Giesshübel stop 3 minutes by train from the main station and 300 m away; Boutique Double 24-28 m² with open-plan bathroom; Hürlimannbad is a separate public spa.
Zurich Youth Hostel: Mutschellenstrasse 114, open all year, 76 rooms and 280 beds, restaurant, bar, 24-hour reception; tram 7 to Morgental.
Greulich Design & Boutique Hotel: 18 rooms (10 Design Rooms with 160 cm bed, 8 Design Double Rooms on two levels with 180 cm bed); extra bed CHF 60 a night.
25hours Hotel Zürich West: designed by Alfredo Häberli, 123 rooms and suites, heated 25 m outdoor pool open daily in summer and closed in the colder months; tram 17 to Fischerweg.

Zermatt's Kurtaxe is CHF 4.00 per night for all accommodation types (Art. 5); children 9 to 15 pay half (CHF 2.00); children under 9 and residents are exempt; the host collects it. Worked example (CHF 40 for 2 adults + a 10-year-old, 4 nights; 1.6% and 2% of an assumed CHF 500 a night room) is editorial arithmetic.
Grand Hotel Zermatterhof's FAQ says the Kurtaxe (CHF 4.00 per adult, CHF 2.00 per child 9 to 15.9) is charged in addition to the room rates.

Zermatt Bergbahnen: winter season starts 1 Nov 2026 and ends 3 May 2027; Sunnegga/Rothorn and Gornergrat areas open 28 Nov 2026; Sunnegga/Rothorn closes 11 Apr 2027 and Gornergrat 18 Apr 2027. 'Only the glacier side is open before 28 Nov' is editorial inference, labelled as such.

Winter ski pass 'from' prices (Zermatt area): half day from 12:15 CHF 68, 1 day CHF 89, 5 days CHF 329, 7 days CHF 436; Zermatt-Cervinia 1 day CHF 104, 5 days CHF 372, 7 days CHF 492. Lowest price applies 1-27 Nov 2026 and 19 Apr-2 May 2027, when Gornergrat railway is not included; other dates cost more (shown in web shop). Prices incl. 8.1% VAT. Pricing is date-dependent (dynamic-style 'from' prices).
Free ski pass for children up to 8.99; children 9-15.99 get 50% off; youths 16-19.99 get 15% off; on Saturdays the Zermatt pass is free for children under 16.
The Peak Pass (28 Oct 2026 to 30 Apr 2027, from CHF 212) covers railways, cable cars and local bus but is not valid on ski and chairlifts.

Zermatt is car-free; private vehicles only to Täsch (5 km before Zermatt); large fines for unauthorised travel; electric vehicles follow the same rules; Matterhorn Terminal Täsch has 2,100 covered spaces and private operators over 1,000.
Zermatt Tourism: Zermatt can be reached in three and a half hours from Zurich Airport and four hours from Geneva or Basel airports; trains run to Zermatt every half hour.

Täsch-Zermatt shuttle: every 20 minutes 5:55-21:55, hourly in the evening until 00:30/01:00, all night at weekends; 12 minutes; return CHF 17.20; half-fare and children 6-15.99 pay 50%; Swiss Travel Pass valid.
Zermatt Tourism lists electric taxis, horse-drawn carriages, bicycles, walking and a free e-bus on two routes (Ski-Bus and Winkelmatten).

Grand Hotel Zermatterhof: Bahnhofstrasse 55; about ten minutes' walk from the station; EV or horse carriage pickup on advance request; 14 room/suite categories 20-76 m2; winter offer: 5 nights in Deluxe Double or above gives a 4-day ski pass valid in Zermatt and Cervinia; ski passes not included in rates.
Mont Cervin Palace: Bahnhofstrasse 31, five-star, 18 room/suite categories, spa Le Club, restaurants incl. Grill Le Cervin and Ristorante Capri; location page gives no walking times.
Unique Hotel Post: Bahnhofstrasse 41; few minutes' walk from the station, lifts and bus stops; free electric-vehicle transfer 08:00-19:00; three restaurants, five bars and clubs.
Zermatt Youth Hostel: Staldenweg 5; 47 rooms, 170 beds; village centre a few minutes on foot; seasonal periods panel did not load.
Hotel National Zermatt: Matterstrasse 39; four-star; 20 metres to the Sunnegga valley station; spa.

Hotel Holiday: Gryfelblatte 4; Sunnegga underground funicular 200 m away; Gornergrat railway and Klein Matterhorn bus stop a few minutes on foot; Standard Double 20 m2, family room 28 m2; free hotel taxi on arrival/departure days.

Hotel Matterhorn Focus: Schluhmattstrasse 131; stands directly next to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise valley station; village under 10 minutes on foot; e-bus Winkelmatten line stop in front; Futura Room 30 m2 with balcony.
Hotel Jägerhof: Steinmattstrasse 85; family-run three-star; 49 rooms; Matterhorn Glacier Paradise valley station about 10 minutes on foot; Sunnegga and Gornergrat about 15; free shuttle 07:30-21:00.
Hotel Berghof: Winkelmattenweg 18; family-run four-star; 28 rooms; 600 m2 spa; Zermatt Tourism's listing says the Matterhorn Express valley station is less than two minutes' walk.

Boutique Hotel Matthiol: Moosstrasse 40; winter season 4 Dec 2026 to 11 Apr 2027; free shuttle from the station 8am-9pm; about a 20-minute walk from the station; Wichje bus stop 3 minutes; flexible winter rates cancel free up to 14 days before arrival.

CERVO Mountain Resort: Riedweg 156; open 27 Nov 2026 to 11 Apr 2027; Nomad 4*, Alpinist and Huntsman 5*; its ski-in/ski-out page says guests live directly next to the slopes; après-ski with DJ sets and live sessions.

Riffelalp Resort 2222m: winter opening 11 Dec 2026 to 4 Apr 2027; reached by Gornergrat Railway to Riffelalp station then a short walk in winter; luggage by skidoo in winter; last train up from Zermatt 23:30; no parking.

On 31 December 2026 the City of Sydney's programme runs a smoking ceremony at 7.30pm, the Calling Country fireworks at 9pm, curated by We Are Warriors, and the midnight fireworks, launched from the Harbour Bridge, the Opera House and other landmarks.
note: The City updates the event pages through November and December; recheck before 31 December. Re-checked 2026-10-26: unchanged; the schedule also lists 8.30pm pylon projections, 8.45pm Welcome to Country and 9.15pm Sydney Harbour Lights.

claim: The City of Sydney says Sydney New Year's Eve attracts more than one million people to Sydney Harbour and surrounding areas.

The City lists 48 vantage points for 2026; Lower Bradfield Park's paid tickets go on sale at 9am on 7 October, the Opera House Forecourt's free tickets at 10am on 26 December, and Clark, Goat and Shark islands, Bradleys Head and Strickland Estate were sold out by 5 October.
note: Re-checked 2026-10-26: Opera House Forecourt free tickets still from 10am 26 December.

claim: Darling Harbour is a free New Year's Eve vantage point with its own fireworks at 9pm and midnight over Cockle Bay; alcohol is prohibited there.

For New Year's Eve 2026 most free vantage points are alcohol-free zones, most don't allow re-entry, and Circular Quay Station closes from 3pm to midnight; the City suggests Wynyard, Martin Place or St James, and Victoria Cross for North Sydney.
On New Year's Eve no unauthorised vessels may enter the harbour exclusion zones from 8pm to 12:45am on New Year's Day.

On New Year's Eve 2026 access to Cockatoo Island / Wareamah is limited to guests booked to stay there; houses and apartments went to a ballot from 3 September, campground bookings opened on 22 September 2026, and on 26 October 2026 the City listed its New Year's Eve accommodation as sold out.
note: Re-checked 2026-10-26: sold out.

claim: Sydney Airport is around 20 minutes from the city centre by train, according to the City of Sydney.

YHA Sydney Harbour requires a minimum 7-night stay for all New Year's Eve 2026 bookings, and from 4pm on 31 December 2026 to 7am on 1 January 2027 its rooftop is limited to guests on its NYE package, who must be 18 or over.
On 5 October 2026 Shangri-La Sydney's New Year's Eve offer was listed from USD 1,738 a night on average, and its terms say a minimum length of stay applies.
note: The site converts prices by visitor currency; we quote the USD figure shown when we checked.

claim: Shangri-La Sydney has 565 rooms and suites over 36 levels at 176 Cumberland Street, The Rocks, with a restaurant and bar on level 36.
Four Seasons Hotel Sydney rises 34 storeys with 531 rooms and suites at 199 George Street; its full-harbour rooms look at the Harbour Bridge and the Opera House.
note: fourseasons.com refuses automated fetches; confirmed through search results from the hotel's own pages.

claim: Sofitel Sydney Darling Harbour has 590 rooms and suites at 12 Darling Drive, a minute's walk from Darling Harbour, sold as harbour, city or bay view.
Hyatt Regency Sydney, at 161 Sussex Street, opened under the Hyatt Regency brand on 1 December 2016 with 892 rooms.
The Great Southern Hotel Sydney has noisy works from 10am to 4pm between 31 August 2026 and 31 January 2027, and no on-site parking from 28 September 2026 until about 31 January 2027.
note: The hotel extended the works from 30 November 2026; corrected publicly on 5 October 2026.

claim: Since 1 October 2025 Taiwan's paper arrival card has been replaced by the online Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC), which is free and is submitted in the week before arrival.
Many Taiwanese hotels and restaurants add a 10% service charge, and tipping is not customary.
Taoyuan Airport MRT express trains from Taipei Main Station (A1) stop only at A3 and A8 before Airport Terminal 1 (A12); in-town check-in is offered at A1 and A3 for some airlines.
note: Fare (NT$160 per secondary sources) and journey time (about 35 minutes) not yet confirmed at Taoyuan Metro; not stated.

claim: Beitou's public bathhouse of 1913 is now the Beitou Hot Spring Museum (since 1998), free to enter, a short walk from Xinbeitou station.
Regent Taipei opened in 1990 and has 538 rooms and suites, about five minutes' walk from Zhongshan station, with a heated rooftop pool.
The Okura Prestige Taipei opened in August 2012 with 208 rooms on Nanjing East Road.
Palais de Chine Hotel, built in 2010 beside the Taipei bus terminal, has 286 rooms; its restaurant Le Palais holds three Michelin stars.
note: Recheck Le Palais's stars when the 2027 Taipei Michelin list is out.

claim: citizenM Taipei North Gate opened in 2017 with some 265 compact rooms opposite the North Gate, near Taipei Main Station.
note: citizenM's own site now redirects to Marriott's brand pages.

claim: Grand Hyatt Taipei opened in September 1990 beside Taipei 101 and has about 850 rooms.
W Taipei opened in 2011 with 405 rooms on the 8th to 31st floors of the building above Taipei City Hall station.
Hotel Royal Beitou, opposite Xinbeitou station, has Beitou's white-sulphur spring water, about 45 to 50°C, piped to every room.
Every room at Grand View Resort Beitou has its own hot- and cold-spring baths; children under 12 are not allowed in its public hot spring.

Thailand's cabinet approved on 27 July 2026 extending the reduced 7% VAT rate (local tax included) for a year, from 1 October 2026 to 30 September 2027; the Revenue Department's VAT guide gives the general rate as 7%.
note: KPMG reports the decree itself as Royal Decree No. 807, issued 20 August 2026; the Royal Gazette text was not opened.

claim: The Revenue Department defines the VAT tax base as the total value received or receivable from the supply of goods or services, including service fees, so VAT is charged on the room rate plus a service charge.

A Thai hotel price quoted with '++' adds a service charge (usually 10%, set by the hotel) and then 7% VAT on the room rate plus the service charge, about 17.7% in all; a room quoted at 3,000++ costs 3,531 baht a night, 10,593 for three nights. This is our arithmetic.
note: The 10% service charge is the hotel's own and not fixed by law; only a secondary source (and bangkok.json th.plus-plus) gives the usual 10%. Consider upgrading th.plus-plus with the Revenue Department source.

claim: Thailand's tourist entry fee is not in force: an earlier plan for 300 baht on air arrivals and 150 baht by land and sea was replaced by a proposal for a flat 450 baht a person for foreign visitors; air arrivals would pay from 180 days after Royal Gazette publication and land and sea about 360 days after that; as of 17 August 2026 the Ministry of Tourism and Sports was preparing a public hearing. No Gazette announcement was found by 19 October 2026.
note: Check mots.go.th / Royal Gazette before publishing; press reports say consultation ran to 28 September and early 2027 for air arrivals, but only the PRD notice was read as an official source.

claim: Airports of Thailand's international passenger service charge for departing passengers rose from 730 to 1,120 baht on 20 June 2026 and is included in the airfare; it applies at Phuket among six airports.

The Phuket Smart Bus airport line costs a flat 100 baht (Airport, Patong, Rawai), payable by contactless Visa, Mastercard or JCB, QR/PromptPay or cash; children under 6 ride free with a paying adult; there is no separate tourist fare.

Airports of Thailand lists the Smart Bus route as Airport, Bann Khian, Cherngtalay, Surin Beach, Kamala, Patong, Karon, Kata and Rawai; its airport stop is at Entrance 3, domestic terminal, floor 3, listed as closing at 11:30 pm.
The Smart Bus Bus Terminal 2 to Patong line is a flat 50 baht, and the free Dragon Line city shuttle connects Central Festival, the Old Town and the OTOP Market.

Airports of Thailand lists the orange Airport Bus route 8411 to Phuket Town: board in the public transport parking area (Exit 3, turn left), fares are calculated on the distance, tickets are sold on the bus or online (QR or cash), operating 8:00 am to 9:00 pm every day.
note: airportbusphuket.com (the operator's site) was serving unrelated gambling content when checked, so it is not cited; no fixed 8411 fare is published by AOT.

claim: Airports of Thailand lists the Phuket Airport Limousine with counters at Entrance 1 in arrivals; the page gives no fares.

The Thai Meteorological Department's advisory of 17 May 2026 forecast waves of about 2-3 metres in the upper Andaman Sea, above 3 metres in thundershowers, and told small boats in the upper Andaman Sea to stay ashore.
The Tourism Authority of Thailand says Thailand's weather has six months of rain in the wet season, three months of dry cooling breezes and three months of heat.
Laguna Phuket's own site lists Angsana Laguna Phuket, Banyan Tree Phuket, Cassia Phuket, Dusit Thani Laguna Phuket, Homm Suites Laguna and SAii Laguna Phuket among its hotels.

Kata Rocks has 34 villas with 90 rooms, all with private pools and sea views; the one-bedroom Sky Pool Villa is 175 sq m with a seven-metre infinity pool, west-facing, overlooking Kata Beach and the Andaman Sea.

Katathani Phuket Beach Resort sits on an 850-metre stretch of sand on Kata Noi Beach, has Thani, Bhuri and Vhari wings (Vhari with a new water park) and says it is less than an hour from Phuket International Airport.

Amari Phuket is at 2 Meun Ngern Road, Patong Beach, with 380 rooms; its site puts Bangla Road's nightlife close by and Jungceylon nearby, and quotes a stay-longer rate as THB 4,160+++ per room per night.

Lub d Phuket Patong, at 5/5 Sawatdirak Road, lists Patong Beach 150 m, Bangla Walking Street 500 m and Phuket Old Town 15 km away, has ladies' dorms, a co-working space and a restaurant and bar, and lists a Patong Night Run on 7 November.

Cape Sienna Phuket Gourmet Hotel & Villas has 58 Studio rooms, 40 Deluxe, 22 Jacuzzi junior suites, 22 Honeymoon suites, 2 Grand suites and 2 Executive pool penthouses (146), a 40 sq m Sea View Studio, and describes itself as on a west-coast headland on Kamala Beach; its offers page lists non-refundable rates.

Keemala has 38 pool villas (16 Clay Pool Cottages, 7 Tent Pool Villas, 7 Tree Pool Houses, 8 Bird's Nest Pool Villas), no private beach, and a complimentary shuttle to Kamala Beach from 11:00 am to 4:00 pm.

Banyan Tree Phuket has 217 villas, each with its own pool, around a lagoon on an 89-acre estate in Cherngtalay; the hotel gives the airport distance as about 16 km, 25 to 30 minutes, and mentions a dedicated beach exit to Bang Tao Beach and RAVA Beach Club.

Cassia Phuket's one-bedroom suites and lofts are 40-52 sq m with a balcony, full kitchen and separate living area, and a shuttle boat crosses the lagoon to its private area of Bang Tao Beach; it calls itself the first and only pet-friendly hotel in Phuket.

The Memory at On On Hotel, 19 Phang-Nga Road, is a Sino-Portuguese building opened in 1927 as the first hotel in Phuket Town; rooms run from Superior to the Memory Suite with free Wi-Fi and a complimentary minibar; its site lists no room sizes.
Sino House Phuket, 1 Montree Road, has 57 rooms, free parking and a spa, is described as a few minutes' walk from Phuket Old Town, and its Superior Room is 31 sq m.
note: The site shows no dated content, so operating status rests on a live Booking.com listing with a Reserve button as well as the site.

claim: The Nai Harn, 23/3 Moo 1 Vises Road, Rawai, lists a 47 sq m Deluxe Ocean View Room on floors 8-9 with daily breakfast included; its guest lift serves up to the 6th floor, with floors 7-9 a short scenic stroll; its site shows One MICHELIN Key in 2026.
SUNSURI PHUKET, 11/5 Moo 1, Rawai, is 500 m from Nai Harn Beach and its site warns of an independent external construction project nearby expected to continue through the remainder of 2027.

Airports of Thailand lists the RTC Chiang Mai City Bus at 30 baht a trip for short or long distances; the R3 Red Line stops at the airport, Wualai Road, Chiang Mai Gate, Pantip Plaza (Night Bazaar), Tha Pae Gate, Chang Phuak Gate and Nimmanhaemin, and the Yellow Line at Nimmanhaemin, Chang Phuak Gate, Three Kings Monument, Tha Pae Gate, Warorot Market and the Night Bazaar; the airport lists it from outside the terminal, 7:00 am to midnight daily.
note: AOT's closing time is stored as 00:00:59. The page itself says to verify fares and routes before travel.

claim: Airports of Thailand lists an Airport Shuttle Bus with route A1 (Nimmanhaemin Road, Huay Kaew Road, City Moat) at 40 baht, A2 (Mahidol Road, Night Bazaar, hotels in the Chang Klan Road area) at 40 baht and A3 (Second Ring Road, 700th Anniversary Stadium) at 60 baht, from the international arrivals area on floor 1, listed 7:00 am to midnight daily; it asks passengers to verify fares and routes before travel.

Airports of Thailand lists a Taxi Meter service at Entrance 1 of the main terminal (7:00 am to 11:00 pm) with an additional 50-baht gratuity collected under a Ministry of Transport announcement, and a flat-rate Airport Taxi counter at Entrance 1 (7:00 am to midnight); the pages give no fares.
Airports of Thailand lists Grab Taxi, Grab Car and Just Grab at Chiang Mai airport, which must use designated pick-up and drop-off points, with the service shown as open 24 hours.

The Pollution Control Department's Environmental and Pollution Control Office 1 (Chiang Mai) summary for 31 March 2026 gave 24-hour PM2.5 of 66.9-330.2 micrograms per cubic metre across Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Lamphun and Mae Hong Son against a 24-hour standard of 37.5, including 70.1 at Si Phum, 104.6 at Chang Phueak and 78.1 at Suthep in Mueang Chiang Mai district, and points to Air4Thai for daily northern readings.
note: A single day's reading, not a season average. Sub-district names are the PCD's (Thai); the hotel sub-districts come from each hotel's Booking.com or own address.

claim: Rachamankha, 9 Phra Singh, says its 25 rooms and suites sit in pavilions around colonnaded courtyards next to Wat Phra Singh, that the walled city has 33 functioning temples with four of notable interest within easy walking distance, that it has a 20-metre pool and a library of over 2,000 books, and that it is 8 minutes from the international airport; its site lists no room sizes.
note: Site has no dated content; operating status rests on the live Booking.com listing (rachamankha) as well.

claim: Tamarind Village, 50/1 Rajdamnoen Road, has 41 guest rooms and 5 suites around flower-filled courtyards, is 15 minutes from the airport and 10 minutes from the Night Bazaar by its own account, and accepts children aged 6 and over.
note: The site still carries an expired September 2025 pool-maintenance notice; ignore. Live Booking.com listing confirms operating.

claim: Stamps Backpackers, 1/11 Chaiyapoom Road, offers semi-private pod dorms (5-bed and 6-bed air-conditioned, 8-bed fan) with a female dorm option, a locker, outlet and reading light per bed, says it is just outside the Old City's northeast corner, an 8-minute walk from Phae Gate, runs air-conditioning from 6pm to 11am in the air-con dorms, charges 200-baht key and towel deposits, lists the Yi Peng Lantern Festival as 24-25 November 2026 and excludes festivals from its SOCIALIZE direct-booking discount.

U Nimman Chiang Mai, 1 Nimmanhaemin Road, has 147 rooms, a rooftop pool, a gym and free bikes; the Deluxe Room is 32 sq m with a balcony, and a third adult is charged an extra THB 1,000 net; its listing describes direct access to One Nimman.
note: 'Direct access to One Nimman' is from the site's structured-data description, not visible body copy.

claim: Art Mai Gallery Hotel, 21 Soi 3 Nimmanhaemin Road, is dedicated to Thai artists with art on themed floors (including Nude Art, Op Art, Pop Art and Lanna Romantic), a rooftop pool, gym, underground parking and the Jarid restaurant.
Kantary Hills Hotel, 44 Nimmanhaemin Road, Soi 12, lists studio suites of 46-54 sq m, one-bedroom suites of 61-76 sq m with a washing machine and two-bedroom suites of 103-115 sq m, and a pool.

137 Pillars House, 2 Soi 1, Nawatgate Road, is a 30-suite hotel in a restored teakwood residence built in the late 1800s as part of the Borneo Company headquarters; suites are 70-135 sq m, the Louis Leonowens Suite has a private pool, and its non-refundable direct rate must be booked at least 10 days in advance.

Anantara Chiang Mai Resort is on the banks of the Mae Ping River with 52 rooms, 34 suites and 25 serviced suites, a 50 sq m Deluxe Room with balcony or terrace, the 1921 House (formerly the British consulate), daily river cruises from its private pier, and is 15 minutes from the airport by its own account.

Dusit Princess Chiang Mai, 112 Chang Klan Road, has an outdoor pool, a gym and the Jasmine restaurant (Chinese and Cantonese); its Deluxe Room is 32 sq m, Premier 46 sq m and One Bedroom Suite 60 sq m; its Superior Room page gives 26 and 28 sq m; it quotes a dinner at THB 655++ per person and rooms as 'Start from 2,500 THB'.
note: Booking.com lists this hotel under its former name slug (royal-princess-chiang-mai); title and Chang Klan Road address match.

claim: Night Bazaar Inn, 9 Charoenprathet Road, Soi 6, is a 50-room hotel in modern Lanna style with a rooftop bar, pool, restaurant and library, 20 minutes from the international airport by its own account; its site lists no room sizes.
note: Site has no dated content; operating status rests on the live Booking.com listing as well.

claim: B2 Santitham Boutique & Budget Hotel, 43 Taeparak Road, lists four room types of 21 sq m for two, a 24-hour front desk and a car park, distances of 1.5 km to Nimmanhaemin, 3.2 km to Chiang Mai Zoo and 4.1 km to the Sunday Walking Street, and a score card on which Food & Beverage (6) is the lowest of ten category scores.
note: Address (43 Taeparak Road) matches the hotel's structured data and Booking.com; the score card is B2's own, shown as 'Rated in October 2026'.

claim: Four Seasons Resort Chiang Mai, 502 Moo 1, Mae Rim-Samoeng Old Road, has pavilions and private pool villas among rice paddies; the Pool Villa is 403 sq m for two adults; it says the resort is 30 minutes from downtown and the airport is 35 km, 30-45 minutes by car; airport transfer pricing is by concierge enquiry.

The Bank of Thailand's Notification No. 37/2569, announced 17 August 2026, lists Tuesday 13, Wednesday 14 and Thursday 15 April 2027 as Songkran Festival holidays for financial institutions; Time Out Bangkok's 2027 calendar also lists Songkran as 13-15 April.

TAT's 26 March 2026 release listed Songkran 2026 events in Bangkok including Silom Road (12-14 April, parade 14 April), Siam Square (12-15 April), ICONSIAM River Park (10-15 April), Royal City Avenue (10-15 April) and Benjakitti Park (11-15 April), and said Silom and Siam Square would again become major water celebration zones; it did not mention Khao San Road.

Thailand's 7% VAT rate is extended by Royal Decree No. 807 to 30 September 2027, per KPMG (a professional-services source, not the Revenue Department).

News reports (Nation Thailand, Pattaya Mail) say the Airport Rail Link is under a four-month interim agreement with its current operator to about the end of January 2027, with a state railway subsidiary due to take over after it; reports differ on the exact date.
Dusit Thani Bangkok is at 98 Rama IV Road, facing Lumphini Park, and its own site says it is connected to the interchange of BTS Sala Daeng and MRT Silom stations.

The Sukhothai Bangkok is at 13/3 South Sathorn Road and its site cites a 25-metre infinity-edged swimming pool amid the grounds and seven bars and dining establishments.
Pathumwan Princess Hotel is at 444 MBK Center, Phayathai Road, connected to MBK, with a skywalk to Siam and the Skytrain described as just minutes away.
Centara Grand at CentralWorld is at 999/99 Rama 1 Road, within CentralWorld, with 505 newly renovated rooms.
Bangkok Marriott Marquis Queen's Park has 1,388 guest rooms and its site says it is a step from EmSphere and BTS Phrom Phong, near Benchasiri Park.
Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Sukhumvit 11 has 160 guest rooms on Sukhumvit Soi 11, a 5-minute walk to Nana BTS, with free breakfast and a fitness centre listed.
Avani+ Riverside Bangkok Hotel has 250 rooms and suites with river views, an infinity pool and six dining outlets, at 257 Charoennakorn Road, Thonburi.
Riva Surya Bangkok has 68 rooms at 23 Phra Athit Road, on the Chao Phraya, with a riverside swimming pool.
Lamphu Tree House says it is within a 5 to 10 minute walk of Khao San Road, with a pool and a newer building a 3-5 minute walk from the main building.

Türkiye's accommodation tax (konaklama vergisi) is set at 1% until 31 December 2026 inclusive by Presidential Decision 11263, published in Official Gazette no. 33240 on 1 May 2026; GİB's guide describes it as a cut from 2% valid 1 May-31 December 2026.
The tax base is the price of the taxable services excluding VAT, it covers other services sold with the room (food and drink, pool use), and the tax must be shown separately on the invoice.

In the GİB guide's invoice examples a hotel stay carries 10% VAT charged on the price before the accommodation tax (example: 80,000 TL + 800 TL tax + 8,000 TL VAT = 88,800 TL). This is an example in the guide, not a statement of the statutory rate.

The M11 metro runs between Gayrettepe and Istanbul Airport (Gayrettepe link opened 29 January 2024; extended to Halkalı on 20 June 2026); Gayrettepe is also a station on the M2 line, whose stations include Taksim, Şişhane, Haliç and Vezneciler-İstanbul Ü.

Metro Istanbul's published tariff page lists, on 18 Oct 2026, a full fare of 46.20 TL (anonymous Istanbulkart) and a single-journey electronic ticket (bir geçişlik) at 65 TL; it does not list fares per line.
Havaist's booking page showed, on 18 Oct 2026, 470 TL from Istanbul Airport to Taksim and to Beşiktaş Meydan and 515 TL to Kadıköy, for one passenger.
Havaist's Sultanahmet line costs 8 euros and runs Çatladıkapı (Sultanahmet) - Eminönü Pier - Şişhane 6 - Türabi Baba Park - Hasköy Park - Miniatürk - Istanbul Airport (Havaist blog, 20 July 2026).
The M4 metro runs Kadıköy-Sabiha Gökçen Airport: 33.5 km, 23 stations, entirely underground; the airport section opened on 2 October 2022.

Havabus Taksim-Sabiha Gökçen costs 485 TL and takes about 1.5 hours depending on traffic (Taksim stop at the Gezi Park metro exit); Sabiha Gökçen Airport's own page confirms Havabus serves Kadıköy and Taksim.
Sirkeci Mansion's site puts Istanbul Airport 54 km away, about an hour's drive; Witt Istanbul's site says about 45 minutes by taxi from the airport, longer at rush hour.
Four Seasons Hotel Istanbul at Sultanahmet describes a neoclassical residence with a courtyard, steps from the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia, with rooms viewing courtyard, garden or streets.
Cheers Hostel: one minute from Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque; dorms of 6, 8 or 10 beds; private rooms; reservation pending until an approval email is received.

Legacy Ottoman Hotel: building designed in 1911 for offices, used as barracks by the French Allied forces 1920-1923; room types Guest, Superior, Deluxe City View, Deluxe Bosphorus; Galata Tower 10 minutes away.
Georges Hotel Galata: building from 1882, a few metres from Galata Tower; butler service; rooftop restaurant Le Fumoir; Deluxe Double rooms 22-25 m2.
Galata Antique Hotel: 19th-century Neo-Renaissance mansion by Alexandre Vallaury in Tünel, 22 rooms, roof-terrace breakfast; not suitable for disabled guests due to the stairway entrance.

Pera Palace Hotel: built from 1892, opened 1895 for Orient Express passengers; architect Alexander Vallaury; first modern hotel in Istanbul with electricity and first with an electric lift; Agatha Christie Room; Room 101 a museum to Atatürk.

Witt Istanbul Hotel (Defterdar Yokuşu 26, Cihangir): former Ogilvy & Mather headquarters reshaped into a boutique hotel in spring 2008; Autoban furniture; steep hill; Taksim Square, İstiklal and Istanbul Modern within walking distance.
Çırağan Palace Kempinski Istanbul describes itself as the only Ottoman imperial palace and luxury 5-star hotel on the Bosphorus, with 317 rooms, an outdoor infinity pool and Sanitas spa.
The Stay Nişantaşı sits on Abdi İpekçi Street above the Prada flagship store, with free access to NuSpa a 3-minute walk away; the group lists The Stay Boulevard Nişantaşı as a separate hotel.

Kuzen Otel (Caferağa, Dumlupınar Sokak 11, Kadıköy): opened 2016, 12 rooms and 20 beds; air conditioning, desk and minibar in all rooms; Kuzen Beer Cafe live music (extra charge) and meyhane; no pets.

Istanbul Life Hotel (Rıhtım Caddesi, Reşit Efendi Sokak 11, Kadıköy): orthopaedic mattresses, non-smoking rooms; says ferry piers, metro and bus stops are within fifty steps; rooms page showed no room details on 18 Oct 2026.
Türkiye's official e-Visa site is evisa.gov.tr.

Dubai's Tourism Dirham is a flat fee per occupied room per night set by hotel classification: five-star or higher AED 20, four-star AED 15, three-star AED 10, two-star AED 10, one-star or budget AED 7, hotel apartments AED 20 (luxury), 15 (deluxe), 10 (standard), guest house AED 7; it is not charged per person.
The Tourism Dirham is charged for a maximum of 30 consecutive nights and is collected from the main guest occupying the room.

Dubai Decree No. 27 of 2019 reduced the municipality fee on sales of hotel establishments from 10% to 7%; hotels' own October 2026 rate terms list a 7% municipality fee, a 10% service charge and 5% VAT per room per night. (The u.ae portal page still lists 10% municipality fees generically; the decree and the hotel terms both say 7% for Dubai.)
The UAE introduced VAT at a standard rate of 5%.
Worked example (our arithmetic, not an official figure): 4 nights at AED 15 = AED 60; 22% of AED 800 = AED 176 (7% + 10% + 5% each applied to the room rate).

On 21 May 2026 the Dubai Media Office reported a second AED 1.5 billion package including exemption from collection of the Tourism Dirham and the sales fees on hotel rooms and restaurants for establishments registered with the Department of Economy and Tourism; the 33 initiatives run for three to 12 months with timelines announced by each entity; no end date for this measure was found. Hotels' own terms in October 2026 (Millennium Airport Hotel offer valid to 31 Dec 2026; Canopy by Hilton hotel-info page) still list the Tourism Dirham.
Canopy by Hilton Dubai Al Seef's own policy page states the Tourism Dirham fee is AED 15 per room per night (AED 30 for two-room family rooms).

The Dubai Metro Red Line serves DXB Terminals 1 and 3: Mon-Thu 5am-midnight, Fri 5am-1am, Sat 5am-midnight, Sun 8am-midnight; up to two pieces of luggage including hand luggage; Red Line passes are sold at ticket offices and vending machines in Terminals 1 and 3. Burj Khalifa / Dubai Mall (R25), Airport Terminal 1 (R14) and Terminal 3 (R13) are all Red Line stations.
DXB buses operate from stands at Arrivals in Terminals 1, 2 and 3; a Nol card is required and cash is not accepted.
Dubai Taxi cars run 24/7 from designated ranks in each DXB terminal with a starting fare of AED 25 plus distance.
Al Maktoum International (DWC) page lists the F55 bus to Expo metro station and the N55 bus to Ibn Battuta bus and metro stations, each every 30 minutes; a Nol card is needed.

Nol fares: Silver card AED 3 (1 zone), AED 5 (2 adjacent zones), AED 7.50 (more than 2 zones); Red ticket AED 4, 6, 8.50; Gold card fares AED 6, 10, 15; 7 zones; children aged 5 and under free on all cards.
The Nol Silver card costs AED 25 including AED 19 initial credit; the paper Nol Red ticket costs AED 2 and can hold up to 10 single trips.
The Dubai Tram links the Dubai Metro and the Palm Monorail and runs along Al Sufouh Road and Jumeirah Beach Road; the RTA stations map lists a Jumeirah Beach Residence 1 tram stop.
Visit Dubai (Department of Economy and Tourism) states that citizens of more than 80 countries are able to get a visa on arrival in Dubai.

Australia's Smartraveller (updated 8 October 2026, still current 21 October 2026) advises exercising a high degree of caution in the UAE; airspace may open or close at short notice, affecting Abu Dhabi and Dubai International flights.

The UK Foreign Office (updated 27 October 2026, still current 4 November 2026) says the context in the Middle East remains deeply unpredictable and the risk of sudden escalation is high, and tells British nationals in or travelling through the Middle East to be prepared for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions.
Jumeirah states Jumeirah Burj Al Arab is undergoing a phased restoration programme and offers to assist with an alternative reservation at one of its other Jumeirah properties in town.

Armani Hotel Dubai occupies the concourse level through the 39th floor of Burj Khalifa with 160 guest rooms and suites designed by Giorgio Armani, steps from the Dubai Mall and Dubai Fountain; the Armani Deluxe Room is 45 sq m with City View; a separate Fountain View category exists. Vida Dubai Mall's own site describes direct access to the Dubai Mall via Chinatown and an infinity pool with Burj Khalifa views.
Rove Downtown: all rooms 26 sqm with sofa bed and mini-fridge (Rover Room, Rover Room Burj View, Gamer Cave); outdoor saltwater pool; less than 10 minutes' walk from The Dubai Mall.
XVA Art Hotel: in the former home of the Seddiqi family in the Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, opened 2003, 15 rooms around three shaded courtyards; Standard Room 13-15 m2.

Canopy by Hilton Dubai Al Seef: 198 rooms, rooftop pool, spa, riverside lounge; Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood 1.50 km; stay from AED 273 per night for 21-22 October 2026; breakfast available for a fee.

Arabian Courtyard Hotel & Spa: 4-star, opposite Dubai Museum on Al Fahidi Street, Bur Dubai; Sharaf DG metro station and Al Ghubaiba metro and bus stations are 500 metres' walk (hotel's own statement); Deluxe Museum View room type.
Jumeirah Beach Hotel, Jumeirah Road, Umm Suqeim 3: designed for families, private beach and pools, Jumeirah Circle kids club, views from every room over Jumeirah Burj Al Arab and the Gulf.
Rove La Mer Beach at J1 Beach, Jumeirah; max occupancy 2 adults + 1 child (4-16); Downtown Dubai, Dubai Mall and City Walk 15 minutes away (hotel's statement).
JA Ocean View Hotel on The Walk at JBR: 346 rooms and suites with sea views, infinity pool, five-star; private balcony listed for Superior Sea View room.
Rove Dubai Marina: 26 sqm Rover Room, outdoor pool, bikes for a small fee, JBR beach, Dubai Marina Mall and Dubai Tram ten minutes away on foot; max 2 adults + 1 child.

Atlantis, The Palm: King and Queen Rooms 45-47 sqm; every Deluxe Room includes unlimited Aquaventure World and Lost World Aquarium access, one daily Atlantis Explorers Club session, beach and pools; FAQ: taxi from Dubai International about 40-60 minutes and about AED 120; up to 35% off stays advertised on the hotel's home page on 21 October 2026.
Sofitel Dubai The Palm: East Crescent, private beach, six pools, 12 restaurants and bars, family apartments with fully equipped kitchens, day passes sold to pools and beach.

Vida Dubai Mall's own page describes modern rooms and suites with views of Burj Khalifa and direct access to Dubai Mall via Chinatown.

UK VAT on hotel accommodation is charged at the standard rate of 20% (the temporary 5% and 12.5% hospitality rates ended on 31 March 2022); for stays of more than 28 consecutive days in a hotel, the reduced value rule relieves the accommodation element from VAT after the 28th day.

claim: The City of Las Vegas states a combined transient lodging (room) tax of 13.38% for properties inside the Primary Gaming Corridor and 13% for properties outside it (schedule effective 1 March 2017, guide revised March 2026); the same totals apply to hotels of 75 or more rooms and to smaller ones.

The stadium share of the room tax is 0.88% inside the Primary Gaming Corridor and 0.5% outside it; the other components (LVCVA 6.12%, Nevada Department of Taxation 0.38%, City 1%, Clark County transportation 1% and education 1%, State 3%, for hotels of 75 or more rooms) are the same in both, giving 13.38% versus 13%.

The City's guide says a property close to the Strip may be in the Primary Gaming Corridor (13.38%) and that room tax should be collected from the guest and shown as a separate charge, not included in the room price.

The FTC's Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees (16 CFR Part 464), effective 12 May 2025, covers short-term lodging including hotels; its FAQ uses a mandatory resort fee as an example that must be included in the total price, displayed more prominently than other pricing information, while taxes and other government charges may be excluded from the upfront total.

The Venetian's resort fee page states a daily Resort Fee of $55 plus tax per night, payable at check-in, including fitness access for two at Canyon Ranch, in-suite internet, boarding-pass printing, local and toll-free calls and PressReader.

Wynn Las Vegas states a daily resort fee of $55 plus tax, including self-parking for up to two vehicles, Wi-Fi, bottled water, calls and fitness access for up to two people; it says smoking is allowed on the casino floor, patios, pool areas and designated hotel floors.

SAHARA Las Vegas states a $54.95 daily resort fee plus 13.38% Clark County tax, including free valet and self-parking, in-room Wi-Fi, fitness and in-season pool access, two bottles of water and local and toll-free calls; it has an official monorail station; check-in is 4:00 p.m.

Plaza Hotel & Casino states a mandatory resort fee of $39.00 per room per day, taxable by 13%, including covered parking, early check-in subject to availability, baggage storage, local/800 calls, fitness centre, bottled water and boarding-pass printing; average room size is 325 sq ft; it is at 1 Main Street at the beginning of the Fremont Street Experience.

Alexis Park All Suite Resort's FAQ states a mandatory resort fee of $37.42 per night and a lodging tax of 13.38%; it describes itself as the largest off-Strip, non-gaming resort in Las Vegas, runs no shuttle to the airport or Strip, and offers complimentary parking.

Our arithmetic: a $150 room with a $55 daily fee and 13.38% tax on both costs $232.43 a night ($82.43, or 55%, above the room rate; $697.29 for three nights); on the Plaza's terms ($39 fee, 13% tax) it is $213.57. This assumes the tax applies to room and fee, as the Plaza states for its fee.

Harry Reid International Airport says taxis are regulated by the Nevada Taxicab Authority and run flat-rate zone fares to the Strip; the Authority lists $22.25 (Zone 1, Sunset north to Tropicana), $26.25 (Zone 2, Tropicana north to Flamingo) and $30.25 (Zone 3, Flamingo north to Stratosphere), a $3 credit/debit card fee, and a 3% excise tax added to all rates and fees (page footer: last updated 04 Sep 2026).

Rideshare pickup at Harry Reid is on Level 2 of the parking garage at Terminal 1 and the Valet Level of the garage at Terminal 3; the airport warns of lane closures in the connector tunnels through December 2026.
The airport's public bus page lists Route 108 (Paradise) and the Red Line (formerly Route 109, Maryland Parkway) at Terminal 1, Level Zero.

RTC's mobile fare page lists the Strip/Downtown services (SDX and Deuce) at $6 for 2 hours, $8 for 24 hours and $20 for 3 days, and residential routes at $2 a single ride, $3 for 2 hours and $5 for 24 hours.
The Las Vegas Monorail lists a single ride at $6.25 full fare and $5.75 as an eTicket, and a 1-day pass at $15.50 full fare and $13.95 as an eTicket; seven stations run from MGM Grand to SAHARA.

Bellagio lists Fountain View King and other rooms of 510 sq ft, overlooks a lake with fountains, hosts "O" by Cirque du Soleil, and states rooms are non-smoking except certain accommodations on the 19th floor of the Bellagio Tower, with designated smoking areas in the casino.
The Venetian's suite page lists a Luxury King Suite of 650 sq ft with a living room, and the Palazzo's Luxury King Suite at 720 sq ft.
The Cosmopolitan lists a City Room Queen of 460 sq ft and Terrace Studio rooms of 730 sq ft with private terraces.

W Las Vegas lists all-suite accommodation with 725 sq ft Premier King and Premier Two Queen Suites, access to the BATHHOUSE Spa, WET Deck and Mandalay Bay venues, and states its suites do not include pullout couch beds.
Luxor lists Pyramid rooms of 420 sq ft with slanted windows and Tower rooms such as the Tower Premier King at 449 sq ft.

Circus Circus's pages list Hotel, West Tower and Suite rooms, the Adventuredome's indoor rides under the pink dome, "Free Parking Always" and a "No Resort Fee Room Special", with no standard resort fee amount stated.

Circa's guest guide states it is a 21+ property including hotel guests, at 8 Fremont Street, with two complimentary Stadium Swim passes per room per night, self-parking at $25.00 a day and valet at $20.00 a day.
Red Rock Casino Resort Spa (11011 W Charleston) lists a 515 sq ft Luxury King with a choice of Strip or Red Rock Canyon views; its booking offer states guests must be 21 or older.
San Francisco imposes a 14% transient occupancy tax (the hotel tax) on the rental of accommodations for stays of less than 30 days.

The Tourism Improvement District (TID) assessment is 2.25% of gross room revenue in Zone 1 and 2.00% in Zone 2; the Treasurer says these assessments may be passed on to customers as a separate item on hotel folios.

The Moscone Expansion District (MED) assessment is 1.25% of gross room revenue in Zone 1 and 0.3125% in Zone 2; the Treasurer's 2013 notice says neither the TID nor the MED assessment may be included in the Transient Occupancy Tax billed to the guest.
note: MED rates read from the 2023 annual statement form and the 2013 notice; the Treasurer's current TOT page names the MED but lists no MED rate. Editor: soften if you want a 2026 rate source.

The 2022 TID plan's list of assessed hotels shows The Clift Royal Sonesta Hotel, Hotel Zeppelin, Fairmont San Francisco, Stanford Court Hotel, Hotel Zephyr, Hotel Boheme, Palace Hotel, Hotel Zetta and The Mosser Hotel in Zone 1; the Inn at the Presidio, Lodge at the Presidio and HI Fisherman's Wharf hostel were not found in the list.

Daily fees on each hotel's own site: The Clift $39 destination fee inclusive of tax; Hotel Zeppelin, Hotel Zetta and Hotel Zephyr $35 plus tax a room a night; Stanford Court $38 plus tax a night, subject to San Francisco occupancy tax; The Mosser's homepage says no amenity fees.
