claim: Room facts from the hotels: Stanford Court Standard rooms are interior-facing, about 205-220 sq ft; the Fairmont's Moderate rooms (Main Building, interior views, one Double bed) are 'best suited for single occupancy'; the Palace's rooms start at 300 sq ft with 11-foot ceilings; The Mosser lists a Shared Bathroom Queen room type.
Fairmont San Francisco, 950 Mason Street, Nob Hill: 606 guestrooms and suites in the historic Main Building and the Tower; Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar; afternoon tea in Laurel Court since 1907.

Palace Hotel, 2 New Montgomery Street: first opened in 1875 and reopened in 1909; Garden Court, Pied Piper bar and a heated indoor pool; the hotel describes itself as near the Financial District, Union Square and the Moscone Center.

Hotel Zetta, 55 Fifth Street: 5-minute walk to SFMOMA and Yerba Buena Gardens, 7 minutes to the Moscone Center and to Union Square; Powell Street BART and Muni station 2 minutes' walk; $100 refundable incidental hold per night.

Presidio Lodging: the Inn at the Presidio has 22 rooms, mostly suites with fireplaces, in a Georgian Revival former officers' quarters; the Lodge at the Presidio is in the Montgomery Street Barracks built 1895-1897 on the Main Post; both include breakfast and wine and cheese; reservations cancelled within 72 hours of arrival are charged the first night; the FAQ points guests to the Presidio Transit Center, Muni and the Presidio GO Shuttle.

Florida applies its 6% state sales tax to transient rentals (accommodation rentals of six months or less); local option transient rental taxes are in addition to the 6% state sales tax and any discretionary sales surtax, and the surtax applies to transient rentals in a surtax county.

Orange County's discretionary sales surtax is 0.5% (school capital outlay surtax, extended effective 1 January 2026 through 31 December 2035); the DOR table lists no 2026 rate change for Orange. Source form is the calendar-2025 edition (R. 11/24), the latest the DOR serves at its 'current' URL.

Osceola County's discretionary sales surtax is 1.5% in total (1% from 1 September 1990 to 31 December 2045 and 0.5% from 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2036); the DOR table lists no 2026 rate change for Osceola.
Orange County's Tourist Development Tax is 6% of the lodging bill, on hotel stays and short-term rentals of less than six months, collected by the county.
Osceola County's Tourist Development Tax is 6% (since 1 July 2004), applied to short-term rentals of less than 180 days.
Our arithmetic: 6% state sales tax + 0.5% surtax + 6% Tourist Development Tax = 12.5% in Orange County; 6% + 1.5% + 6% = 13.5% in Osceola County. On a $200 room: $225 (Orange) and $227 (Osceola).

Kissimmee is the seat of Osceola County; Winter Park is in Orange County, three miles north of Orlando; Orlando is listed among Orange County's cities; the Central Florida Tourism Oversight District covers about 25,000 acres in Orange and Osceola counties.

The FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees (16 CFR Part 464), effective 12 May 2025, covers short-term lodging; a mandatory resort fee must be included in the total price, while taxes and other government charges may be excluded from the upfront total.

MCO's ground-transportation page lists approximate rates: to the Disney resorts area local bus $4, shuttle van $23/$37, taxi $52-$68; Lake Buena Vista $2 / $23/$37 / $47-$55; International Drive $2 / $21/$33 / $38-$45; Kissimmee hotels $2 / $29/$49 / $45-$75; Downtown Orlando $2 / $20/$32 / $38-$45; Winter Park/Maitland $2 / $29/$49 / $45-$55. The shuttle-van page says fares are per person and to check with the attendant for round-trip fares. The second van figure is unlabelled on the page.

LYNX buses serve MCO from Terminal A, Level 1 (Commercial Lane spaces A38-A41); the airport lists $2.00 per destination or $4.50 all day, and LYNX lists a $2.00 single ride and a $4.50 all-day pass, requested from the operator when boarding.

Ride-share pick-up at MCO is at the Arrivals curbs: Level 2 at Terminals A and B (24 hours a day) and Level 6 at Terminal C; taxis are metered, flat rates are not authorised, and metered fares may vary from the airport's approximate rates.

A Brightline station at MCO operates daily 5am-11pm, with trains to Orlando, West Palm Beach, Boca Raton, Fort Lauderdale, Aventura and Miami; the airport also lists on-airport and off-airport rental car companies with free shuttle buses to off-airport locations.

Disney says guests at Disney Resort hotels and select other hotels can enter Walt Disney World theme parks 30 minutes early every day of their stay including check-in and check-out days, with valid admission; the benefit continues through 2027; the list includes Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa, Disney's Pop Century Resort and Drury Plaza Hotel Orlando Lake Buena Vista.

Universal says guests of its hotels can enter a theme park up to an hour before opening with Early Park Admission (valid admission, select attractions); Loews Portofino Bay Hotel, Hard Rock Hotel and Loews Royal Pacific Resort get free Universal Express Unlimited; hotels offer complimentary shuttle buses, with water taxis and walking paths at select hotels; Cabana Bay is listed among Value Inns and Suites.

Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa: Deluxe Resort at 4401 Floridian Way, Lake Buena Vista; Victorian-style; complimentary Resort Monorail one stop to Magic Kingdom; Beach Pool with waterslide; spa; Seven Seas Lagoon; page notice that the resort is undergoing refurbishments.

Disney's Pop Century Resort: Value Resort at 1050 Century Drive, Lake Buena Vista; fads of the 1950s through 1990s; Hippy Dippy Pool; Skyliner gondola to EPCOT and Disney's Hollywood Studios; page notice of construction and refurbishment.

Drury Plaza Hotel Orlando - Disney Springs Area: 2000 Hotel Plaza Boulevard; an official Walt Disney World hotel by its own description; half a mile from Disney Springs; free shuttle to all four WDW theme parks; free hot breakfast; free 5:30 Kickback; saltwater pool; no resort fee; parking $28 per night.
Loews Portofino Bay Hotel: replica of an Italian seaside village, three pools, water taxis to the parks; named by Universal for free Universal Express Unlimited.
Universal Cabana Bay Beach Resort: retro style inspired by classic Florida beach resorts of the 1950s and 60s; two pools, a winding river, a bowling alley (fees apply), food court.

Rosen Centre Hotel: 9840 International Drive; 1,254 deluxe guest rooms and 80 suites; connected to the Orange County Convention Center; complimentary Universal Orlando shuttle (sign up at concierge); no resort fee; self-parking $40 plus tax; Universal Orlando 10 minutes (3.5 miles), Walt Disney World 14 minutes (6 miles).

Rosen Inn at Pointe Orlando: across International Drive from Pointe Orlando, 20-minute walk or short drive from the Orange County Convention Center and ICON Park; official Universal Partner Hotel with free scheduled shuttle to Universal Orlando Resort and SeaWorld Orlando; paid Disney transport; no resort fees; three pools.

Gaylord Palms Resort & Convention Center: 6000 West Osceola Parkway, Kissimmee; 4.5-acre garden atrium; Cypress Springs Water Park with seven waterslides; full-service spa; self-parking $40 per day, valet $55 per day; no resort fee amount on the Marriott page.

Margaritaville Resort Orlando's FAQ states a taxable resort fee of $48 plus tax per room, per night; self-parking $20 plus tax per vehicle per night; check-in age 21; no direct airport shuttle; complimentary theme-park shuttles (reservations required); 265 guest rooms and suites at 8000 Fins Up Circle, Kissimmee; 10 to 15 minutes from Walt Disney World and 20 to 25 minutes from SeaWorld and Universal.

The Alfond Inn: 300 East New England Avenue, Winter Park; opened in 2013; Alfond Collection of Contemporary Art (Rollins College) installed throughout; Classic King 323 sq ft, Classic Queen (two queens) 358 sq ft; resort pool; complimentary house cars around Winter Park daily 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM, first-come, up to four guests.

Hotel Beauden, Autograph Collection: 325 South Orange Avenue, Orlando; steps from the Dr. Phillips Center and Kia Center; Altira Pool + Lounge; nightly Steinway grand piano performances in the Garden Rotunda; Marriott's page title still reads Grand Bohemian Hotel Orlando while the page body says Hotel Beauden; valet parking $42 per day.

Aloft Orlando Downtown: 500 South Orange Avenue; steps from City Hall, Dr. Phillips Center, the Kia Center; outdoor pool; W XYZ bar with live music; 24/7 pantry; valet parking $30 per day (no self-parking listed).
From 1 May 2025 the City of San Diego transient occupancy tax is 11.75% in Tax Zone 1, 12.75% in Tax Zone 2 and 13.75% in Tax Zone 3, applied to stays of less than one month.
The Tourism Marketing District assessment is 2.00% for lodging businesses in San Diego with 70 or more rooms, and the operator may elect to pass it on to the guest.

The Municipal Code defines Tax Zone 3 as a contiguous downtown area, Tax Zone 1 as two noncontiguous parts of the city north of State Route 56 and south of State Route 54, and Tax Zone 2 as the rest; the city's zone lookup map shows each address, and the city's release says rates are higher closer to the Convention Center.
Our arithmetic: on a $300 room, 13.75% is $41.25 and 2% is $6.00 (total $347.25); at 12.75% plus 2% the total is $344.25.

The Hotel del Coronado's own reservation policies list current room taxes and assessments at 11% (subject to change); Coronado is a separate city from San Diego. Our arithmetic: 11% of a $300 room is $33.

MTS Route 992 serves both airport terminals' elevated platforms and Downtown, every 15 minutes from 4:30 a.m. to 1 a.m. daily, about 15 minutes to Santa Fe Depot; MTS gives the fare as $3.00 and contactless tap payment is accepted on the validator.
The San Diego Flyer is a free shuttle between the airport terminals and Old Town Transit Center, 4:45 a.m. to 12:30 a.m., every 20 to 30 minutes, for transit riders only.
The trolley does not stop at the airport; the airport's page routes riders by Route 992 to Santa Fe Depot (Blue and Green Lines) or Courthouse Station (Orange Line).

MTS adult fare is $3 one way on trolley, bus and Rapid, $1.50 reduced fare; PRONTO includes two-hour transfers and fare capping up to the $7 day pass, cash is a single ride with no transfers, and riders 18 and under ride free with a Youth PRONTO account.

The Blue Line runs San Ysidro to UTC via Old Town, County Center / Little Italy, Santa Fe Depot and America Plaza; the Green Line stops at Seaport Village, Convention Center, Gaslamp Quarter, Santa Fe Depot and Old Town, and continues to Mission Valley.

Pendry San Diego is at 550 J Street, Gaslamp Quarter, with a rooftop pool, six dining destinations, Petco Park 0.2 miles away, valet parking $70 a night including tax, and a nightly amenity fee (amount not stated on the FAQ).
Hotel Republic San Diego, Autograph Collection is at 421 West B Street; self and valet parking are each $70 a day and there is no airport shuttle.
Porto Vista Hotel is at 1835 Columbia Street, with valet-only parking at $55 a night for a standard vehicle.

Hacienda Hotel Old Town lists a complimentary shuttle to the airport, Old Town Transit station and the cruise terminal from 6:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. (pick-ups need a call 45 minutes ahead), and parking at $30 a night.
Paradise Point charges a Resort Amenities Fee of $46 per room per night, included in the guestroom rate, and parking of $49 a night.
Tower23 Hotel's valet parking is $35 a night.
La Valencia's nightly resort fee is $39 plus taxes; the hotel first opened on 15 December 1926; room sizes run from 250 sq ft (Vintage) to 800 sq ft (Icon Suites).

The Hotel del Coronado adds a mandatory $50 per room per night ($35 resort charge plus $15 Historic Preservation Fund charge); self-parking is $59 and valet $79 a night; it is at 1500 Orange Avenue, about 15 minutes from the airport, reached by bridge or ferry, with no airport shuttle.

Glorietta Bay Inn's resort fee is $40 a night; it stands across from the Hotel del Coronado in the former Spreckels Mansion and offers a complimentary hot breakfast and heated pool; second-floor rooms are reached by stairs.

Florida levies a 6% tax on the total rental charged for hotel and similar accommodation (s. 212.03, 2026 statutes); the Department of Revenue says discretionary sales surtax applies to transient rentals and that the $5,000 surtax cap does not apply to them.
Miami-Dade County's total discretionary sales surtax is 1% for calendar year 2026 (DR-15DSS).

Miami-Dade County says transient rentals carry 6% in total beyond state sales tax: 3% Convention Development Tax (county-wide except Surfside and Bal Harbour), 2% Tourist Development Tax and 1% Professional Sports Facilities Franchise Tax (both county-wide except Surfside, Bal Harbour and Miami Beach).

The City of Miami Beach levies a 4% resort tax on the rent of a room in any hotel, motel, rooming house or apartment house (and 2% on food and drink); Miami-Dade County lists the same 4% on top of the 3% Convention Development Tax for Miami Beach facilities.

Our arithmetic from the official rates: Miami Beach 6% + 1% + 3% + 4% = 14%; mainland Miami (Brickell, Wynwood, Coconut Grove, Coral Gables) 6% + 1% + 3% + 2% + 1% = 13%. Faena and Freehand each state 14% tax on their resort fees and EAST Miami quotes 13% tax on its rollaway-bed fee.

claim: Our arithmetic: a $300 room plus a $60 daily fee, with both taxed (as Faena and Freehand state for their fees), is $410.40 a night at 14% (Miami Beach) and $406.80 at 13% (mainland), i.e. $110.40 and $106.80 above the room rate.
Miami-Dade Transit's fare page lists Metrorail and Metrobus at $2.25 full fare, a 1-day pass at $5.65, free Metromover, and free bus-to-rail and rail-to-bus transfers.

Miami-Dade County: Metrorail operates 5 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week, payable by contactless card at the gate; on weekends Orange Line trains run only as an airport shuttle between Earlington Heights and MIA, and riders from further north change at Earlington Heights. The airport lists the Orange Line for Brickell, Government Center, Historic Overtown/Lyric Theatre and Coconut Grove.

The airport's public transportation page lists a Miami Beach bus every 30 minutes from 6 a.m. to 11:40 p.m. between the MIA Metrorail station and Miami Beach (41st Street to South Pointe Drive) for $2.25 each way, and lists Route 150 Miami Beach Airport Express among routes serving the airport. (Freehand's FAQ quotes $2.35 and 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.)
The airport lists metered taxi fares from MIA with a $2.00 airport origination fee and a $15 minimum fare; taxis are on the arrivals (ground) level.

Broward County's FLL page: free shuttle buses run from the terminals to the Tri-Rail station at Dania Beach (Tri-Rail serves Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties), and Broward County Transit Route 1 stops at the Rental Car Center.

Brightline's airport shuttle costs $12 per guest plus a $3 fuel surcharge with a same-day Brightline ticket, runs about twice an hour from MiamiCentral and the Fort Lauderdale station, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily, to MIA and FLL respectively.

Brightline runs between Miami and Orlando with stops in Aventura, Fort Lauderdale, Boca Raton and West Palm Beach; MiamiCentral is at 600 NW 1st Avenue, and the county names Metrorail's Historic Overtown/Lyric Theatre station as the Brightline transfer.

Miami-Dade County: Metromover is a free elevated people mover, seven days a week, in downtown, Omni and Brickell (21 stations, incl. the Kaseya Center); the Financial District station was to close temporarily for five weeks from Saturday 24 October, with the Brickell Loop continuing from the Brickell station.

The City of Miami Beach's citywide free trolley: South Beach loops run 7 days, 8 a.m. to 11 p.m., about every 20 minutes (reaching Lincoln Road Mall, the Bass Museum and the New World Symphony); the Middle Beach Loop runs 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. at about 20 minutes.

Wynwood Walls (2516 NW 2nd Ave): adults $12, youth 13 to 17 $5, seniors $10, children 12 and under free; open 10:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.; no Metrorail station in Wynwood, nearest Historic Overtown/Lyric Theatre and Culmer about 1.5 miles south; Metrobus Route 2 and the free City of Miami trolley (Mon-Sat) on NW 2nd Ave.
The Miami Design Preservation League's daily Art Deco Walking Tour from 1001 Ocean Drive lasts about two hours over roughly 1.5 miles; adults $50, seniors $40, youths $35, children free.

The City of Coral Gables says the Venetian Pool, 2701 De Soto Boulevard, has been enjoyed since 1923, is fed by spring water from an underground aquifer, and is closed on Mondays (open Tuesday to Sunday).
Vizcaya Museum and Gardens says on-site restoration is under way and it has reduced adult admission from $32 to $20 while it continues.

The Betsy (1440 Ocean Drive): two pools, direct beach access, nightly live jazz at the Piano Bar; Classic King 250 to 275 sq ft; resort fee $62 plus tax per room per night; check-in age 21; describes itself as on the quiet end of Ocean Drive.

National Hotel (1677 Collins Avenue): adults-only, check-in age 21; 137 rooms and suites; calls its infinity pool the longest infinity-edge pool in Miami Beach; Classic rooms 250 to 300 sq ft; a daily resort fee applies, amount not stated.

Catalina Hotel & Beach Club (1732 Collins Avenue): across the street from a public beach, two pools, three bars, complimentary beach towels; mandatory resort fee $30 plus tax; check-in age 21; third-party valet $40 a day plus taxes.
Faena Hotel Miami Beach (3201 Collins Avenue): Bay View Room 489 to 615 sq ft, Premier Oceanfront Room 727 sq ft; resort fee $65 plus 14% tax; overnight valet $68++ per vehicle.

Freehand Miami (2727 Indian Creek Drive): five-minute walk from the beach, under a mile from South Beach nightlife, pool terrace and two craft cocktail bars; rooms by Roman and Williams; Standard Family Room 240 sq ft; resort fee $35 plus 14% tax; no private car park; $100 refundable deposit; no longer books by the bed.

Four Seasons Hotel Miami (1435 Brickell Avenue): describes a two-acre rooftop deck, the city's largest, with pool, cabanas and hammocks; Cityscape Room 500 sq ft; valet $65 a day, self-parking $60; MIA 8 miles/20 minutes and FLL 45 minutes by car per the hotel; no resort fee amount stated.

EAST Miami (Brickell City Centre neighbourhood): four outdoor pools; Urban King 300 sq ft with private balcony; destination fee $54 plus tax per night; check-in age 21; $250 per night security deposit.

Eurostars Langford (121 SE 1st St): 126 rooms in a 1925 Beaux Arts building that once housed the Miami National Bank; Deluxe room 26 m2; rooftop temporarily closed; external parking USD 64.2 per night taxes included.

Arlo Wynwood (2217 NW Miami Court): rooftop pool and bar, 24-hour fitness centre, complimentary bikes; MIA 7.2 miles (15 to 20 minutes) and FLL 30 to 45 minutes by car per the hotel; urban fee $35 plus tax per room per night; valet only from $45 a night; minimum check-in age 21; does not accept tap-to-pay wallets.

Mr. C Miami Coconut Grove (2988 McFarlane Road): rooftop pool, Bellini restaurant, Superior King 304 sq ft; no house car or shuttle; valet-only parking, overnight $55; nightly amenity fee $28 inclusive of tax.

Biltmore Hotel (1200 Anastasia Avenue): pool of about 23,000 sq ft, one of the largest hotel pools in the continental US; 10,000 sq ft gym; resort fee $23 per room per day; MIA about 18 minutes and 3.7 miles by car; Miracle Mile 1.5 miles.

Hotel Colonnade (180 Aragon Avenue, Miracle Mile): Colonnade Room 309 sq ft; outdoor pool; a daily destination fee applies (amount not stated on the pages read) including a $15 food and beverage credit; overnight valet $46 plus tax.

DC's Office of Tax and Revenue lists the sales and use tax rate on rooms, lodgings or accommodations as 15.95%, and 18% on parking or storing motor vehicles; the rate rose from 14.95% to 15.95% on April 1, 2023, and OTR's October 2025 notice extends the 15.95% rate through September 30, 2027.
Our arithmetic: 15.95% of a $300 room rate is $47.85, making $347.85 a night; no separate per-night city charge appears on the OTR pages we read.

The Smithsonian states free admission at all locations except Cooper Hewitt in New York City; the National Museum of African American History and Culture, the National Air and Space Museum in DC and the National Zoo require free passes or tickets, and other locations do not use passes for general admission.

The 2027 Masters is played at Augusta National from Monday 5 to Sunday 11 April 2027, with Monday to Wednesday as practice rounds and tournament rounds from Thursday 8 April.
On the Monday practice round, patron parking opens no earlier than 6:00 a.m., ticketing gates open at 7:00 a.m., the course opens at 7:30 a.m. and gates close at 6:00 p.m.
All 2027 Masters tickets have been allocated, Augusta National is the only authorised seller and resale is prohibited; 2028 applications are listed as open 1 to 20 June 2027.
Augusta National directs hotel enquiries to the Augusta Convention and Visitors Bureau (706-823-6600) and private home reservations to the Masters Housing Bureau (706-821-1300).
Free Masters parking is first-come, first-served along Berckmans Road between the North and South Gates, with more than 8,500 spaces; lots fill quickly and close at capacity.
Other parking along corridors such as Washington Road typically costs $40-60 and does not accept cards, per Destination Augusta.
The rideshare lot is at 2800 Washington Road and the taxi lot at 2740 Washington Road, both within a short walk of the North Gate.

Augusta National names Augusta Regional Airport as closest, and says Delta will run up to 20 direct flights daily to Augusta during the 2027 tournament; Destination Augusta lists daily Delta and American flights.
Destination Augusta says Masters week brings increased demand for lodging, dining and transportation, making advance planning essential.
Georgia innkeepers must collect a $5.00 per night state hotel-motel fee from guests; marketplaces collect it for short-term rentals booked through them.
Georgia DOR's general rate chart effective 1 October 2026 lists Richmond County at 9% and Columbia County at 8%, with the 4% state rate included.

Courtyard by Marriott Augusta, 1045 Stevens Creek Road, lists complimentary on-site parking and The Bistro with Starbucks coffee; pets are charged $20 a day.
Red Roof Inn Augusta - Washington Road, 3030 Washington Rd Building A, lists a $50 refundable deposit per room and one pet staying free.
Augusta Marriott at the Convention Center, Two Tenth Street, lists Augustino's restaurant, indoor and outdoor pools, valet parking at $25 a day and a garage clearance of 8 feet 6 inches.
The Partridge Inn Augusta, 2110 Walton Way, describes itself as a registered historic hotel with 143 guest rooms in Hilton's Curio Collection.
Hampton Inn & Suites Augusta West, 4081 Jimmie Dyess Parkway, is off I-20 exit 194, lists complimentary self-parking and Augusta Regional Airport 13 miles away, with no airport shuttle.
Holiday Inn Express & Suites Augusta West - Fort Gordon, 4087 Jimmie Dyess Parkway, is right off I-20 exit 194 and 3 miles from Fort Gordon Gate #1, with free breakfast and a pool.
DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Augusta, 2651 Perimeter Parkway, lists indoor and outdoor pools, complimentary self-parking, breakfast for a fee and no airport shuttle.
Crowne Plaza North Augusta, 1060 Center Street, lists parking at $12 a day and a complimentary shuttle seven days a week, 7am to 10pm, within about five miles and based on availability.
Holiday Inn Express North Augusta - SC, 138 Stephens Farm Lane, is immediately off I-20 at Exit 5 and lists free breakfast.
The Willcox, 100 Colleton Avenue SW, Aiken, says each stay includes a complimentary breakfast.
Holiday Inn Express & Suites Aiken, 2897 Whiskey Road, lists free breakfast, pets at $50 a night and a page heading inviting guests to stay during the Masters Tournament.

Alexis Park's home page says it is the largest off-Strip, non-gaming resort in Las Vegas and three minutes from the Strip, with Parlor, Monarch and LOFT Suites.

Viator (US/Canada residents product) 1-day park-to-park $230.53 and 2-day $364.22 for 9 Dec 2026, price includes 6.5% Florida sales tax; free cancellation before 8 Dec for the 1-day option.

Bryant Park's Bank of America Winter Village: the free-admission Rink runs 28 October 2026 to 28 February 2027 and the Holiday Shops 28 October 2026 to 3 January 2027.

claim: YOTEL New York Times Square is at 570 Tenth Avenue, with Solo rooms of 10.6 sq m and a 15 to 20 minute walk to Times Square by its own FAQ.
Empire State Building tickets bought on its own site are non-refundable, but the reservation can be changed through Manage My Booking.
The 102nd floor deck is enclosed (1,250 ft); the 86th floor deck is open-air (1,050 ft); the 102nd is reached by glass elevator from the 86th.
All visits require a timed reservation; a Flex ticket lets you choose a date and arrive any time that day.

The building may ask for proof of identity (passport, driver's licence or credit card) and bans large bags and tripods; there are no lockers.

Express access to Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift is not included in Universal Express, Universal Express Unlimited or the Express Add-On; VIP Experience, R.I.P. Tour and Guided Theme Park Tour Add-On products are exceptions; Express tickets bought before 31 August 2026 are unaffected.

The park advises checking its ticket store for a Sold Out date before leaving and says tickets may be unavailable at the booths when the park reaches capacity.

Top of the Rock sales are final and non-refundable; tickets may be rescheduled up to 24 hours before the visit, subject to availability, and price differences may apply.
Children aged 5 and under receive free admission; age bands are adult 13-61, child 6-12, senior 62+.

Top of the Rock is open daily 8 AM to 12 AM with last entry at 11:10 PM.
There is a security checkpoint for all visitors; outside food and beverages, weapons and tripods are not permitted.
The observation experience spans the 67th, 69th and 70th floors; the deck is 850 feet above Midtown and SKYLIFT raises visitors 30 feet above the 70th floor.
The Christmas Tree and The Rink are not visible from the observation decks; the VIP pass lists a Christmas Tree Experience 12/3-1/3.

Noi Bai airport bus route 86 to Hanoi Railway Station costs 50,000 VND a trip, departing 7:00 to 22:15.
Noi Bai airport route 17 (to Long Bien, 5:10-22:00) and route 90 (to Kim Ma, 5:00-22:30) each cost 15,000 VND a trip.
The airport says taxis serving passengers must have working, calibrated meters, and publishes a taxi fare table applying from 1 March 2025 (the table itself is an image that was not read).
Noi Bai International Airport has IATA code HAN and is in Noi Bai Commune, Hanoi.
La Siesta's offers pages quote packages 'Net' rates 'including tax and service charge'.
Church Boutique Hotel's page describes Hang Gai as Hanoi's 'Silk Street' and Dong Xuan Market as the largest traditional market in Hanoi, within walking distance of the hotel.
Hanoi Pearl Hotel's site places Ngoc Son Temple, the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre and St Joseph's Cathedral within a few minutes' walk of Hoan Kiem Lake.

Fraser Suites' Hanoi guide lists the Ho Chi Minh complex (mausoleum and presidential palace), Tran Quoc Pagoda (oldest Buddhist pagoda in Hanoi, on a small peninsula in West Lake) and the Xuan Dieu-Quang An dining strip (7-minute walk from the hotel).

La Siesta Classic Ma May (formerly Hanoi La Siesta Hotel & Spa) opened in November 2014 with 65 rooms and suites, Moonlight Sky Bar, La Spa and gym, Red Bean Restaurant; the La Siesta site lists four Hanoi properties.
Church Boutique Hotel 95 Hang Gai is a 35-room boutique hotel on Hang Gai; the Church group lists 58 Hang Gai, Hang Trong and Nha Tho hotels.
Hanoi Backpackers Hostel & Rooftop Bar, 1 Hai Tuong lane / Ta Hien Street, offers 6-, 8- and 12-bed dorms, a 25 m2 Deluxe Double and a 30 m2 Family Room, and sells tours at its front desk.

Apricot Hotel, 136 Hang Trong, has 123 rooms (Sketch 25-30 m2, Canvas 30-32 m2, Gallery 50 m2, Masterpiece 80 m2), rooftop bar One36, and a press release warning of fake websites impersonating the hotel.

Hanoi Pearl Hotel, 6 Bao Khanh Lane, calls itself a 4-star boutique hotel a minute's walk from Hoan Kiem Lake, with Pearl Lounge on the roof, The Candles Restaurant and P-spa; it calls Bao Khanh Lane 'famous animated'.
La Siesta Premium Lakeside is on the banks of Hoan Kiem Lake with an outdoor pool overlooking the lake; its lake-facing rooms are the Suites.
Sofitel Legend Metropole Hanoi, 15 Ngo Quyen Street, steps from the Opera House, open since 1901, has 358 rooms and suites and a historic Heritage Wing, and says it won two MICHELIN Keys in 2026.
Hotel de l'Opera Hanoi - MGallery, 29 Trang Tien Street, is adjacent to the Hanoi Opera House; Junior Suite, L'Opera Suite and Executive Suite are listed as Opera House View.
Pan Pacific Hanoi, 1 Thanh Nien Road, Ba Dinh Ward, has twin views of West Lake and Truc Bach Lake and describes itself as on the fringe of the city centre.
FTE Ba Dinh Hotel, 268 Buoi Street, says rooms include a private bath, wi-fi, cable TV and full breakfast, with a pool and gym on the top floor and the Tequila rooftop bar.
The Hanoi Club Hotel & Residences, 76 Yen Phu Street, on the shore of West Lake, has 88 hotel rooms and says hotel guests have access to club facilities; one lake-view room measures 35-40 m2.

Fraser Suites Hanoi, 51 Xuan Dieu Street in Syrena Tower, has 280 serviced residences, a rooftop pool and Mizumi on level 13; a coffee machine is only in Executive categories; it describes the Old Quarter as a 10-minute drive.

The Caravelle Saigon's offer terms state that rates are subject to a 5% service charge and current government tax, and the hotel quotes a deluxe room at VND 3,800,000++ per night in a Tet 2026 offer (stay 9-23 February 2026); other hotels set their own service charge.

In 2017 Ho Chi Minh City's tourism department proposed a charge of VND 23,000 a night on visitors in city accommodation and the city's vice chairman rejected it; no current city tourist tax was found.

Metro Line 1 single-trip fares are by distance, VND 7,000 to 20,000 in cash and VND 1,000 less cashless (VND 6,000 to 19,000); from Ben Thanh it is VND 7,000 to Thao Dien and VND 20,000 to Suoi Tien Terminal; a one-day pass is VND 40,000 and a three-day pass VND 90,000.

Metro Line 1 opened on 22 December 2024 and has 14 stations from Ben Thanh via Opera House, Ba Son, Van Thanh Park, Tan Cang, Thao Dien and An Phu to Suoi Tien Terminal; it does not serve Tan Son Nhat Airport.

Route 109 runs between the Sai Gon bus station (Pham Ngu Lao) and Terminal 3 of Tan Son Nhat Airport; the city's Public Transport Management Centre announced on 28 April 2025 hours of 5:30-22:40 at T3 and 5:45-22:30 at the bus station, every 15-25 minutes, about 9.3 km and about 45 minutes on average; no current adult fare could be confirmed from the operator.

Hotels publish drive times from Tan Son Nhat Airport: Hotel des Arts Saigon 20 minutes, Novotel Saigon Centre a 20-minute drive, Hotel Nikko Saigon 25 minutes; the Majestic, Nikko and Windsor Plaza offer airport transfers.

Hotel Majestic Saigon is at 1 Dong Khoi Street on the Saigon River; a five-star heritage hotel since 1925 with 175 rooms and suites, a pool and the M Bar rooftop bar; its Century Deluxe page says some rooms have limited views and rooms are assigned on check-in.
Caravelle Saigon is at 19-23 Lam Son Square facing the Opera House; the hotel cites 66 years of legacy; Deluxe rooms are about 34 sqm and Opera rooms have large soundproofed windows.

Rex Hotel Saigon is at 141 Nguyen Hue with 286 rooms and suites; Deluxe rooms in the East Wing are 28 sqm; it began as a French garage in the early 20th century; the hotel says rooms vary in standard, style and size.

Silverland Ben Thanh Hotel is at 14-16 Le Lai; the hotel describes itself as steps from Ben Thanh Market and directly opposite Metro Line 1; rooms listed at 26-38 sqm; rooftop swimming pool; Smith's Kitchen & Bar on the 12th floor; connecting rooms.

Liberty Central Saigon Citypoint is at 59 Pasteur on the corner of Le Loi, with 171 rooms and suites, an infinity rooftop pool, Above Sky Bar and an in-house cinema; its site offers 25% off the best available rate for bookings at least 14 days ahead; no room sizes published.

The Common Room Project is a hostel at 250 Bui Vien with a 14-bed mixed dorm with a full-length balcony onto the walking street, an 8-bed female-only dorm, a private ensuite room and a nightly family-style dinner.

Hotel des Arts Saigon (MGallery) is at 76-78 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, officially opened October 2015; Deluxe rooms are 30 sqm; The Albion by Kirk Westaway on the 23rd floor and Social Club Rooftop Bar on the 24th; the owner's art collection is displayed in the corridors; Booking.com lists it in District 3.

Novotel Saigon Centre is a four-star at 167 Hai Ba Trung with 247 rooms, a pool, Food Exchange restaurant and the 20th-floor OnTop bar; Superior rooms are 27 sqm; Accor lists Notre-Dame Basilica 700 m and Ben Thanh Market 1.8 km (22 minutes' walk).

Villa Song Saigon is at 197/2 Nguyen Van Huong in Thao Dien, a French colonial boutique hotel on the Saigon River; Villa Rooms are 26-41 sqm with a la carte breakfast 6:30-10:30am, pool and gym access.

Vinpearl Landmark 81, Autograph Collection is at 720A Dien Bien Phu in Landmark 81, Vietnam's tallest building, with 223 rooms with floor-to-ceiling windows, an infinity pool on the 47th floor, Oriental Pearl on the 66th; the hotel says Tan Cang Metro Station is under 10 minutes away by electric bus.

Windsor Plaza Hotel is in District 5 (hotel entrance 1 Su Van Hanh; Booking.com lists 18 An Duong Vuong), with a pool and fitness centre on the 24th floor, an executive lounge on the 25th and a complimentary city shuttle; Deluxe Twin and King rooms are 32 sqm.

Hotel Nikko Saigon is at 235 Nguyen Van Cu, a 23-storey hotel with 334 rooms and 53 service apartments, 40 sqm Deluxe rooms, a garden pool on the fourth floor, Ming Court; the hotel lists driving times of 10 minutes to Ben Thanh Market, 12 to the Notre-Dame Basilica and Saigon Opera House and 25 to the airport.

Da Nang International Airport has IATA code DAD.
Danabus route 12 (city route) serves Da Nang International Airport, costs 8,000 VND a trip, and runs daily 5:30-19:00.

Danabus route 06 runs between the airport and the Vietnam-Korea University of Information and Communication Technology via the Dragon Bridge; 15,000 VND up to half the route, 22,000 VND full route, daily 5:30-19:00.
Hai Van Bus (suburban route) runs from Da Nang airport to Hoi An (Cua Dai parking lot) for 120,000 VND a trip, daily 7:30-16:00.

Hoi An Ancient Town ticket: 80,000 VND (general landscape, one monument of Japanese Covered Bridge or Quan Cong Temple, two self-selected monuments) or 120,000 VND (same one monument, one museum-system site and three self-selected monuments); valid up to 3 days; children under 16 exempt; the notice, dated 29 January 2026, lists a 50% discount for certain Vietnamese groups only and no nationality-based rate.
The heritage centre notice sets 'Walking and Cycling town' hours in the Ancient Town of 9:00-21:30 in summer and 9:00-21:00 in winter.

Hoi An hotel sites print 'Danang' in their addresses (Little Oasis: 215 Le Thanh Tong Street, Hoi An, Danang; Allegro: 86/2 Tran Hung Dao Street, Hoi An, Danang), and Hoi An Historic Hotel describes the Ancient Town's streets as lantern-lit.
Little Hoi An Group hotel sites (Little Riverside, Allegro) list room rates in USD with '++' after the price.
The National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting's English-language Da Nang page carries a 10-day weather forecast, and its site has a Tropical cyclone section.

Hotels' own distance claims: Haian Beach puts the airport 4 km away; Pullman 15 minutes from the airport and city centre; InterContinental 30 minutes (20 km) by car from the airport and 13 km from Da Nang city; Novotel's page gives Hoi An Ancient Town at 29.6 km, 46 minutes' drive.

Novotel Danang Premier Han River's ALL.com page gives Han Market 1 km, Cham Museum 2 km, the Han River 20 m (3-minute walk), and Da Nang beach 4.4 km (11-minute drive); it describes itself as on the west bank of the Han River.
Diamond Sea Hotel's site calls it 'the iconic My Khe Beach' in its Ocean Premier room description.
InterContinental says its resort lies in the Son Tra Peninsula Nature Reserve on 39 hectares, overlooking Bai Bac Bay with a 700-metre secluded beach.

claim: TSA: liquids, gels, creams and pastes in carry-on must be in containers of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less, carried in a quart-sized bag; medications are exempt.
TSA allows larger amounts of medically necessary liquids, gels and aerosols in reasonable quantities for the trip, to be declared to officers at the checkpoint; carry-on and checked both allowed.

TSA: scissors are allowed in carry-on if the blade is less than 4 inches from the pivot point; in checked bags, sharp objects should be sheathed or securely wrapped.

TSA/FAA: checked bags may hold no more than 70 oz (2 kg) or 68 fl oz (2 L) of medicinal and toiletry articles including aerosols per person, no single container above 18 oz (0.5 kg) or 17 fl oz (500 ml); aerosol nozzles must be protected.

UK government: at most airports liquids in hand luggage are limited to containers of 100ml or less; some airports may allow up to 2 litres; where a bag is required it holds no more than a litre and measures about 20cm x 20cm; rules depend on the airport, including connections and the return journey; containers up to 2 litres are allowed at all UK airports for essential medical purposes.

UK government: tablets, capsules, syringes and inhalers are allowed in hand and hold luggage; proof (doctor's letter or prescription copy) is needed only for liquid medicine in containers over 100ml; ice packs in hand luggage: contact the airport first, allowed in hold luggage; staff may open containers.

UK government: keep medicine containing a controlled drug in hand luggage; carry a prescription or doctor's letter and check destination rules with its embassy; bringing medicine into the UK is limited to up to 3 months' supply, with a letter showing name, travel dates, medicine, quantity, dose, strength and prescriber's signature for non-residents; Schedule 1 drugs need a licence.

CDC: kit should cover documents, medicines and supplies; prescriptions preferably in the original bottle; bring copies of prescriptions; some countries restrict medications, so check with the destination's embassy; antibiotics, antimalarials and antivirals only if prescribed.

NaTHNaC (TravelHealthPro): all travellers should carry a first aid kit tailored to the individual and destination; recommended contents (wound care, painkillers, antihistamines, rehydration salts, loperamide, thermometer, tweezers, prescription copy and prescriber letter with drug names); regular medicines in hand luggage with an extra supply in the hold; sterile medical kit in the hold; keep medicines in original labelled packaging; pseudoephedrine decongestants illegal in some countries; common medicines may be hard to find abroad and counterfeits exist; buying overseas discouraged as quality cannot be assured.

Embassy of Japan in the UK: narcotics such as codeine and morphine need permission irrespective of amount; non-narcotic medicines need a Yunyu Kakunin-sho if more than 1 month's supply; examples allowed up to a month's supply without permission include paracetamol, ibuprofen, aspirin, salbutamol inhalers, statins, blood pressure tablets, antibiotics, vitamins and eye drops.

Japan MHLW Narcotics Control Department: medicine containing narcotics (codeine, morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl) or stimulants' raw materials (pseudoephedrine) needs permission before entry; some medicines cannot be imported even if prescription at home; medical certificate with name, address, specific reason, drug list with doses and strengths, signature, issued within 3 months; apply at least 14 days before travel.
Embassy of Japan in the US: Yunyu Kakunin-sho must be applied for and received before leaving for Japan and declared to customs on arrival; apply at least two weeks in advance.

FAA PackSafe: alcohol more than 24% and up to 70% ABV in unopened retail packaging: 5 L per packaging and 5 L total per passenger; alcohol over 70% ABV is listed as a separate category.

49 CFR 175.10(a)(4): passengers may carry alcohol of not more than 24% ABV, or more than 24% and not more than 70% in unopened retail packagings not exceeding 5 litres, in carry-on or checked baggage, with a total net quantity of 5 litres per person.

UK CAA: alcoholic beverages above 24% and up to 70% ABV must be in retail packaging with no more than 5 L total net quantity per person; beverages up to 24% are not restricted; passengers must contact their airline in advance for clarification.

UK government: liquid foods such as soup, jam, honey and syrups count as liquids and should be packed in the hold if possible; duty-free liquids may go through security if sealed in a security bag at purchase with the receipt sealed in the bag and visible; the bag must not be opened until the final destination.

TSA: for inbound international flights with a connection to the US, duty-free liquids over 3.4 oz (100 ml) may be in carry-on if purchased internationally, packed by the retailer in a transparent tamper-evident bag with no signs of tampering, with the original receipt and a purchase within 48 hours; TSA recommends packing them in checked baggage.

FCDO's solo and independent travel guidance says to leave an itinerary with someone at home and agree how regularly you will be in contact, and to consider leaving photocopies of documents such as passport and insurance policy.

FCDO says to book accommodation before you travel, in particular the first night, because you are most vulnerable when you first arrive in a foreign country, tired and unsure of your surroundings; know the address and have alternative accommodation.
FCDO suggests arranging airport transfers before you arrive, using only official, licensed and reputable taxis, travelling in busy train carriages and avoiding hitchhiking.

FCDO lists accommodation habits: never leave the key where someone can note the room number, close windows, lock the door when inside, use the spy hole or chain, consider a door wedge, check smoke alarms and fire exits, and be aware of carbon monoxide risks.
FCDO says that if you feel uncomfortable or in danger, being safe is more important than being polite, and to contact the local police if fearful for your safety or in danger.

STEP is a free US State Department service that lets US citizens travelling or living abroad receive security updates from the nearest US embassy or consulate; the information lets the embassy contact the traveller in an emergency and try to reach them for family.
FCDO tells travellers to check country travel advice and sign up to receive email alerts when it is updated.

FCDO says to make sure you can access money abroad including quickly in an emergency, ensure you can reach enough money if your main payment method fails (for example if you lose your phone and cannot complete two-factor authentication), and keep a backup of key information such as accommodation, flight and passport details.

FCDO's France advice: pickpockets can work in gangs, one distracting while another goes into the bag; keep passport, cards and valuables in separate bags or pockets, use inside compartments, carry the bag across the body, and do not get distracted around tourist attractions and ATMs.

FCDO's Thailand advice: do not lose sight of your card during transactions, there have been incidents of ATM skimming, use an ATM in a bank and protect your PIN; beware job scams that appear too good to be true.

FCDO's Chile advice: unlicensed taxi drivers at Santiago airport add digits to the fare (5,000,000 CLP instead of 50,000) and some passengers are persuaded to enter a PIN into a card reader whose display cannot be read.
FCDO's South Africa advice: be wary of unregulated drivers posing as Uber or other taxi app drivers, especially at airports.

FCDO's Spain advice: thieves posing as police officers may ask to see your wallet; genuine officers will ask to see ID but will not ask for wallets or purses; buy your own drinks and keep them in sight.

UK government Travel Aware guidance on spiking: keep an eye on your drink, do not drink it if it smells or tastes odd, do not accept drinks from strangers, plan your trip home, report suspected spiking to local police; methanol is sometimes illegally mixed with spirits in some parts of the world.

TravelHealthPro (NaTHNaC) says informal and illegal production of fake alcohol is common in many parts of the world, and that excessive alcohol use and illegal drugs may invalidate insurance claims; travel insurance should cover planned activities, pre-existing conditions, belongings and medical repatriation.

FCDO says to have appropriate travel insurance even if visiting friends and family or knowing the country well, and to check that a policy covers the places visited, the duration and planned activities.
